## T-120 batch 16 gap: `base: working` overlay runs use a full checkout of the snapshot (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **Open.** Accepted departure (F5): the design's delta layer (§5.2) is not built; a run of `base: working` mounts `.base/<W>/tree`, a full checkout of the snapshot commit, shared only by runs of the same `W`.
- **Why.** The delta layer needs a one-shot overlay mount to write whiteouts and its own cache keyed by `W`; the cost difference only matters for big repositories with a dirty session.
- **Closes when.** `addOverlay` builds `.base/<HEAD>` plus a `.delta/<W>` lower (one-shot bwrap applying `git diff --binary HEAD W`), refcounted like the base, with a test that the delta's deletes are whiteouts.

## T-120 batch 16 gap: overlay runs differ from checkout runs in namespaces and host view (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **Open.** Accepted departures (F6 rows 3, 4, 6): every process of an overlay run lives in the holder's user and pid namespaces (setuid programs do not elevate, `/proc` lists only the run's processes, a process the run leaves is killed when the run ends; a checkout run's could outlive it); a `./program` path resolved by exec before the call starts (`resolveBashExecutable`) is looked up on the host, where an overlay run's files are absent; a transcript read by path inside an overlay run is named through `/proc/<holder>/root` and is valid only while the holder lives; an unsandboxed call of either run is unconfined, so for an overlay run the layers and the base checkout are reachable by path.
- **Why.** They follow from the mount existing only inside the holder (C3) and from "no sandbox, no confinement"; none lets a sandboxed call do what a checkout run's cannot (`TestOverlayAndCheckoutRunsAreConfinedAlike`).
- **Closes when.** Each is either accepted in the schema text or handled (resolving relative programs inside the view; making the base read-only to an unsandboxed run needs a sandbox, not jad).

## T-120 batch 16 gap: base cache entries are collected only by overlay runs (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **Open.** Garbage collection of the base cache runs when an overlay run of that repository starts or ends; unheld non-HEAD entries (and the holders of runs lost without a record) stay until then. A server killed inside `Create` after it made `.overlay/<run>` but before the run's folders were registered leaves that folder without a state file and no record, so the entry it counted for is kept (nothing is deleted) until someone removes the folder.
- **Why.** No startup sweep was added so that recovery stays as P3 left it; the window is a few milliseconds.
- **Closes when.** `SubagentManager.recover` and `RecoverDelegatedWorktrees` sweep the cache once at startup, and a sweep treats an `.overlay/<run>` without `jad-run.json`, with a free lock and older than the git timeout as dead.

## T-120 batch 16 gap: holder identity without pidfd, and concurrent recovery of sub-agent manifests (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **Open.** (1) On a kernel without `pidfd_open` (before Linux 5.3) a holder is checked by pid and start time only, and `nsenter -t <pid>` takes a pid whichever kernel, so a check and the use of the pid are not atomic (microseconds; the holder is jad's own child until it is waited for, so its pid cannot be reused meanwhile, but a holder recorded in a state file and found by a later server is not). (2) Two servers that start at the same moment can both adopt the manifest of a dead third server and retry its kept worktree; an overlay run is protected by the overlay flock (the second one gets `worktree.ErrHeld` and skips), a delegated record by its `.lock` file, a kept checkout run of a sub-agent manifest by nothing.
- **Why.** nsenter has no pidfd option; manifest adoption has always been unlocked (P3).

## Async final results: ref file, ref_transcript and remote limits (Go, 2026-11-12)

- **Done.** A finished profile_message, sub-agent or remote handle saves its whole answer in `<async dir>/<kind>/<id>.txt` (the exec pattern, same age sweep); `ref` is that file, `ref_transcript` the transcript, `bytes` the answer's size, `cut` whether the delivered text is shorter. Sub-agent answers are captured in `SubagentManager.finish` before the `result_max_bytes` cut. The cut of the short summary kept beside a stored result no longer sets `cut`.
- **Done, remote.** The remote API has a new route `GET /runs/{id}/result?offset=&limit=` that serves a run's whole final text as plain bytes in parts (header `X-Result-Bytes` = whole size), and a view query `text_max_bytes` that lowers the view's text. The hub asks every view for the text that fits its `max_response_bytes` after JSON escaping (so a poll can no longer fail as too large because of a long answer), and when the view is `cut` it reads the whole answer from the route in parts of `max_response_bytes` into the result file (temporary file, renamed when complete; sizes checked against `X-Result-Bytes`). A sub-agent run served by the remote API keeps its whole answer in memory (`subagentRun.full`, external runs only) instead of its `result_max_bytes` cut; the remote's `result_max_bytes` now bounds the view only. Covered end to end by `async_final_ref_test.go` (hub + real remote API), `result_route_test.go`, `remote/run_test.go` and the app test `TestRemoteAPISubagentAnswerBeyondTheLimitsIsServedWholeByTheResultRoute`.
- **Open.** (1) A remote run has no `ref_transcript`: the remote's transcript is not reachable from this host as a file (the `transcript` tools can read it by name). (2) If the result file cannot be written, or the remote lacks the result route (an older server) or fails it, the entry has `ref` empty and `cut` true (a warning is logged); the entry carries no separate error field, and an older remote that ignores `text_max_bytes` can still send a view over the hub's `max_response_bytes`, which fails the poll as before. (3) The hub puts no total size limit on the answer it saves (each part is bounded by `max_response_bytes`); a remote's answer is bounded by what the remote's model produced. A new hub-side cap would be a configuration key and was not added. (4) The result files are removed by the age sweep, not when their record is pruned, as for exec; a read of `ref` after the sweep fails. (5) The remote keeps the whole text only for its run retention (`run_retention_ms`); the hub reads it right after the run ends, and a failure then is case (2). (6) Runs started without an async handle (no async tool) are returned inline and cut, with `truncated`, and save no file. (7) An external sub-agent run holds its whole answer in memory as long as the manager keeps the finished run (`keep_finished`), so a very long answer costs that memory on the serving host. (8) The remote profile_message server returns its answer whole in memory as before; only the sub-agent path changed there.
- **Why.** The inline limits (`result_max_bytes`, the poll cap) stay what bounds the model's context; the file is what carries the answer.
- **Closes when.** (1) the remote API names a transcript the hub can read; (3) a hub-side `max_result_bytes` setting is wanted.

## Isolation P6 per-run stdio MCP servers: open gaps (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **Open.** (1) Per-run servers are not optional: every isolated run (a sub-agent, fresh or resumed, or a delegated profile run) with stdio MCP tools starts its own set of server processes, so a server that keeps state (an index, a browser profile) starts empty for each run, and a run pays the start time. (2) The run's servers are not tracked after a hard stop of the server: no pid is recorded. Normal end, a cancelled start and a timed-out start are tested to end the server and its grandchild, in a checkout and an overlay, with and without a bwrap sandbox (`TestRunMCPLoaderStopsTheServersProcessGroup`; a cancelled or timed-out start kills the group at once, `stdio_kill.go`). A server that ignores stdin closing and SIGTERM holds the run's end for the SDK's three terminate delays (about 15s, not configurable here) before its group is killed. A hard-killed jad (SIGKILL) is not tested: a bwrap or overlay-holder server ends with its namespace by the way those are started (`--die-with-parent`), an unsandboxed checkout-run server ends only if it exits when its stdin closes. (3) Streamable HTTP servers are not per-run, and a stdio server of a session whose sandbox does not list `mcp` is started in the worktree but not confined (an absolute path still reaches the session's folder; shown for checkout and overlay by `TestRunMCPLoaderServersAreConfinedByTheSessionsSandbox`), so an isolated agent with MCP tools stays a writer for scheduling (D10) and takes its checkpoint. (4) Fixed 2026-11-10 (follow-up): a set is for one server set key, workspace and effective sandbox, so a narrower nested child gets servers of its own and no agent calls another's. What remains: agents share a set only when their sandbox is identical by content, so each distinct narrowing costs one more set of processes for the run; a toolset's servers are not started for an agent whose sandbox reaches more than the toolset's own (the run fails); a run's servers are never started in a plan-mode form of their own (see "Plan mode and run servers" below: no plan-mode run has run servers, and a plan-mode caller's delegated target gets its servers in the caller's plan-mode form); and a set stays up until the run ends, not until the agent that needed it does. (5) A tool the run's server stops listing makes the call fail with an error naming it (the run goes on); it does not end the run. (6) The delegated run's catalog is still built before its worktree exists, so the target session's own stdio servers are started in the session's folder by that build and are not called by the run. (7) LSP servers and hooks of an isolated run still see the session's folder, resource subscriptions of a run's servers are not read by the session's change notes, and the clone materialiser half of P6 is not built (no Linux use: reflink needs btrfs or XFS). (8) macOS (seatbelt) was not run.
- **Why.** (1) A setting would add a key to the loader, schema and tests for a choice nobody asked for; D10's fix was per-run servers. (2) A pid list would be one more state file per run, and the recovery paths (`SubagentManager.recover`, `RecoverDelegatedWorktrees`) have no run-scoped MCP state to read. (3) HTTP endpoints have no folder; confinement is the sandbox's job, not jad's (cwd alone is not a boundary). (4) A server is a long-lived process, so its sandbox cannot follow a call's plan mode; the set is for the sandbox it was started in, and a call from another sandbox is refused instead of served by it. (5) The tool list the model saw was fixed at load. (6) Building the catalog after the worktree needs the worktree to be opened before the model is prepared. (7) Out of the P6 row's scope. (8) No Mac runner.
- **Plan mode and run servers (traced 2026-11-10 follow-up; no bypass found in P6).** Run servers exist only for an isolated sub-agent run and for a delegated `profile_message` run (`bound_runner.go` starts them after `PlanMode` has narrowed the catalog, but a delegated run is never a plan-mode run: `profile_delegation.go` does not set `Plan`, and a user's plan-mode run uses the session's servers). So the cases are: (a) *Plan-mode main run:* `Catalog.PlanMode` keeps an MCP tool only if it is `ReadOnly` (the resource and prompt list/read tools, read-only by the protocol) or a `plan_mode.allow_tools` entry names it, whole; this is unchanged by P6 and the session's servers are as they were. (b) *Sub-agent called from a plan-mode run:* the call is refused when `changesWorkspace()` is true. P6 kept an isolated agent with MCP tools and a tool that changes files a writer (`TestIsolatedAgentWithMCPToolsStaysAWriterForPlanMode`), so plan mode still refuses it; an isolated agent that is allowed in plan mode (a reader by its tools list, or without MCP tools) runs like its `exec` does, in its own worktree and its sandbox, which plan mode never narrows for a child. Its servers start in that same sandbox, so P6 gives them no more reach than its `exec` has. (c) *`profile_message` from a plan-mode run* (kept only by `allow_tools`, then `callerEnvironment` gives the target the caller's plan-mode sandbox): the target's sandbox, and so its servers (`runServerSandbox`), are in that plan-mode form; `TestRunMCPLoaderServersOfAPlanModeCallersTargetKeepThePlanForm` runs the real bwrap chain (confine, run environment, loader) and checks a server writes the plan paths and not the workspace its normal form writes. What stays: a sandbox that does not list `mcp` leaves the server unconfined whatever the mode (as for the session's servers, and as `exec` outside a sandbox that lists it); a server belongs to no call, so `{tmp}` in its sandbox is the system temp folder (`sandboxExpander`), which a plan-mode form should not list for a server.
- **Open (unrelated to P6, found while tracing).** A sub-agent whose `tools` list names only `mcp:` tools (no `exec`, `tool_smith`, `subagent` or `profile_message`) is a reader by `ChangesFiles` (MCP tools are not counted), so a plan-mode run may call it and it may call an MCP tool that writes, in the session's folder when it is not isolated. This was so before P6 (the session's servers) and P6 changes it only for isolated agents (checked 2026-11-10: `changesWorkspace`, `ChangesFiles`, `IsChangeTool` and every `ReadOnly`/`MayChangeFiles`/plan-mode line are identical to HEAD apart from a comment; a run in the session's folder gets no `MCPRoute` and starts no servers, `TestRunsThatNeedNoServersOfTheirOwnStartNone`; `startRunMCP` does nothing unless the workspace is an isolated run's worktree). Not fixed: it decides what counts as a change tool, a user-visible rule. Not recorded with `bug-report-memory`: no such helper exists in this workspace. **Closes when** a decision says whether an agent with MCP tools is a writer for plan mode (`ChangesFiles` counting `mcp:` entries, or a tool-level read-only hint).
- **Closes when.** (1) an `isolation.mcp` setting (per run or the session's) is wanted; (2) the run's state file (`jad-run.json`, delegated record) records the pids or a process-group id, and recovery kills them, or a crash test shows the namespaces and stdin close are enough; the SDK's terminate delays become a setting; (3) HTTP servers get a per-run proxy, or the writer rule is relaxed for runs whose stdio servers are all sandboxed and that have no HTTP tools (a new decision); (4) a set is stopped when its last agent ends (a reference count), or a run's servers take a plan-mode sandbox form; (5) a changed tool list ends the run, if that is preferred; (6) the delegated worktree opens before `prepareRun`; (7) per-run LSP and hooks are scheduled; (8) a macOS run.
- **Verified (2026-11-10, second follow-up).** The previous gate's one failure was `TestToolSmithStandbyBridgeUsesTheStandbysToken` comparing a fresh and a standby run of a bridged script: the rendering carries `nested_duration_ms: N` (the time the bridge took; `tool_smith_bridge.go`), which the test's `toolSmithVariable` did not mask (it masked `N ms` only), so the two differed whenever a run was slow. The assertion now masks `nested_duration_ms`, and `TestToolSmithComparableIgnoresTheBridgeDuration` pins that durations are ignored and a call count is not (a mutation without the mask is caught). The behaviour the test checks (the bridged run takes the standby, the nested call works, the two runs render alike) is unchanged. `GOFLAGS=-timeout=40m verify-go.sh --race "./internal/tools/mcp/ ./internal/tools/native/ ./internal/app/"` then exited 0: gofmt, vet, test, race (mcp 130s, native 677s, app 470s) and diffcheck all exit 0. The earlier note that the gate did not exit 0 is closed. Not run: macOS (seatbelt) tests, no runner.

## Plan mode, scheduling and checkpoint for sub-agents with MCP tools, nested children and remote agents (Go, 2026-11-12)

Closes the open point of "Isolation P6 per-run stdio MCP servers" (an agent whose `tools` list names only `mcp:` tools was a reader) and the plan-mode part of D10.

- **Rule.** A sub-agent that shows an MCP tool not marked `ReadOnly` is a writer (`subagentAgent.mcpWrites`, read by `changesWorkspace` and `changesFiles`): it takes the parent's checkpoint, runs alone under ordered scheduling, is handed off as a writer, and a plan-mode run refuses a call to it with `plan_mode`. It does not depend on `tools` having a native change tool, on the list being explicit or absent (an unrestricted agent in a session with no `exec` is judged by its MCP tools), on isolation, or on a sandbox. A server's `readOnlyHint` is still not read; an unknown tool is a writer, so only the resources and prompts tools (`ReadOnly` by the protocol) leave an agent a reader. The earlier rule (isolated or sandbox-reader agent with a change tool and any MCP tool) is kept. `NativeSubagentAgent.ChangesFiles` (config time) is unchanged: it does not know the loaded tools, so `isolation: worktree` is still refused for an agent whose list names only MCP tools.
- **Resume.** A `resume` that names no agent is judged by the agent of the run it continues (`withResumeAgent`); before, with two or more agents the call picked none and was a reader call, so a writer run could be resumed in plan mode, unserialised and without a checkpoint.
- **Nested children.** A child's catalog is not narrowed by plan mode, so the guard is carried: `planModeGuard` sets `ExecutionContext.PlanGuarded` on the calls it lets through, `ForNested` copies it into the child's run (`ToolExecution`), and `subagentTool.execute` applies the same refusal (`planModeRefusal`) to a call made with it, at every depth. A tool that `plan_mode.allow_tools` keeps whole is not guarded, so its children are not either: the allow entry means the same at every depth. No setting was added.
- **Remote agents.** The subagents request has no plan-mode field and the remote starts its child without a plan guard, so a remote start is refused in plan mode (`Tool.PlanModeRefusal` of the subagent tool), top level and nested, unless an allow entry keeps the tool whole. This stops the start on this host; it does not confine the remote host (a remote can run any profile of its own, and an allowed call is not told about plan mode). Outside plan mode a remote call on another machine keeps its classification (no local checkpoint, no local writer slot, may run beside reads); one on this host is a writer (follow-up below).
- **Tests.** `subagent_plan_mcp_test.go` (explicit list, no list, ReadOnly-only list; scheduling and checkpoint inputs; plan refuse/allow; resume; nested and grandchild; remote), `TestPlanModeMarksGuardedCallsForNestedRuns`, `TestMCPOnlySubagentTakesTheParentsCheckpoint` (app, real checkpoint and stdio server); `TestIsolatedAgentWithMCPToolsStaysAWriterForPlanMode` now expects the MCP-only agent to be a writer.
- **Nested writers (follow-up, 2026-11-12).** No run of a child has a checkpoint or an ordered slot of its own; the call at the top is the only one the parent's checkpoint and `ChangesState` belong to. So `subagentTool.callWrites(arguments, below=true)`, behind `MayChangeFiles` (checkpoint, ordered scheduling, `roundChangesWorkspace`), also counts what an agent may start: `subagentAgent.nests` (max_depth 2 or more and the agent's tools show `subagent`) plus `nestsWriter`: some agent of the tool is a writer by its own tools (`changesWorkspace`) or an allowed remote shares this host. It looks at every agent, not at the one the child will pick (the child's model decides), so it holds at every depth and is a plain read of the agents under `RWMutex.RLock` with no lock held by the caller: nothing nests a lock, and no checkpoint or slot is taken below the top. Over-approximation, on purpose: an isolated or sandbox-reader nesting agent counts too, and a sandbox choice is ignored. `startRunFrom` uses it for `changes` and `touches`, so such a call runs to its end inside the call (`background` stays false: the checkpoint is the call's) and its result carries the change note. A nesting reader with no writer to reach (only readers, only `ReadOnly` MCP tools, or `max_depth` 1) stays a reader, so legitimate read-only nesting is neither serialized nor checkpointed. Plan mode asks without it (`callWrites(arguments, false)` in `planModeRefusal`): it refuses each call at its own depth through `PlanGuarded`, so a nesting reader still runs in plan mode and only its writer grandchildren are refused. Tests: `subagent_nested_writer_test.go` (reachability, no-writer, max_depth 1, plan, classification at child and grandchild level) and, through the real launcher, stdio MCP server and a real checkpoint, `TestReaderChildThatStartsAnMCPWriterTakesTheParentsCheckpoint`, `TestPlanModeRunRefusesAnMCPOnlyChild`, `TestPlanModeRunRefusesAnMCPWriterGrandchildOfAReaderChild`, `TestPlanModeRunStillRunsAReaderChild`.
- **Remote agents on this host (follow-up).** Evidence: `remoteBackend.StartSubagent` runs the child in `config.WorkingDir` of the remote profile it resolves, a path on the remote's machine, and the request carries no workspace, so this host cannot know whether it is its own folder; a unix socket or a loopback entry (`remote.Entry.SameHost`: `unix://`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, an unspecified address) is a server on this machine that can be given the session's folder. So a call to such a remote, or to one whose entry cannot be read, is now a writer for the checkpoint and ordered scheduling (`remoteSharesHost`), and a nesting agent that can reach one is too; a remote at another address stays a reader. Plan mode refuses every remote start as before. **Limits, open:** (1) a network file system that shares the folder with a remote at a non-loopback address, or a loopback port forward to another machine, cannot be told from here; (2) an allowed (allow entry) remote call is not told about plan mode. The third limit of this follow-up, a same-host remote run that outlives its call as an async handle, is closed (next but one entry). Closes when `remoteapi.SubagentRequest` carries the plan state and the workspace identity, or a decision makes every remote call a writer. Tests: `TestRemoteAgentOnThisHostIsAWriterForSchedulingAndCheckpoint`, `TestNestingReaderIsAWriterWhenItCanReachARemoteOnThisHost`, `TestRemoteSubagentNeverChangesLocalCheckpointOrLimits` (another machine's address).
- **MCP-only worktree (follow-up).** Config: `isolation: worktree` and `sandbox.isolation.mode: worktree` on an agent whose list names only `mcp:` tools were already refused at load (`subagentIsolation`, `layout_load.go`); the message now says an `mcp:` tool does not count, and `TestNativeSubagentWorktreeRefusals` has the case. Call time: a sandbox choice with `isolation.mode: worktree` silently left an agent with no native change tool in the session's folder (`withCallSandbox`: nothing to isolate), which is right for a reader but not for an agent that changes files through MCP tools (an MCP-only list, or an unrestricted agent in a session with no `exec`): `chooseSandbox` now refuses it with `sandbox_unavailable` and a message naming the cause (`TestWorktreeChoiceIsRefusedForAnMCPOnlyAgent`). An unrestricted agent whose config says `isolation: worktree` in a session with no `exec` is isolated, as before (the MCP servers of an isolated run start in its worktree, P6).
- **Same-host remote is never a handle (follow-up 2, 2026-11-12).** Trace: `startRemote` registered an `rs_` handle of the async manager for any call whose caller can collect one and returned it when `block_ms` ran out, with no `background_writers` gate (that gate is local, `backgroundSafe`). So a remote classified a writer by `remoteSharesHost` could keep changing this host's files after the call returned, outside the call's checkpoint and ordered slot. Fix: `handled` is false when `remoteOnThisHost(entry)` (`remote.Entry.SameHost`): the call waits for the remote run to end as a local writer does, whatever `block_ms` says, registers no handle, and a cancel of the call stops the remote run; the remote timeout (`RemoteTimeoutMs`) still bounds the wait. A remote of another machine is handed off as before. A nested start (inside a child) is the same code, so it also waits. (The window between scheduling and start in which an edited entry could give one call two answers is closed by follow-up 3.) `remoteOnThisHost` is a package variable only so a test can place its loopback test server on another machine (`newRemoteSubagentFixtureOn` does, for the name `peer`); nothing sets it in production. Tests: `TestRemoteOnThisHostIsNeverHandedOff` (block_ms 0 waits, no handle in the async list, answer returned, the other machine's remote is still a handle), `TestRemoteOnThisHostIsStoppedWithItsCall`; the handle-returning check is caught by a mutation that removes the same-host term. Limit: the wait holds the call's slot for as long as the remote runs, up to the remote timeout; and a remote session on the other side is still its own (the remote's transcript and its own checkpoint are not this host's).
- **Model-facing marker (follow-up 2).** The agent list the model reads (the subagent description and the result of a call with no task) is marked from the same classification as scheduling (`subagentTool.agentMarker`): an agent with a native change tool, an MCP tool not marked `ReadOnly`, or a path to a writer by nesting (`nestsWriterLocked`) is `[can change files; runs to its end]`, or `[can change files; may run in the background]` when it may be handed off (`background`); an isolated agent with a change tool and nothing that reaches the session's folder keeps the worktree marker; a reader, and a nesting reader with no writer to reach, is unmarked. The MCP tools exist only after the native catalog is built, so the tool builds its description at construction (`nests` is set first) and again in `bindMCP` (before the catalogs, so the copy a nesting child holds carries it), and the owner passes its native catalog through `SubagentMCP.Redescribe` (`Catalog.WithDescription`, a new catalog; the resolver does it after `BindToolsets`). The remotes line names the remotes whose server runs on this machine (`remoteListText`) as `[can change files; runs to its end]`. This changes the golden description of the tool for agents with MCP write tools, nesting readers and same-host remotes; the description for a config with none of them is unchanged. Tests: `subagent_marker_test.go` (markers against `ChangesState`, the call-with-no-task list, a child's copy, readers, `max_depth` 1, isolation, remotes), `TestAgentListTheModelReadsMarksMCPAndNestingWriters` (app, the description the provider receives; caught by removing the resolver's `Redescribe`), `TestCatalogWithDescriptionReplacesOnlyThatToolsDescription`. Limit: a sandbox choice that makes a call a reader (or a writer) is not in the list; the marker is the agent's own, over-approximated as the classification is. The description is built from the remote entries as they are when a session is prepared.
- **Entry snapshot (follow-up 3, 2026-11-12).** `startRemote` and `remoteSharesHost` read the entry file separately, so an edit between scheduling (`MayChangeFiles`: a reader slot, no checkpoint) and start could run a call to a now-same-host server as a reader. Fix: the tool reads each allowed remote's entry once when it is built (`takeRemoteSnapshot`; one run, as a catalog is built per prepare) and keeps `remoteSnapshot{sameHost, address}` for good. Scheduling, the checkpoint, the nesting classification, the description and the handle decision (`handled`) all use the snapshot (`remoteSharesHost`, `sameHostRemotes`), never the file. At start the entry is read once more; a remote the snapshot put on another machine is started only if `Entry.Address()` (socket path or host:port) equals the snapshot's, otherwise the call is refused with `remote_changed` and nothing reaches the server; the client is then made for the entry just checked (`Directory.ClientFor`, `startRemoteRunOn`), not for a third read of the file, so what is checked is what is connected. A remote the snapshot put on this machine (or whose entry could not be read when the tool was built) stays a writer that waits for its end whatever the file says later, which is the safe direction. Other edits (token, timeouts, description) apply as before. A run that lasts longer than an entry edit must be restarted to use a moved remote: fail-safe, as the refusal says. Tests: `TestRemoteEntryEditedBetweenSchedulingAndStartIsRefused` (scheduled as a reader, file edited to the loopback server, `MayChangeFiles` unchanged, start refused, no request reached the peer), `TestRemoteEntryEditsThatAreSafeDoNotChangeTheCall`, `TestDirectoryClientForUsesTheGivenEntry`; mutations that drop the address check, read the file in `remoteSharesHost` or drop the same-host handle term are caught. Not covered by a test: the window between the start's read and `ClientFor` is closed by construction (the client takes the entry as an argument); a mutation back to `Client(name)` is caught only in the `remote` package test. `newRemoteSubagentFixtureWith` writes extra entries before the tool is built because the tool now reads them then.
- **Same-host is a heuristic, not confinement (follow-up 3).** `remote.Entry.SameHost` reads the address only: a unix socket, `localhost`, `*.localhost`, a loopback or unspecified IP. It does not resolve DNS and does not look at file systems, so these read as another machine and their calls are neither checkpointed nor serialized here: a name that resolves to this machine, this machine's own LAN or public address, a tunnel or loopback port forward to another machine (the reverse: a forward from another machine's address to ours), and a network file system shared with a server at another address. A remote's own run, transcript and checkpoint are on its side, and plan mode cannot be passed to it. Conservative choices made instead of guessing: an entry that cannot be read is a writer; a remote the tool does not know is a writer. Not chosen: classifying every remote as a writer, which would serialize and checkpoint all remote calls to protect against shares nobody can detect from here. The caveat is also in `remote.Entry.SameHost`, `remoteSharesHost`, `design_remote.md` section 13 and the `url` description of `sample/schemes/remote.schema.json`. **Closes when** the remote API carries the workspace identity (or a decision makes every remote call a writer, or the entry file gets an explicit `shares_files` flag).
- **Sibling serialization (follow-up 2).** `TestSiblingReaderChildrenThatStartMCPWritersRunOneAfterTheOther` (app): one parent response with two calls to a nesting reader whose grandchild writes through a stdio MCP server; through the real tool batch, launcher and a real checkpoint the explorers' model requests alternate (first, last, first, last) and one checkpoint covers both; a mutation that drops the nesting term runs them side by side and fails it.
- **Open: a child's own MCP calls in plan mode.** A reader child has no MCP tool that may write, but a child started by an allow entry (whole tool) in plan mode has its full catalog, including MCP write tools: this is what the allow entry asks for, and stdio MCP servers of a plan-mode run keep their normal sandbox form (`MCPSandbox`, see P6). Closes with a decision on a plan-mode form for servers.
- **Not tested.** A remote request served by `remoteBackend.StartSubagent` has no test for plan mode (it has no plan state). The plan-mode parent and child through the real launcher is now tested end to end (follow-up above), and so is the serialization of sibling calls (follow-up 2).

## profile_message `context_trigger`: compact or reset the target from its own transcript (Go, 2026-11-12)

- **Shape.** `tools.native.profile_message.context_trigger: {action: off|compact|reset, after: 0}`. `action` defaults to `off`; `after` is a token threshold, default 0, and is accepted (and does nothing) while `action` is `off`, as `compact_after` was with `compact` off. An explicit `null` is read as absent, like the other numeric settings. The loader is `sessionfs/native_profile_message_context_trigger.go`; the settings carry `NativeProfileMessageSettings.ContextTrigger`, the tool copies it to `ProfileMessageRequest.ContextTrigger`, and `app.profileMessenger.contextStep` runs it in `ProfileRunRequest.BeforeRun` (the target's run registered and its transcript lock held).
- **Legacy aliases.** `compact` (`off|on`) and `compact_after` still load, because live configs use them (`.jad/tools/jad/profile_message.json`): `compact: on` is action `compact`, `compact_after` is `after`. Writing `context_trigger` together with either legacy key is a config error that names both, not a silent override (a `null` legacy `compact_after` or `context_trigger` counts as absent; `compact: null` stays refused as before, audit P2A-R2-04). The legacy keys stay in the allowlist and the schema, marked as aliases. **Superseded (2026-11-10):** the aliases were removed; see "profile_message legacy `compact`/`compact_after` removed and latest transcript path" at the end of this file.
- **Token source.** The trigger no longer reads `ProfileInfo`, so `usage-cache.json` plays no part: a compaction republishes it with the latest response zeroed, which made `compact_after: 0` miss any target that had been compacted (and a stale cache could equally over-count). `messages.jsonl` decides: `transcriptHasContent` (anything but whitespace) first; then, with `after: 0`, no token count at all (a transcript with content but no completed response is acted on); with `after > 0`, `profileMessenger.transcriptTokens` scans the transcript for the last completed response's input tokens (`webui.AddCompletedRecord`, one retry on a changed snapshot) and acts only when they are strictly greater than `after`; none means no action. That read neither reads nor writes `usage-cache.json`. `ProfileInfo` (the `profile` tool's info action and the remote info route) is unchanged and still reports the cached usage.
- **Empty transcript.** A missing, empty or whitespace-only `messages.jsonl` gets no maintenance. A compact logs the Warn `messages.jsonl is empty - nothing to compact`; a reset logged it at Debug only (superseded by T-011: it now logs the Warn `... nothing to reset`). The message is sent either way. A failed usage read is the Warn `profile_message usage read failed; not compacting|resetting`.
- **Claim (once per caller run and target).** *Superseded for compact by "profile_message compact on every call (T-010)" and for reset by "profile_message reset on every call (T-011)" below: no claim exists any more.* Unchanged for compact: the first message of a caller run to a target acts, later ones skip, and a positive `after` takes the claim only when the threshold is passed (the existing tests pin that a target that grows past `after` during the run is handled by a later message). New: with `after: 0` the claim is taken before the transcript is looked at, so a reset never wipes what an earlier message of the same run wrote to a target that was empty; with a positive `after` an empty or below-threshold target does not use the claim. A call that carries no caller-run id (`callerRun == 0`) is never claimed. Traced: `callerRunKey` is set only in `boundRunner.Run`, and a sub-agent's tool calls run on a context the sub-agent manager owns (`SubagentManager.ctx`, not the caller's; `CallerValues` is read only for the cost meter and hook reporter), so a sub-agent's `profile_message` never carries it (`TestAChildsProfileMessageCarriesNoCallerRunValues`; `Execution.RootRun` is the first child's run id, not the caller run, and nothing forgets it). Such a call cannot tell its first message from a later one, so a **compact** keeps acting on every call as before (it only costs a repeat), while a **reset that is due fails closed** (see Reset failures). "Each time" in the request is read as each first message of a caller run, not each message.
- **Reset.** `reset` deletes the target's whole history and what derives from it: `messages.jsonl`, the compaction cache and its backup, the transcript backup, the usage, cursor, run-error and state-context caches and the deleted-history archive (`TurnStore.Reset`), then stops the target's own async handles and sub-agents and drops their unread completion signals (`ResetSessionChildren`, the same reset the HTTP route and the `profile` tool do). It is destructive, irreversible (no backup is written) and never on by default; the schema says so. It runs through `Resolver.resetTarget` (`ResolveMaintenance`, then the `resetResolved` that `ResetProfile` now shares), not `ResetProfile`: `ResetProfile` takes the process lock (which the run already holds, so it would wait forever) and refuses with `ErrRunActive` because the run is registered, as `TestContextTriggerResetWorksUnderTheHeldRunWhereResetProfileRefuses` shows. Like `compactTarget` it takes neither the mutation gate nor the process lock: the held transcript lock and the registered run keep other writers and mutations out. Other callers' queued messages (`profileQueues`) and the caller's own handles are not touched (`ResetOwner` is keyed by the target's owner); a queued message starts after the target is free and gets its own `BeforeRun`, so a reset happens at its start, never beside another run. See Reset failures for what a failed reset does.
- **Reset failures fail closed (supersedes "sends anyway" for reset).** `ProfileRunRequest.BeforeRun` is now `func(ctx) error`; an error fails the start like any that ends before the run (run finished as failed, transcript released, `OnEnd` called, `StartProfileRun` returns it; a queued message's handle ends with it and the line goes on). `contextStep` returns a `*native.ContextTriggerError` (tool code `context_trigger_failed`, text "was not sent the message ... Nothing was sent, and the history may be untouched or partly cleared", client-safe reason only; the detail goes to a Warn log) for a reset that is due and (a) failed, (b) could not locate or read the target transcript, (c) could not count tokens for a positive `after`, or (d) has no running caller run (closeout 2: a sub-agent call now carries its caller's id; only a genuinely missing or ended one is refused). The claim is given back (`callerRunTargets.release`), so the caller's next message of the run retries; once a reset succeeds the run's later messages do not reset again. An empty target and a threshold not passed are not failures. **Compact is unchanged**: a failure is logged and the message is sent anyway.
- **Partial reset failure (superseded by closeout 2 below: the transcript is now published last, so a failed reset is retryable).** `TurnStore.Reset` removed the compaction caches, then atomically empties `messages.jsonl`, then removes the other derived files and the deleted-history archive. A failure at the first two steps leaves the history intact (retry is safe: the same message retries). A failure at a later step (`TestContextTriggerPartialResetFailureLeavesAnEmptyHistoryAndIsNotRetriedByTheTrigger`) leaves an empty history with some caches still present and skips `ResetSessionChildren`; the message is still not sent, but by the empty-transcript rule the retry finds nothing to reset and goes through, so the leftover caches and the target's children are only cleaned by an explicit reset (the `profile` tool or the HTTP route; `resetTarget` after the cause is fixed).
- **Remote.** A remote target (`remote:<name>/...`) is never compacted or reset: the remote API offers info only and a remote server's profiles are not changed on a caller's behalf, and the peer is not asked for info either. The configured trigger is not silently ignored: with `reset`, `executeRemote` refuses before sending (`context_trigger_unsupported`, "cannot reset a remote profile. Nothing was sent"); with `compact` (the legacy `compact: on` alias was removed later) the message is sent and the result carries the information key `context_trigger: compact was not applied ...` (`ProfileMessageNotes`, on inline answers and async handle starts). `off` is silent. `TestRemoteProfileMessageContextTriggerIsNeverSilentlyIgnored` and `TestRemoteProfileMessageCompactNoteOnAnAsyncHandle` pin it.
- **Tests.** `sessionfs` (defaults, aliases, conflicts, enums, bounds, unknown keys, schema agreement), `tools/native` (the setting reaches the messenger, the model schema has no `context_trigger`, remote), `app/profile_message_context_trigger_test.go` (stale/zero cache, no-usage zero threshold, positive threshold from the transcript, last-response rule, empty/missing/blank, real reset with derived files, claim, held-run path, child cleanup, failure, queued and async messages), plus, for the closeout: fail-closed reset (hook, real failure via an unremovable compaction cache, partial real failure via an unremovable usage cache, unreadable transcript, token-count failure, queued message, compact still sends), no-caller-run refusal, a mutation of the target in progress (gate held) and a race of `ResetProfile` against trigger resets (`-race`), `httpapi` `BeforeRun` error, and the sub-agent context. Mutations that go back to `ProfileInfo`, drop `ResetSessionChildren`, drop the empty check, drop the zero-threshold claim, make the threshold `>=`, drop the legacy conflict check, return nil instead of the trigger error, drop the claim release, drop the no-caller-run check, ignore the `BeforeRun` error, or drop the remote refusal or note each fail a test.
- **Open (kept by decision): compacted target with an empty `messages.jsonl`.** A compaction leaves `messages.jsonl` empty (retained turns live in the compaction cache), so by the strict empty-transcript rule a trigger does nothing, **a reset does not clear that compaction summary until the target answers again** and the next run resets it, and a compact warns `messages.jsonl is empty - nothing to compact` even when a cache exists. This is the requested rule, documented in the schema; counting a present compaction cache as content would change it.
- **Superseded (see the closeout 2 section below): sub-agent callers cannot use a reset trigger.** A due reset from a sub-agent's `profile_message` is refused (no caller run id), never run on every message. A sub-agent's compact still acts on every message. Closes by carrying the root caller run's id into the sub-agent context (and forgetting it when the root run ends), which touches the sub-agent manager.
- **Superseded (see the closeout 2 section below): partial reset failure is not finished by the trigger.** See Partial reset failure: leftover derived files and un-stopped children after a late `Reset` failure need an explicit reset. Closes by having `resetResolved` stop the children whenever the history was emptied, or by a trigger that also looks at the derived files.
- **Open: compact failure still sends.** Only reset fails closed; making a failed compaction fail the message too would change `compact_after` behaviour live configs rely on. Superseded (2026-11-10): the legacy `compact_after` key is gone, so only `context_trigger` configs are affected.
- **Open: HTTP-versus-trigger exclusion is tested in-process.** The mutation gate, the held lock and the registered run are exercised (`TestContextTriggerWaitsOutAMutationOfTheTarget`, `TestContextTriggerResetRacesWithExplicitResets`, `TestContextTriggerResetWorksUnderTheHeldRunWhereResetProfileRefuses`), not over the HTTP routes with a real handler and not across processes (the cross-process lock is the same one a user run takes).
- **Open: remote compact is not performed.** A remote profile is never compacted or reset; the caller is told by a refusal (reset) or a note (compact). Closes with a remote API for maintenance.

## profile_message `context_trigger` closeout 2: caller run for sub-agents, retryable reset (Go, 2026-11-12)

- **(Removed by T-011: the caller-run id and `withCallerRun` are gone.) Caller-run id reaches sub-agents (supersedes "a sub-agent call never has an id").** `subagentLauncher.Run` now copies `callerRunKey` from `SubagentRequest.CallerValues` (the calling tool call's values, `context.WithoutCancel`) onto the child's context, as it already did for the cost meter and the hook reporter (`withCallerRun`). Only the value is copied: the child's context stays the sub-agent manager's (its own cancellation, timeout and stop/reset handling, and the sub-agent manager's ownership of the run are unchanged; `TestWithCallerRunCopiesTheIdAndKeepsTheChildsOwnContext`), an id already on the child's context is kept, and a nested sub-agent copies from the context of the call that started it, so the whole tree carries the id of the `boundRunner.Run` that started it. A reset or compact therefore happens once per caller run and target for the tree. `TestContextTriggerResetRunsOncePerCallerRunAcrossSubagentsAndNestedSubagents` runs the real service end to end (HTTP run, `subagent` tool through the real launcher, a child that messages the reviewer and starts a grandchild that messages it too): one reset at the child's message, none at the grandchild's, a new reset in the next run of the caller, and no run entry left behind.
- **Genuinely missing or ended id.** The guard stays: a due reset with no caller run fails closed. "No run" now also covers a run that has ended: `callerRunTargets` tracks active runs (`begin` in `boundRunner.Run`, `forget` at its end) and `claim` refuses a run that is not active instead of recreating its entry, because a background sub-agent (a handle) can outlive the run that started it and an entry for a dead run would never be forgotten (it also leaked before). A compact with no running run acts like it did without an id (every message); a reset is refused (`...no running caller run`, `TestContextTriggerResetOfAnEndedCallerRunFailsClosed`, `TestContextTriggerResetWithoutACallerRunFailsClosed`).
- **Reset order, so a failed reset is retryable (supersedes "Partial reset failure").** `TurnStore.Reset` now removes the compaction caches (first, as before), then the derived files (usage, cursor, run-error and state-context caches, transcript backup, compaction cache and backup), then the deleted-history archive, and publishes the empty `messages.jsonl` last (`Journal.ReplaceRecords`, one atomic rename). Failure semantics: a failure or crash at any step before the publish leaves the history in place with only caches missing; every removal ignores a file already gone, so running Reset again finishes the job, and the trigger's retry sees a non-empty transcript and runs it again, which also stops the children (`resetResolved` runs `ResetSessionChildren` only after a successful `Session.Reset`, so children of a profile whose history is intact keep running until the retry succeeds). After the publish there is nothing left to fail except a best-effort second removal of the derived files, whose error is ignored (it only drops a cache a concurrent usage scan may have written for the old transcript between the removals and the publish; such a cache no longer matches the transcript and was never used). The strict rule is unchanged: a genuinely empty transcript is still no action. Tests: `transcript` `TestResetFailingOnADerivedFileKeepsTheHistoryAndRetries` and `TestResetFailingToPublishKeepsTheHistoryAndRetries` (real failures: an unremovable cache; an unwritable transcript directory), `app` `TestContextTriggerFailedResetIsRetriedWithTheHistoryIntactAndFinishesTheCleanup` (real failure, the same run's next message retries, derived files and the target's children are cleaned only once it completes), and the unchanged `TestContextTriggerEmptyMissingOrBlankTranscriptIsLeftAlone`. Reversing the order again fails the transcript tests.
- **Why not a "reset pending" marker.** A marker file written before the reset and removed after it would also make the empty-transcript retry possible, but it adds a durable state that recovery, run start and every reader would have to honour, and a crash between steps already is a retryable state under the new order. Ordering alone gives the same guarantee with no new state.
- **Open: data removed by a failed reset.** A reset that fails before the publish can already have removed the transcript backup (`messages.backup.jsonl`), the deleted-history archive and the compaction cache (which can hold the retained turns of a compacted history whose `messages.jsonl` is empty), all things the reset deletes anyway, with the history left in place. A user who abandons the reset after the error keeps the history but not those. Closes with a two-phase removal (rename to a trash name, delete after the publish), which was not worth the extra state for data a reset discards by definition. The Reset test that already pinned the compaction cache going first (`TestResetKeepsTheTranscriptWhenTheCompactionCacheCannotBeRemoved`) shows this predates the change.
- **Closed by closeout 3 below: failure after the rename.** If the rename of the empty transcript succeeds but the directory sync fails (`DurabilityTurn` and `DurabilityStrict`), `Reset` returns an error although the history is gone: `resetResolved` then does not stop the children, the message is refused, and the retry finds an empty transcript and goes through. Closes by having `Reset` report whether it published (the journal's generation changed) and `resetResolved` stop the children in that case.
- **Open: background sub-agent after its run ended.** A handle that sends `profile_message` after the caller's run ended has no running caller run, so a due reset is refused for it and a compact acts on every message. Closes by remembering the claims of a run until its handles end, which needs the sub-agent manager to tell the resolver.
- **Closed by T-010: compact for a sub-agent is once per caller run now.** (Compact is evaluated on every message again.) A sub-agent that compacted on every message before now compacts once per caller run and target, like the caller; a test pins reset only (the compact claim is the same code).

## profile_message `context_trigger` closeout 3: published versus unpublished reset (Go, 2026-11-12)

- **Outcome is typed.** `Journal.ReplaceRecords` returns a `*transcript.PublishedError` when its rename already replaced the transcript and only the directory sync after it failed (`DurabilityTurn`/`DurabilityStrict`); every other error from it means nothing was replaced. The error text is unchanged, so compaction, which also calls it, behaves as before. `TurnStore.Reset` treats a published failure as a reset that happened: it still runs the invalidation and the best-effort second removal of derived files, and returns `reset applied but not confirmed durable: <cause>` (still a `*PublishedError` for `errors.As`). An unpublished failure returns as before, before the transcript was touched.
- **Children.** `resetResolved` (shared by `ResetProfile`, the HTTP route and the trigger's `resetTarget`) stops the target's children and drops their signals for a published failure too, then returns the error: the history they were started from is gone whether or not the publish is durable. An unpublished failure stops nobody. Tests: `TestResetResolvedStopsTheChildrenWhenTheResetWasPublishedButNotConfirmed` (plain failure stops none; published stops only the target's child, with the reset reason), and in `transcript` `TestResetWhoseDirectorySyncFailsAfterTheRenameReportsItAsPublished` (injected `dirSyncHook` failure: empty history, derived files gone, typed error, retry succeeds once the sync works) and `TestReplaceRecordsReportsOnlyAPostRenameFailureAsPublished`.
- **Trigger.** The message is still not sent (fail closed), the claim is given back, and the reason the model sees is `the reset was applied but could not be confirmed durable and may need attention`; the log is a Warn `reset applied but not confirmed durable`. A retry, which finds the empty transcript, does nothing and the message goes through: that is right when the history is cleared (the in-process state is cleared and the children stopped), and if a crash brings the old file back the next run's trigger resets it again. `TestContextTriggerResetPublishedButNotConfirmedFailsTheMessageAndSaysSo` pins the reason, the log and that nothing is sent.
- **Wording.** The tool result and the schema no longer say the history "is left as it was": a reset that fails before the publish can already have removed the caches, the transcript backup, the deleted-history archive and the compaction cache. The tool text is now "the context_trigger reset ... could not run (<reason>). The message was not sent, and the reset may need attention: check the profile before relying on its history"; the reasons are `the reset failed and may need attention` and the unconfirmed-durable one above.
- **Open: no real directory-sync failure outside tests.** The failure is injected through `Journal.dirSyncHook`; it was not reproduced on a real filesystem. A crash after an unconfirmed publish is not simulated either.

## profile_message legacy `compact`/`compact_after` removed and latest transcript path (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **Breaking removal, no compatibility layer.** `tools.native.profile_message.compact` and `compact_after` (aliases of `context_trigger {action: compact, after}`, kept by the 2026-11-12 decision) are gone from the loader (`NativeProfileMessageSettings` is filled from `context_trigger` alone), the key allowlist, `sample/schemes/setting.schema.json` and the tests. A config that still has either key fails to load with `tools.native.profile_message.compact was removed; use context_trigger {action, after} instead ...` (or `compact_after`), the house form for removed keys (`removed_keys.go`), checked before the allowlist so the key is named whatever its value (including `null`) and even beside `context_trigger`. The old "context_trigger cannot be combined with the legacy ..." error is gone with the aliases. `context_trigger` is unchanged. The live `.jad/tools/jad/profile_message.json` already used `context_trigger`; configs elsewhere that still use the aliases must be edited (`compact: on` is `action: compact`, `compact_after` is `after`). The historical entries above stay as the record of what was decided then.
- **`latest` no longer repeats the transcript path where the result names it.** The still-running `block_ms` result of `profile_message` already carries `transcript:` (and `caller_transcript:`) in its information, so its `latest` block now says `last transcript step <id>` instead of `transcript: <path> (last step <id>)`. The too-large and no-steps-yet branches drop the path too; the no-news block keeps its `no new activity since` line and then the last step (nothing when the transcript has no step). `activityLatest` takes a `namePath` flag; `profileMessageDriver.latest` passes `!info.inline`, and `latestInfo.inline` is set only when the text goes into the starting call's own result (`latestText`). `async status`/`wait`/`list` of a running `profile_message` handle do not repeat any path elsewhere (a running entry has no `ref_transcript` yet), so their `latest` still names the path once, as before. A sub-agent always names it (`namePath` true), so its output is unchanged: no evidence of the same duplication, and the sub-agent start result carries no transcript key. `TestLatestActivityWithoutPathNamesOnlyTheLastTranscriptStep`, `TestProfileMessageHandleReportsTheTargetsActivity` and `TestSubagentHandleReportsItsActivityThroughAsyncStatus` pin the three.
- **Open: the schema text of `latest_scan_max_bytes`** now says a larger transcript "is not summarized, and the block says so", with the path named only for a sub-agent; there is no test that reads that sentence. Closes with a schema-description test if the wording is ever relied on.
- **Open: the race gate needs a longer timeout for the native package.** `verify-go.sh --race "./internal/tools/native/"` runs `-count=3` and hit Go's default 10m test timeout (the plain suite passes); it passes with `--race "-timeout 60m ./internal/sessionfs/ ./internal/tools/native/"`. Closes with a timeout setting in `verify-go.sh`.

## sub-agent `latest` no longer repeats the transcript path in the start result (Go, 2026-11-13)

- **Correction of the entry above.** The sub-agent running `block_ms` result does carry `transcript:` (`withTranscript` in `renderRun`, once the child has a folder), so its `latest` block repeated the path. `subagentDriver.latest` now passes `!info.inline` to `activityLatest`, like `profileMessageDriver`: the start result's `latest` says `last transcript step <id>` and the path appears once, as `transcript:`. `async status`/`wait`/`list` (`inline` false) still name `transcript: <path> (last step <id>)` in `latest`, once.
- **No folder yet.** `run.dir` is empty until the launcher calls `OnTranscript`. Then there is no `transcript:` item and `activityLatest` has no path to name either (`no transcript yet`), so nothing is lost. `run.dir` is set once and never cleared, so `subagentTool.await` takes its view again after building the latest block: a folder the block saw is always in the transcript item. A run that ended in between renders as the finished result (and is marked read) instead of a running one.
- **Remote** sub-agents and remote `profile_message` are unchanged: `remoteLatest` never names a path.
- Tests: `TestSubagentHandleReportsItsActivityThroughAsyncStatus` (path once in the start result, once per poll), `TestSubagentStartResultWithoutFolderThenPollNamesTranscript`.
- **Race check (2026-11-13).** `go test -race -count=3 -timeout 60m ./internal/tools/native/ -run 'TestSubagent|TestProfileMessageHandle|TestLatestActivity'` exited 0 (`ok`, 25.7s), covering both sub-agent tests above and the profile_message one. No race reported. The full-package `verify-go.sh --race` was not run (see the timeout entry above).
- **Open: no deterministic test for the second `run.view()` in `await`.** The window between the first view and the latest block (folder set in between) cannot be forced from a test: `asyncmgr.Manager.drivers` is private so the subagent driver cannot be wrapped, `await` takes its views itself, and `run.mu` is taken by both `view()` and the driver, so holding it cannot separate them. It would need a production hook. Closes with a test seam in `await` or a fake `AsyncHost`.

## Unified agent runs R0: baseline, inventory, drift and phase plan (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **What R0 adds (tests only, no production change).** `app/run_baseline_golden_test.go` with goldens in `app/testdata/run_baseline/`: a three-level ephemeral tree (`TestRunBaselineNestedSubagentTree`: session, child and grandchild `messages.jsonl`, and the tools array of every provider request, which pins that the child at `max_depth` has no `subagent` tool), a remote API sub-agent start plus resume (`TestRunBaselineRemoteSubagentStartAndResume`: both run folders, the seeded copy of the source, the status keys), and a `profile_message` chain (`TestRunBaselineProfileMessageChain`: dev/coder -> review/reviewer, the reviewer's call back refused as `profile_cycle`, both persistent transcripts). Masked: temporary paths, the random hex of a run folder, remote run ids, and input batch ids and content tokens as placeholders numbered per file (so a resumed copy still shows equal ids). `JAD_UPDATE_RUN_BASELINE=1` rewrites them; a rewrite is a contract change. `native/unified_run_inventory_test.go` lists every field of `SubagentRequest` (8), `subagentStart` (32) and `ProfileMessageRequest` (13) with its destination in the design (caller, spec, admission, registry, starter, open) and fails when a field changes. `mutate-check.sh` caught four mutations: the sub-agent summary text, the `profile_cycle` text, the leaf catalog choice in `startRunFrom`, and the resume seed copy in `openStore`.
- **Drift from the design (written at `d72ef85`, 11 commits behind `a18f9f47`).** Line references and sizes moved (`subagent.go` 896 -> 1104 lines, `subagent_manager.go` 1214 -> 1263, `subagent_call.go` 520 -> 541, `subagent_worktree.go` 369 -> 458, `subagent_remote.go` 397 -> 460; `admitNestedLocked` is at :694, `subagentStart` :559, `hookTool`/`hookWith` :251-264). New since the design: `ProfileMessageRequest.ContextTrigger` and the caller run id carried across sub-agent levels (`withCallerRun`, `callerRunKey`, T-003/T-004); `subagentStart.runMCP` (P6 per-run stdio MCP in the worktree), which the starter's step 4 must keep, although section 3.6 says MCP stays per session or toolset; the immutable remote scheduling snapshot (`remoteAgentSettings`). The section 3.3 table is wrong on one source: `RemoteCaller` is a context value (`WithRemoteCaller`), not an `ExecutionContext` field; the chain max, child-call mark and remote hops are context values too (`profile_message.go`), and the cost meter and hook reporter are `session` types while `session` imports `tools`, so a `CallerContext` in `tools` cannot name them (R1 must keep them as context values or put interfaces in `tools`).
- **Phase plan under the decider's rule (no behaviour change in R1-R5, behaviour in R6).** R1: `CallerContext` built beside the existing fields (inventory test updated, field-walk test added), nothing reads it yet. R2: `Resolver.StartRun` for ephemeral runs only, a move of `subagentLauncher.Run` with `childConfig` and the native catalog kept. R3: one loader for `agents`, `agents_dir` (`agent.json` kept, no refusals) and profiles into a template, with the child's config still based on the caller's `SessionConfig`. R4: catalog from `prepareRun`, keyed by (template, environment, plan mode, at-max-depth) so the leaf tool set stays. R5: one registry and admission with today's counting kept. R6: U1, U3, U4, U7 and the section 3.2 config order. R7: dead paths, schema text, `sample/`, docs. Each phase keeps the R0 goldens equal and runs `verify-go.sh`.
- **Decided (Master, 2026-11-10): no behaviour change through R5; the behaviour-changing steps move to R6.** Three design steps would change behaviour inside R3-R5, and all move to R6: section 3.2 (template config from root, session, template instead of the caller's config; it changes what a child inherits when the caller is not the session's default profile), section 3.6 (depth checked at call time, no leaf catalog; it would add `subagent` to the deepest child's tools, which `nested_tree_tools.txt` forbids) and section 3.5 (`max_depth` over both kinds, one chain; it changes when a `profile_message` from a child is refused, and a profile reached by `profile_message` would no longer start its children at depth 0, which `profile_target_subagent_tools.txt` pins). R3-R5 move code only, keeping today's config base, tool sets and counting. The R0 goldens stay byte-equal through R5 and are rewritten only by an R6 decision. Also kept: `agent.json` loading (U2), `subagent_stop` as the only hook of an ephemeral run (U5), the UI as it is (U6), and the remote limitations (no `model` or `sandbox` argument on a remote agent, no local transcript or catalog for a remote run).
- **Open until R6: U1, U3, U4, U7.** The user decides them when R6 starts. Until then nothing of them is built, and the goldens show today's behaviour: for U3, the child is narrowed by the session profile's `tools.deny` only; for U4, `max_chain` is counted on its own; for U7, `max_depth` defaults to 2 with a maximum of 8. *Superseded (2026-11-11): see "Unified agent runs: completion assessment and accepted departures (T-007)".*
- **Baselines added in the R0 follow-up (closes the four R0 gaps).** All four use the same harness, masks and update switch. Run ids `sub_…` and `rr_…` are masked as numbered placeholders.
  - **`TestRunBaselineLocalSubagentResume`.** A session run starts explore; a second run resumes it through the `subagent` tool's `resume` argument. The run id is read from the run's manifest (`<id>.json`), because a finished blocking result does not name it. Goldens: `local_resume_session.jsonl` (the second result carries `resumed_from`) and `local_resume_children.txt` (the resumed folder starts with a copy of the source).
  - **`TestRunBaselineRemoteSubagentFromTheCaller`.** A layout session's `subagent` tool with `remotes: ["peer"]` starts `remote:peer/demo/dev/coder/explore` on a second service (the e2e server). Goldens: the caller's transcript with `remote_run: peer/<remote-run-1>`, the caller's tool definitions, and the child transcript on the serving side (`remote_caller_*`). The tool refuses a session with only `remotes`, so the toolset also has one inline agent and `async`.
  - **`TestRunBaselineProfileMessageTargetStartsASubagent`.** dev/coder sends `profile_message` to review/reviewer. The reviewer's run starts explore (`tools: [skill, subagent]`), which reads the notes skill. Goldens: all three transcripts (the child's folder is under the reviewer's `tools/.subagents`) and the tools of every request (`profile_target_subagent_*`).
  - **`TestRunBaselineSampleAgentDefinitions`.** `sample/subagents` is loaded through `agents_dir` in a session with the sample coding natives (`exec`, `async`, `subagent`) and the `decide_systemone` extension. Golden: `sample_agent_definitions.txt`, with the session's tools, then each agent's tools and first-request input (prompt and task). explore gets `exec`, `async`, `decide_systemone` and `subagent`; triager gets `decide_systemone` only.
  - **Checks.** `mutate-check.sh` CAUGHT five mutations: the seed copy (local resume), the `remote_run` information (remote caller), the depth of the leaf choice (profile target), the agent tool filter and the prompt text (sample definitions). All `TestRunBaseline*` tests pass with `-count=5` and with `-race -count=3`.
- **Open: limits of these baselines.**
  - The sample agents never call `decide_systemone` (there is no classifier server), so the baseline pins that tool's definition and the prompts, but not its output.
  - The local-resume test changes the fake provider's script between its two runs, under the provider's mutex.
  - The masking hides a change to the masked formats themselves (batch id, content token, run id, folder suffix); those formats have tests of their own.
  - Closes by adding a scenario beside these when a phase needs more.
- **Isolation-sensitive tests (Linux, bwrap at `/opt/my/bin/bwrap`).** `go test ./internal/app -run 'Sandbox|Worktree|RunMCP|Isolat|ProfileDelegat'` and `go test ./internal/tools/native -run 'Sandbox|Worktree|RunMCP|Isolat|Holder|Overlay'` exited 0 (27 and 114 top-level passes, no failure); the only skips are the two by-design `no_sandbox` slow cases of `TestRunMCPLoaderStopsTheServersProcessGroup`. The known isolation gaps (clone half of P6, D7) stay deferred; R2-R5 must keep these tests green.

## Unified agent runs R1: CallerContext carried beside the existing fields (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **What R1 adds.** `tools.CallerContext` (`internal/tools/caller_context.go`) and `ExecutionContext.Caller()`. It mirrors the 18 run-scoped `ExecutionContext` fields (the set `ForNested` keeps), renaming three to the design's names (`WorkspaceRoot` -> `Workspace`, `AgentDepth` -> `Depth`, `ProcessOwner` -> `HandleOwner`). It adds three fields the call site fills: `RemoteCaller` (from `WithRemoteCaller`), `ModelChoice` and `SandboxChoice`. `SubagentRequest.Caller` is set in `startRunFrom` (`subagentCaller`) and `ProfileMessageRequest.Caller` in `profileMessageTool.execute` (`profileMessageCaller`). Nothing reads either field; `Execution`, `CallerValues`, the request fields and the context values stay the source of truth. No change to `app/` is needed, so the design's R1 file list (`app/subagent.go`, `app/profile_message.go`) is not touched.
- **It describes the caller, not the started run.** `Caller` is built from the calling call's `ExecutionContext` at the start, before the manager sets the child's depth, handle owner and root run, and before a worktree moves the child's root and path scope. Those rewrites write only `request.Execution` (`openWorktree`, `SubagentManager.start`) or a copy (`profile_delegation.go`, `movedScope`), so the caller snapshot cannot go stale or pick up the child's scope. Pointers (`Environment`, `PathScope`) are the caller's own, not copies.
- **Tests.**
  - `tools/caller_context_test.go`: a field walk over a filled `ExecutionContext`. It fails when a run-scoped field has no `CallerContext` counterpart, when `Caller()` drops or changes one, when a per-call field is mirrored, or when a `CallerContext` field is neither mirrored nor filled by the call site. It also checks that `ForNested()` keeps the same caller context.
  - `native/caller_context_test.go`: the propagation tests.
    - Subagent call: sandbox choice, model, remote caller, environment identity, and the child's own scope unchanged.
    - Nested start: the leaf's caller is the boss (depth 1, the boss's run id and root).
    - Worktree child: the caller keeps the session's workspace while `Execution` moves into the worktree.
    - `profile_message` from a plan-mode child: the caller's raw environment beside the request's plan-mode form; the request fields unchanged.
  - The R0 inventory lists `Caller` on both requests.
  - `mutate-check.sh` CAUGHT five mutations: building the subagent caller from the child's context, dropping `RemoteCaller`, dropping `SandboxChoice` (profile_message), dropping `RemoteHops` from `Caller()`, and removing a mirrored field from the struct. A manual run of the last one showed the walk's message for the removed field (MCPRoute).
- **Open: caller facts still carried as context values.** Not in `CallerContext`:
  - The cost meter and hook reporter are `session` types, and `session` imports `tools`.
  - `callerMessagesPathKey` (CallerTranscript) and `callerRunKey` (T-003 caller run id) are keys private to `app`.
  - The profile chain is read from the httpapi registry (`RunningProfileRunChain`).
  - `max_chain` and the child-call mark are context values set by `profile_message`.
  - They reach a run as before, through `CallerValues` or the call's context.
  - Closes in R2 (`StartRun` takes `CallerValues` as the values carrier) and R5 (one chain in admission). Interfaces in `tools` for the meter and reporter are possible if R2 needs them typed. *Superseded (2026-11-11): see "Unified agent runs: completion assessment and accepted departures (T-007)".*
- **Open: hazards for the phase that first reads `Caller`.**
  - `CallerContext.RequestInteraction` is the caller's raw question channel. A child that outlives its call gets `closedChannelGuard` on `Execution` only. R2 must keep that guard, not read the raw channel for a handle or background run.
  - `CallerContext.Environment` is the caller's ceiling as carried. `ProfileMessageRequest.Environment` is its plan-mode form (`callerEnvironment`). R5 must narrow by `PlanMode` when it reads `Caller.Environment`.
  - `ModelChoice` is the trimmed argument; `SandboxChoice` is the sandbox the run starts in (for a resume without a `sandbox` argument, the source's, D22).
  - Holding `Caller` keeps the caller's hooks and environment reachable for the request's life, as `Execution` already does; no behaviour change.
- **Checks.**
  - `go test ./internal/tools/ ./internal/tools/native/ ./internal/app/ ./internal/httpapi/` exited 0.
  - The R0 goldens (`TestRunBaseline*`) pass with `-count=5` and `-race -count=3`, unchanged.
  - The new and related native and tools tests pass with `-race -count=3`.
  - No `messages-golden-diff` baseline build was run: nothing reads the new field, and the R0 goldens cover the transcripts and tool definitions.

## Unified agent runs R2: ephemeral runs start through Resolver.StartRun (Go, 2026-11-10)

- **What R2 adds.** `app/run_start.go`: `RunKind` (only `RunEphemeral`), `RunTemplate` (`Base` = the configuration of the session that holds the subagent tool, `Agent` = the agent definition), `RunSpec`, `RunResult` and `Resolver.StartRun`. The body of `subagentLauncher.Run` moved unchanged into `runEphemeral`; the only edits are the receivers, now `*Resolver` or plain functions over `RunTemplate`/`RunSpec`. `subagentLauncher.Run` is now a thin adapter: `ephemeralRunSpec` maps every `SubagentRequest` field to the spec, `StartRun` runs it, and the result is mapped back. The `native.SubagentLauncher` interface, `SubagentRequest`, the manager and every native file are unchanged.
- **Architecture chosen (departs from design §3.4).**
  - `StartRun` is synchronous and returns `(RunResult, error)`. There is no `RunHandle` yet. The manager already owns the goroutine, the slot, the timeout context, `openWorktree`, `startRunMCP`, the panic recovery in `runLauncher`, the async-handle sweep, `closeWorktree` and `finish`, in that order. A `StartRun` that started its own goroutine would put the run outside `runLauncher`'s `recover` and duplicate the manager's cancel and wait. The manager calls the launcher, and the launcher calls `StartRun` in the same goroutine, so the panic boundary and the order are unchanged by construction. A `RunHandle` comes when a caller needs a run that outlives the call, which is R5's persistent path.
  - The design's steps 2 (admission) and 4 (worktree) stay in `SubagentManager`. `StartRun` does no admission, so nothing is admitted twice. Step 5 (`prepareRun`, the catalog from the resolver) is R4. Step 1 (template config order) is R6. Until then the template base is the calling session's config, which is the config `childConfig` copied before.
  - `RunSpec` carries five bridging fields beside the design's five: `CallID`, `Tools`, `Execution`, `CallerValues` and `OnTranscript`. They are what the tool and manager still decide. R4 removes `Tools`, and R5 moves `Execution`'s run scope and `CallerValues` into admission and `Caller`.
  - No cycle: launcher -> `StartRun` -> `runEphemeral`, and nothing in `runEphemeral` calls a launcher.
- **Behaviour kept.** The task is JSON-encoded in the adapter, before the store opens instead of after; `json.Marshal` of a string cannot fail, so nothing visible changes. Error texts, the folder name (`<callID>-<hex>`), the seed copy, the prompt cache key scope (`MessagesPath` + agent name), the compaction settings without `Summary`/`OnSummaryError`/`Overflow`, state context, `LeafBudget`, the cost meter and hook reporter from `CallerValues`, `withCallerRun`, `RecordUnrecordedSpend` and `subagent_stop` are the same code. Two comments that named `subagentLauncher.Run` as the carrier of the caller run id now name `Resolver.StartRun`.
- **Still unread.** `RunSpec.Caller` is carried but not read; `Execution` and `CallerValues` stay the source of the run's scope. The R1 hazard stands: a background or handle child's question channel is guarded on `Execution` by the manager, so a later phase must not read `Caller.RequestInteraction` in its place.
- **Tests.** `app/run_start_test.go`:
  - `TestEphemeralRunSpecCarriesEveryRequestField` walks `SubagentRequest` and checks that every field reaches the spec unchanged, so a new request field fails until it is mapped.
  - `TestStartRunRefusesAKindItDoesNotStart`: no folder is made and `OnTranscript` is not called.
  - `TestStartRunReportsAModelErrorBeforeItMakesAFolder`: the error still starts `load the model of agent <name>: `.
  - `TestStartRunOfACancelledCallKeepsItsFolderAndReportsTheCancel`: the error is `context.Canceled`, one `OnTranscript` call names a `call_1-<hex>` folder under the storage directory, and no work is reported.
  - `subagent_resume_seed_test.go` now calls `openEphemeralStore` with a `RunSpec`.
  - `mutate-check.sh` CAUGHT five mutations: the adapter dropping `Caller`, `Seed` (R0 resume golden) and `CallerValues` (cost cap test), removing the kind check, and `subagent_stop` reporting the wrong agent name.
- **Verified: one goroutine from `recover` to the moved body (R2 follow-up).**
  - `SubagentManager.start` launches the run with `go m.execute(ctx, run, spec, holdsSlot)` (`subagent_manager.go`). `gonav callers SubagentManager.runLauncher` shows its one caller is `SubagentManager.execute`, which calls it synchronously (`result, err := m.runLauncher(childContext, spec)`).
  - `runLauncher` sets `defer recover()` and returns `spec.launcher.Run(ctx, spec.request)` in the same frame. `subagentLauncher.Run` calls `ephemeralRunSpec` and then `l.resolver.StartRun` directly. `StartRun` returns `r.runEphemeral(ctx, spec)` directly. `runEphemeral` calls `childConfig`, `providerAPIKey`, `openEphemeralStore`, `OnTranscript`, `runStreamer`, `session.NewRunner`, `stateContextFor`, `runner.Run` and `subagentStopHook` in sequence (checked with `gonav show`).
  - `grep -nE '(^|[[:space:]])go [a-zA-Z_(]'` over `app/run_start.go` and `app/subagent.go` finds only two comments ("go to the calling run's", "go to the server log"), and no `go` statement. So no new goroutine carries moved code, and a panic in `ephemeralRunSpec`, `StartRun`, `runEphemeral` or `subagentStopHook` unwinds into `runLauncher`'s `recover`, as it did before R2. No fix was needed.
  - Not covered by that `recover`, before or after R2: goroutines started inside unchanged callees such as `session.Runner.Run` (tool calls, stream handling) and the manager's other goroutines. R2 did not change them.
- **Deferred tests (open).**
  - Injected-panic test: no test panics inside `runEphemeral` and checks that the run finishes as `failed` with "sub-agent launcher panicked". The boundary holds by the call chain above. Add the test before R5, which is the first phase allowed to move the goroutine or add a `RunHandle`. It must fail if `StartRun` starts its own goroutine.
  - Direct success test: no unit test calls `StartRun` for a run that succeeds. The success, timeout, stop, hook, cost, compaction, state-context, provider-key and resume paths are covered through the manager and launcher by the existing integration tests and the R0 goldens. Add a direct test when `StartRun`'s contract changes (R4 catalog, R5 persistent kind or `RunHandle`), using a provider fixture.
- **Golden coverage versus `messages-golden-diff` (closed for R2's scope).**
  - The R0 goldens in `app/testdata/run_baseline/` compare transcripts and provider tool definitions byte for byte after masking. They passed unchanged after R2 with `-count=5` and in the `-race -count=3` set.
  - `messages-golden-diff` was then run against a pre-R2 baseline, following the skill. Two detached worktrees of HEAD `a18f9f47` were made in `/tmp`. `cur` got every uncommitted backend change (R0, R1, R2). `base` got R0 and R1 only: the `internal/tools` diff and every untracked file except `app/run_start.go` and `app/run_start_test.go`, so its `app/subagent.go` is the pre-R2 launcher. Both built with `go build -o /tmp/mgd/<tree>-go ./cmd/jad` (exit 0).
  - Scenario: the seven `TestRunBaseline*` tests, run in each tree after its `testdata/run_baseline` was deleted and with `JAD_UPDATE_RUN_BASELINE=1`, so each tree wrote fresh output. They cover the nested tree, local resume through `subagent`, remote start and resume, a remote sub-agent from the caller, the `profile_message` chain, a `profile_message` target that starts a sub-agent, and the `sample/subagents` tool definitions. Both trees use the same in-process stub provider and inputs. All seven passed in both trees (exit 0).

These are 5 `.jsonl` transcripts plus 10 `.txt` files that hold 14 more `messages.jsonl` and every provider request's tools array. The `cur` output was also `diff -r`-equal to the repo's goldens (exit 0). Scratch worktrees and binaries were removed, and the repo goldens were not touched.

The scenarios run the same `app` service code in-process, which is the code R2 moved.
