  - **Classification is conservative:** whether a narrowed child is a writer (`changesFiles`, `nestsWriter`) still follows its agent's whole tool set, so a narrowed child may be scheduled as a writer (runs inline, takes the checkpoint) though its narrowed tools only read.
  - **Per-run MCP servers:** an isolated child's own stdio servers (`runMCP`) and a delegated worktree's (`StartMCP`) start for the agent's or profile's servers even when the inherited deny removes all their tools; the tools are unreachable, but the processes start.
  - **Queued profile_message start:** shares `request()` with the immediate start; not tested separately.
  - **Provider history:** a text-only target whose history holds earlier tool calls was tested with the Responses fixture only; a translator that requires tool definitions next to tool history (Anthropic) is not verified. The same holds for a profile whose own settings leave no tool.
  - **In memory only:** the ceiling is not persisted; a queued message or a run recovered after a restart has none (neither survives a restart today).
  - Not measured: no benchmark. The per-call cost is one pass over the child's tools per deny entry, and a new catalog only when it narrows.
  - **Verification limitation (unrelated flake):** one `verify-go.sh` run failed only because `internal/tools/mcp` `TestOAuthLoginStoresTokensAndARunUsesAndRefreshesThem` hung until the 10 m timeout (blocked in `Login` waiting for the authorization code). The package has no change in T-007, and the same hang reproduces on a clean worktree of HEAD `a18f9f47` (1 of 3 batches of `-count=20`). Recorded as a bug report; closing it needs a fix of the test's loopback/callback handshake (or a deadline on its context).

## Unified agent runs U3 follow-up: a tool_smith script reaches only its own run's tools (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Gap closed.** A script reached the owner's `tools.native.tool_smith.tools` filtered by the owner's profile and the run's `Deny` only. So a sub-agent's script ran tools its agent's allow list leaves out, and a run whose request named tools (`RunOptions.Tools`, the run route's `tools`) gave its scripts tools the run itself did not have. Verified before the fix: `TestToolSmithScriptOfAChildIsBoundByItsAgentsAllowListOnly` (scripter lists `tool_smith`, `read`, `subagent`; its script ran `grep`) and `TestToolSmithScriptReachesOnlyTheToolsTheRunsRequestNamed` (a run narrowed to `tool_smith` reached `skill`) fail with the filter removed (mutation-checked).
- **Decision: a run-specific filter, not the dispatching catalog.** New `ExecutionContext.RunTools func(Definition) bool` (mirrored in `CallerContext.RunTools`, as the field-walk tests require). `ToolSmithNested.allowed` keeps a bound tool only when `RunTools` is nil or covers it, after the profile and `Deny`.
  - A sub-agent's `RunTools` is its own child catalog's `Has` (after the caller's deny narrowing), set in `startRunFrom` on every start and resume. That catalog holds lazy tools gated, not dropped, so a lazy extension tool the child may load stays reachable from its scripts.
  - A bound (persistent) run sets it on every run: nil without a request list, `AnyEntryMatches(options.Tools)` with one, the same rule `Catalog.Only` uses.
  - Why not `Dispatcher.Has`: the dispatching catalog of an owner run in plan mode is the plan catalog, which drops every non-read-only tool. A plan-mode `allow_tools` entry for `tool_smith` is documented to keep the tool whole, so scripts would lose their write tools in plan mode. That is a behaviour change outside this task, so plan mode does not change `RunTools`.
  - No allow list is inherited: `RunTools` is the run's own, never a ceiling. Each child replaces it with its own catalog, and a profile_message target's bound runner sets its own. A child whose agent has no list keeps every tool from its scripts under a narrowed caller (tested). Deny stays the only inherited ceiling (U3).
  - No remote change: `RunTools` is a function in memory and is not sent; a remote run's own request `tools` narrows it on that server through its bound runner.
- **Unchanged:** owner runs with no request list (nil `RunTools`), lazy extension tools in owner runs (`TestToolSmithScriptRunsAnAllowlistedLazyExtensionToolOnly`), the refusal a script sees (`tool X not allowed; allowed: …`, status `invalid_input`), tool definitions and goldens. The tool_smith description is model-visible and was not changed. The `setting.schema.json` description of `tool_smith.tools` now states the rule.
- **Tests:** native `TestToolSmithScriptOfAChildIsBoundByItsAgentsAllowListOnly` (replaces the gap pin; also no inheritance to a grandchild, owner unchanged), `TestToolSmithBridgeKeepsOnlyTheRunsOwnTools`, `TestToolSmithScriptReachesALazyExtensionToolOnlyWhenTheRunsOwnToolsHoldIt`; app `TestToolSmithScriptReachesOnlyTheToolsTheRunsRequestNamed` (real bound runner and interpreter; no list, a list without the tool, a list naming it, an `mcp:` entry). `mutate-check.sh` 6/6 caught with real test failures: filter removed in the bridge, nil passed from tool_smith (native and app), the child inheriting the caller's `RunTools`, the child line removed, the bound runner line removed.
- **Open:**
  - **Plan mode:** a plan-mode run's scripts still reach the non-read-only tools the run had before plan mode, when `tool_smith` itself is kept (a plan-mode `allow_tools` entry). That is today's documented behaviour, not changed here; bounding scripts by the plan catalog needs a decision.
  - **Interpreter:** the new script tests skip without bun or a TypeScript-capable node, as the existing tool_smith tests do. They ran here.
  - **Toolset children (not verified):** the bridge holds the owner's tool instances; whether a toolset child's script should reach its toolset's own tool copies (and hooks) instead was not examined. Unchanged by this follow-up.

## Unified agent runs template T0: characterization done; R3a stopped on a composition conflict (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Scope.** T0 of the template plan (agent composition, MCP wrapper and sampler, settings stamps), then R3a only if T0 showed one composed config is safe. Only tests and an opt-in test fixture changed (`app/run_mcp_test.go`: `JAD_APP_STDIO_MCP_START_LOG` start log, `JAD_APP_STDIO_MCP_ASK` sampling tool `ask`); no production code, no golden.
- **T0 (a) composition, observed.**
  - `sessionfs` `TestAgentToolsetConfigDiffersFromTheCallersOnlyInToolsSelectionAndIdentity`: for a caller profile whose toolset carries exec, async, the subagent section, a hook and an MCP server, with a session state context, sandbox and a profile `tools.deny`, the config an agent's toolset is loaded as (`AgentToolsets[key]`) differs from the caller's config in exactly: the tool surface (`Native*` of both toolsets, `MCPServers`, `Hooks`, `StateContext`, `NativeSubagent`, `AgentToolsets`), the identity `loadLayoutSessionSettings` sets after the composition (`Profile`, `DefaultProfile`, `Profiles`, `ProfileNames`, `ProfilePath`, `RemotesDir`) and the selection (`ModelPath`, `ModelPaths`, plus `ReasoningEffort` when the caller selected `openai/cheap@high`). Everything else (sandbox, compaction, persistence, image settings, profile deny, ...) is equal. The derived `ModelPath` is neither the selected model nor a catalog model file.
  - `app` `TestAgentRunConfigLayersTheAgentOverTheCallersSelection`: with the caller's selected `openai/cheap@high`, `childConfig` gives a plain agent and a toolset agent the selected model and effort, and an agent with its own model that model with its own (empty) effort; every run keeps the caller's subagent section. The toolset's derived config as the run base fails: `openEphemeralStore` refuses it (`tools.native.subagent is not configured`) and it does not carry the selection.
- **R3a decision: not implemented (conflict, evidence above).** One composed config "root → session → caller profile → agent" cannot serve both the run and the tools of a toolset agent without changing behaviour:
  - The tools of a toolset agent come from a composition in which the agent's toolset replaces the profile's (the caller profile's toolset is not part of it).
  - The run reads, from the same struct, parts that only the caller's composition has: `NativeSubagent.StorageDir` (`openEphemeralStore`; the subagent section often sits in the profile's toolset, `sample/jad/tools/coding/full.json`), the selected model and effort (`childConfig`), `Hooks` (`subagentStopHook` reads `Template.Base.Hooks`) and `StateContext` (`stateContextFor` reads the base). The toolset composition drops the subagent section and deletes the state context on purpose (`loadAgentToolsets`, `compose`).
  - So a single config is a per-field merge of two compositions. For agents without a toolset R3a is exactly today's `childConfig`, and moving it into `sessionfs` would be a cosmetic wrapper. Stopped as instructed.
  - **What closes it (needs a decision):** (A) "caller facts last": the template config is the agent's composition (root, session, caller profile settings, the agent's toolset or else the profile's, the agent's fields), then caller facts layered after it: the selected model when the agent has none, the subagent section (storage, limits), the state context, the stop hooks and the prompt-cache scope. It needs those fields classified as caller facts (design 3.3 does not list them) and a field-walk test that fails on an unclassified `SessionConfig` field. (B) Keep the two configs and drop R3a from the plan. R4a (split `buildRegisteredCatalog`) does not depend on this choice.
- **T0 (b) MCP, observed (two bugs, recorded as bug reports, not fixed here).**
  - `TestConfinedProfileMessageRunRestartsTheTargetsSharedStdioServerInTheCallersSandbox`: a profile_message run narrowed by the caller's sandbox restarts the target's shared stdio server inside the caller's sandbox (start count 1 after two own runs, 2 after the message run with 1 start under the caller's command sandbox, 3 after the next own run). Cause: `targetConfiner` narrows the runner's config, and `buildRegisteredCatalog` sets the shared manager's wrapper from it. It contradicts the comment of `profile_message_sandbox.go` (D10). Mutation-checked (wrapper line removed: caught).
  - `TestProfileMessageModelChoiceStaysTheSamplerOfTheTargetsSharedServersUntilItsNextRun`: after a message run with `model: openai/small`, the target's shared server's sampling is answered by `model-small` until the target's next own run prepares again. The earlier code-trace bug report (sampler overwritten by any catalog build) is now confirmed at runtime. Mutation-checked.
  - `TestAgentToolsetMCPServersHaveNoSampler`: a toolset server's sampling request is refused (no sampler on the toolset manager); with a sampler set on that manager the same server is answered (control).
  - Closing either bug needs a decision touching D10/D20: per-run MCP managers for narrowed runs (the `runMCPLoader` pattern) or a per-run sampler/route, or refusing a narrowing that covers mcp.
- **T0 (d) settings stamps, observed.** `TestSettingsStampSeesEveryTemplateInputButMCPServerFiles`: edits of an agent's toolset file, an agent folder's `agent.json` and another profile of the session make the caller's stamp stale. MCP server files are not stamp inputs, for the session's servers and an agent toolset's alike: the config keeps only their path and the MCP manager reads the file on every `LoadTools` (`getConnection`), so an edit reaches the next prepared run without a new load. Consistent, not a template gap.
- **Update (2026-11-11, next section):** the first MCP bug (narrowed run rewraps the shared server) is fixed; the sampler bug stays open (T-008). **Closed (2026-11-11):** the sampler bug is fixed by T-008 (last section).
- **Open.** R3a (decision A or B above); the two MCP bugs; R4a (done since: see "R4a catalog assembly split" below)/R4b, U1 and the decisions 2 to 5 of the proposal are unchanged. Not measured: no benchmark (no production change). *Superseded (2026-11-11): see "Unified agent runs: completion assessment and accepted departures (T-007)".*

## Unified agent runs template prerequisite: a narrowed profile_message run no longer rewraps the target's shared MCP servers (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Bug (T0 (b), confirmed).** A profile_message run narrowed by its caller's sandbox built its catalog on the target's MCP manager that every run of the profile shares (`sharedMCPManager`) and set that manager's command wrapper from the narrowed config. Because the wrapper key changed, the target's stdio server restarted inside the caller's sandbox, then restarted again outside it on the target's next own run (starts 1 → 2 → 3). A listing taken before the restart called a closed connection: before the fix, `TestConfinedRunsAndTheTargetsOwnRunKeepTheirOwnServers` sees the target's own tool answer `{"status":"error"}`. The pre-fix effect on in-flight work comes from that test, which calls the listings directly, not from a background child running at the time.
- **Approach.** Neither the sandbox nor D20 is bypassed. A narrowed run lists and calls its session's MCP servers on a manager of its own narrowing (`Resolver.runMCPManager`).
  - The manager key is `<setting path>\x00<profile>\x00confined\x00<sha256 of the narrowed wrapper key>`. Its stdio servers start in the narrowed sandbox, as before the fix, and the profile's shared manager is no longer touched by such a run.
  - `targetRunner` records the scope (`profileDelegation.mcpScope`) only when the narrowing changes `mcpSandboxWrapper`. No caller sandbox, a caller sandbox that does not cover mcp over a target without one, the remote API's runs and users' runs keep the shared manager, unchanged.
  - Runs narrowed the same way share one manager. Different narrowings never restart each other's servers, so a listing keeps calling the server it was listed from, in its own sandbox.
  - An isolated (worktree) narrowed run lists on its narrowing's manager. That manager is routed (`SetRouteKey("")`, same as before the fix), so its calls still reach the servers started in its worktree (`TestConfinedDelegatedRunsMCPCallsStillReachItsWorktreeServer`).
  - Per-run managers of isolated runs (`runMCPLoader`) are unchanged.
- **Why not one manager per run.** A run's servers would have to stop when the run ends. Session-owned handles and background children of a non-isolated message run outlive it, and their MCP calls would fail (an isolated run cancels them at its worktree close; a non-isolated one does not). A manager per narrowing lives as long as the target session's shared manager does.
- **Tests (app).**
  - `TestConfinedProfileMessageRunLeavesTheTargetsSharedStdioServerAlone` replaces the T0 pin `TestConfinedProfileMessageRunRestartsTheTargetsSharedStdioServerInTheCallersSandbox` on purpose. Starts are 1 → 2 (one wrapped) → 2 after the next own run → 2 after a second message narrowed the same way.
  - `TestConfinedRunsAndTheTargetsOwnRunKeepTheirOwnServers` covers this sequence:
    - the target's own listing and two listings from different caller sandboxes are prepared;
    - every listing is called in turn, interleaved, and each is answered by its own start (`[a]`, `[b]` and untagged; 3 starts);
    - `releaseSessionChildren` removes both narrowing managers, and their listing no longer answers.
  - `TestProfileMessageRunGetsAnMCPScopeOnlyWhenTheNarrowingMovesItsServers` checks which runs get a scope of their own and which do not.
  - `TestConfinedDelegatedRunsMCPCallsStillReachItsWorktreeServer` covers the isolated narrowed run.
  - The test fixture gains `JAD_APP_STDIO_MCP_TAG`.
- **Verification.**
  - `mutate-check.sh`: 4 of 4 caught, each a test failure (not a build failure; a fifth attempt did not compile and is not counted). The mutations were: scope ignored in `runMCPManager`; scope not recorded; scope not passed to `prepareRun`; and a scope given to a target whose own mcp sandbox the narrowing left unchanged.
  - Full `app` package: ok.
  - `-race -count=2` on the confined, MCP-loader, delegated, toolset and sandbox-choice groups: ok.
  - No golden changed.
- **Open.**
  - **Sampler (T-008, separate).** A narrowing's manager takes the sampler of the last narrowed run that prepared on it. A narrowed message with a model choice no longer changes the target's shared sampler, but a message that is not narrowed still does (`TestProfileMessageModelChoiceStays...` unchanged). **Closed (2026-11-11, T-008):** no manager takes a sampler from a prepare any more.
  - **Lifetime and number** (closed 2026-11-11, see "MCP narrowing lifetime" below). A narrowing's manager and its server processes stay until the target session is deleted or the server stops, like the profile's shared manager. Each distinct narrowing (caller sandbox, caller places, sandbox choice, plan-mode form) adds one. A caller sandbox that is edited leaves the old narrowing's servers running until then. Closing them earlier would need a user count, or an idle close that does not break handles left running.
  - **Isolated narrowed runs** (closed as far as feasible 2026-11-11, see below). Listing the tools starts the narrowing's server in the session folder, under the caller's sandbox. The calls go to the worktree's servers, so that server only lists tools (before the fix the shared server was restarted for the same listing).
  - **Not covered by the narrowing (unchanged).** The MCP servers of the target's agent toolsets (`loadAgentToolsetMCP` reads `AgentToolsets`, which `withRunSandbox` does not narrow) and a remote target.
  - **Resource notes** (closed 2026-11-11, see below). A narrowed run's resource-change note still reads the shared manager (`resourceChangesNote`), so changes its own narrowing's servers report are not told.

## Unified agent runs MCP narrowing lifetime: a narrowing's servers live while its runs and their lineage's work go (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Scope keys, as found.** A narrowing's manager was keyed by `<setting path>\x00<profile>\x00confined\x00<sha256 of the narrowed wrapper key>`. The wrapper key is the JSON of the narrowed sandbox with the caller's places filled in, so a caller in a per-run worktree (an isolated sub-agent, an isolated message target) gives a new key per call. Each manager lived until the session was deleted or the server stopped, so their number had no bound.
- **Ownership (`internal/app/mcp_scope.go`).**
  - `Resolver.holdMCPScope` hands each narrowed run a hold (`mcpScopeHold`) of the manager of its scope, creating it when none is held; a count per manager lives under `Resolver.mu`. `boundRunner.runLocked` takes it before `prepareRun` and passes it down (`prepareRun`, `buildToolCatalog`, `buildRegisteredCatalog`, `runMCPManager` now take the hold, nil for the shared manager).
  - The release is deferred first, so it runs after the worktree close, the child sweep and `endRunStop`. A run that ends before it has a lineage key releases at once; otherwise `releaseMCPScopeAfter` records the hold under the run's lineage key and releases it once nothing under that key is live in any async or sub-agent manager of the resolver (`lineageLive`).
  - Only the run's own calls and live work under its key can call the run's tools, and only those can start more work under the key, so once nothing is live the release cannot come too early. A resumed child gets the catalog of the run that resumes it.
  - Notification, not polling: `asyncmgr.Manager.SetLineageEnd` (called outside every lock when a handle with a lineage completes, or its registration fails after the row was added) and `SubagentManager.SetRunEnd` (after `finish`, for a run with a lineage) call `Resolver.checkMCPDrains`, which costs one lock when nothing waits. New queries: `asyncmgr.Manager.HasLiveLineage`, `SubagentManager.HasLiveLineage`.
  - The last release closes the manager, synchronously at the run's end, in a goroutine when a handle's end triggers it. A session delete or shutdown still closes it while held; the later release finds another or no manager under the key and closes nothing.
- **Result.** At most one narrowing manager per scope, and only while a run of it or work under such a run's lineage is going. Runs narrowed alike at the same time share it. A later message narrowed alike starts its servers again (a stateful server loses its state between messages, as a per-run isolated server already does). Nothing that is still in use is stopped; work under an unrelated lineage does not keep a manager.
- **Resource notes.** `resourceChangesNote(scope)` reads the run's own manager (`runMCPManager`), so a narrowed run no longer takes the changes the target's shared servers reported for the target's next own run.
- **Isolated narrowed runs.** The scope gets a per-run suffix (`NewRunLineageKey("isolated_run")`), so the listing manager is the run's alone; once `StartMCP` started the worktree's servers, `mcp.Manager.StopStdioServers` stops its stdio servers (streamable HTTP connections stay, they are called). Every stdio call of the run is covered by the worktree route, so the stopped servers are never called. The listing start itself remains: avoiding it would mean opening the worktree and its servers before the catalog is built, a reorder of the run's setup.
- **Tests.**
  - app: `TestANarrowingsMCPServersStayWhileTheMessagesWorkGoesAndStopOnceItEnds` (a handle registered under the message run's lineage keeps the manager; an unrelated live handle does not; a second message shares it with no new start and its end does not close it; the handle's end closes it and the server process; no drain left pending). `TestANarrowedRunDoesNotTakeTheResourceChangesOfTheTargetsOwnServers` (new fixture option `JAD_APP_STDIO_MCP_TOUCH`). `TestConfinedDelegatedRunsMCPCallsStillReachItsWorktreeServer` now checks one server runs while the run goes and none after. `TestConfinedRunsAndTheTargetsOwnRunKeepTheirOwnServers` now releases holds one by one and checks the other servers keep answering. `TestConfinedProfileMessageRunLeavesTheTargetsSharedStdioServerAlone` now expects the second message to start its own server (starts 1 → 2 → 2 → 3) and no manager left. `TestProfileMessageRunGetsAnMCPScope...` checks equal scopes for runs narrowed alike and a scope of its own per isolated run.
  - asyncmgr: `TestLineageEndTellsEachEndOfAHandleUnderALineage`. native: `TestRunEndTellsTheEndOfARunUnderALineage`.
  - `mutate-check.sh`: 12 of 12 caught, each a test failure (logs read): release ignoring the drain; drain check a no-op; hold count ignored; Complete not telling; asyncmgr `HasLiveLineage` false (app and asyncmgr); sub-agent end not telling; sub-agent `HasLiveLineage` false; resource note on the shared manager; isolated stdio not stopped; isolated scope shared; lineage filter in `lineageEnded` dropped.
- **Open.**
  - **Sub-agent path at app level** (closed for background sub-agent handles 2026-11-11, see "MCP narrowing lifetime: background sub-agent at app level" below). `lineageLive`'s loop over sub-agent managers is covered by the native tests of `HasLiveLineage`/`SetRunEnd` only; no app test keeps a narrowing alive with a live unmanaged sub-agent run. Closing it needs an app fixture whose narrowed target starts a background child.
  - **Conservative holds.** Work a narrowed run started in another profile (a profile_message it sent) carries the run's key and keeps the manager until it ends, though it never calls these servers. Bounded by that work.
  - **Shutdown and lost handles.** Handles ended by `asyncmgr` Close or a peer-server check tell nothing; the resolver closes every manager at shutdown anyway, and foreign handles carry no lineage.
  - **Isolated listing start** remains (above). **Sampler** stays T-008 (closed 2026-11-11, T-008 section). **Agent toolset servers and remote targets** stay outside the narrowing, unchanged.

## Unified agent runs MCP narrowing lifetime: background sub-agent at app level (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Test** (`internal/app/mcp_scope_subagent_test.go`, tests only, no production change). A narrowed profile_message run of review/reviewer (caller sandbox covering mcp) starts a real background sub-agent (`finder`, `block_ms` 0, an async handle and a sub-agent run) and ends while the child holds in its first provider request.
  - `TestABackgroundSubagentOfANarrowedRunKeepsItsMCPServersUntilItEnds`: after the message ended, one narrowing manager and one pending drain remain; the child is then let go and its call of the m/stdio `lookup` tool is answered by the narrowing's server in the caller's sandbox (`[caller] MCP wrote`, one start, one wrapped); after the child ended the manager, its server process, the pending drain and the hold count are gone.
  - `TestABackgroundSubagentEndingWhileItsNarrowedRunEndsReleasesTheServersOnce`: the child is let go inside `Resolver.runnerReturned`, so its server call and its end race the run's own drain look; same assertions on the answer and the cleanup.
  - Both check, at `runnerReturned` (after the runner returned, before the drain), that `lineageLive` already sees the child under the run's key.
- **No false release during child creation (proof, checked in code).** The drain look (`releaseMCPScopeAfter`) runs only after the run's runner returned. A sub-agent is started inside a tool call of the run, and both records are made before that call returns: the handle row, with the caller's lineage, in `subagentAsyncHandle.begin` -> `asyncmgr.Register`; the run, in `m.runs` under `m.mu`, in `SubagentManager.start`. Between the two, the handle row is live. A nested start from a run with a chain depth fails fast instead of queueing. So the child is live under the key before the look. The same holds for work the child starts: it is started inside the child's tool call, while the child is still active. A run's state turns terminal only in `finish`, after its launcher returned. The handle row turns terminal after that, in `async.end`. The new runnerReturned check pins the first step at app level.
- **Mutations.**
  - `lineageLive` ignored in the drain: caught by both tests (no manager after the message; the child's server call fails with `{"status":"error"}` in the race test).
  - Both end callbacks removed: caught (manager never closes).
  - Both `HasLiveLineage` false: caught (child not live at runnerReturned).
  - Each single end callback, or each single `HasLiveLineage`, is not caught on its own. A handle child is both an async row and a sub-agent run, and the run turns terminal before its handle ends, so either side alone still holds and drains. The native and asyncmgr unit tests still cover each side alone.
- **Race.** `-race -count=10` on these two tests plus the narrowing lifetime, confined and scope-rule tests: pass, no data race.
- **Open.**
  - A sub-agent run that is live with no handle after its narrowed parent ended keeps the manager through the sub-agent side of `lineageLive` alone. This can happen when the parent's blocking call returned on a cancel while the child, a top-level run of the target's manager, still ends. No app test covers it: it would need a child that keeps calling MCP after its stop, which the fixture cannot drive deterministically.
  - Full `verify-go.sh` was not rerun for this tests-only change, as Master allowed. The app package's focused groups and `go vet ./internal/app/` were run.

## MCP sampling belongs to the run whose call the server serves (T-008) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Bug, confirmed again before the fix.** `buildRegisteredCatalog` set `SetSampler(mcpSampler(config))` on the MCP manager shared by every run, tool listing and remote start of one session file and profile; the sampling handler read the manager's sampler when the request came. With the old code restored (mutate-check), a run with `openai/small` held after it listed its tools was answered by `model-large` after a `GET .../tools` and a remote `StartSubagent` (both the default model), and a profile_message's background child (`openai/small`) was answered by `model-large` after the target's next own run.
- **Fix.**
  - A connection runs one tool call at a time (`callMu`), and the call is already carried to the client handlers (`activeCall`, used by elicitation). `activeCall` now also holds the sampler of the listing the tool came from, and `Manager.sample` prefers it over the manager's.
  - New `mcp.Manager.LoadToolsSampled(ctx, servers, cwd, sampler)`; `LoadTools` is it with nil (the manager's sampler, as before), so its callers and tests are unchanged.
  - `buildRegisteredCatalog` lists with `LoadToolsSampled(..., r.mcpSampler(config))` and no longer calls `SetSampler`: the shared and the narrowing managers never get a sampler. A run's tools, the catalogs of its children (built from that run's catalog, `bindMCP`), its scripts and its background children therefore sample with that run's config (model, credential), however long they outlive it and whatever runs or listings come later.
  - Unchanged: the per-run managers of isolated runs (`runMCPLoader`) keep `SetSampler` with their run's config (one run owns each), and their toolset-key managers have none; the agent toolset managers (`loadAgentToolsetMCP`) have none, so a toolset server's sampling stays refused (`TestAgentToolsetMCPServersHaveNoSampler` passes unchanged). The request budget stays per connection, shared by every listing (tested). Confinement, narrowing holds and cleanup are untouched (no new manager, no new key).
- **Why not a sampler per run on the manager, or a context value.** A per-run map on the manager needs a key the server's request does not carry; a context value does not reach the handler, because a call runs on the connection's context (`callTool` derives `callCtx` from `c.ctx`). The connection's single active call is the one reliable link from a server request to the run.
- **Behaviour change.** A sampling request on a shared or narrowing manager outside one of the server's tool calls (during a resource read or prompt get, which do not set the active call, or between calls) has no run and is refused (`this client cannot sample right now`); before, the last listing's model answered. An isolated run's own servers still answer with their run's model. By code reading only: no fixture samples outside a tool call. Schema text of `sampling` (`sample/schemes/mcp-server.schema.json`) updated.
- **Tests.**
  - mcp: `TestSamplingIsAnsweredByTheSamplerOfTheCallsListing` (a call whose sampling is in flight keeps its listing's model while another listing and `SetSampler` happen; later calls of each listing and a `LoadTools` listing; no manager sampler refuses); `TestConcurrentCallsOfDifferentListingsSampleWithTheirOwnModels` (3 listings x 8 concurrent calls on one connection); `TestSamplingBudgetIsPerConnectionAcrossListings`.
  - app (`mcp_sampling_run_test.go`): `TestMCPSamplingOfARunIsNotTakenOverByAListingOrARemoteStart` (also: the remote child samples with its own default model; the shared manager has no sampler afterwards) and `TestProfileMessageModelChoiceSamplesOnlyForItsOwnRunAndItsChildren`, which replaces the pin `TestProfileMessageModelChoiceStaysTheSamplerOfTheTargetsSharedServersUntilItsNextRun`.
  - `mutate-check.sh`: 4 of 4 caught, each a real test failure read in the log: old `SetSampler` + `LoadTools` restored in `buildRegisteredCatalog` (both app tests); listing sampler dropped from `activeCall`; manager sampler preferred over the call's; call sampler ignored.
- **Race.** `-race -count=3`: mcp sampling and client-feature tests; app sampling, toolset sampler, narrowing, confined, MCP loader and background-child groups. No data race.
- **Open.**
  - Sampling during a feature tool (resource read, prompt) or between calls is refused on shared managers (above); answering it would need those calls to carry the run, which they cannot without serialising them with tool calls. Not observed in any fixture. **Corrected (2026-11-11, next section):** that reason was wrong: feature requests already run under `callMu`. A run's resource and prompt tools now carry their run; between calls stays refused, now tested.
  - MCP prompt requests (`promptSessionConfig`) use the shared manager and have no run, so a server sampling during a prompt request is refused. (Still so; the next section tests it for the user's resource read.)
  - A per-run isolated manager's sampler is still set on the manager; it is owned by one run, so no other run can change it.

## MCP sampling attribution: outside-call refusal, feature tools and the protocol limit (T-008 follow-up) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Traced attribution.**
  - Requests sent on a connection: `callTool` and `connection.request` (resource and prompt tools, the user's resource and prompt requests, subscribe/unsubscribe, resubscribe, log level) all take `callMu`, so they run one at a time. Only `listTools` (and the initialize handshake) runs beside them.
  - **Protocol 2026-07-28 (what the SDK client offers and SDK servers answer):** sampling and elicitation come as input requests in the result of a `tools/call`, `resources/read` or `prompts/get` (multi round-trip). The client middleware fulfils them inside that request, under `callMu`, so the connection's call is exactly the one asking. The SDK's server refuses to send `sampling/createMessage` on its own on this protocol (`assertServerInitiatedRequestAllowed`).
  - **Older protocols:** the server sends `sampling/createMessage` on its own. Nothing names our request: JSON-RPC over stdio has no such field, and over HTTP the SDK v1.8.0 client reads POST streams and the standalone stream into one channel and gives handlers only `Session` and `Params`.
  - **Closed by the security follow-up below (2026-11-11): such requests are now refused.** Earlier text: **So, the limit (pinned, not fixed):** an older-protocol server's request that it sends unprompted, or during a `tools/list` beside a call, while an unrelated call is in progress is answered for that call's run (`TestLegacySamplingSentOnItsOwnDuringAnUnrelatedCallGoesToThatCall`). What would close it: an SDK and protocol that link server requests to client requests (the 2026-07-28 input requests do), or refusing older-protocol standalone sampling altogether, which would end sampling for those servers. Not decided here. The misattribution stays within one manager (one profile, one narrowing, or one isolated run) and one server, inside its budget, opt-in per server file.
  - A context value carrying the call into the request's context would add nothing: under `callMu` it always equals the connection's call (tried; mutations removing it were not caught, so it was dropped).
- **Fix: resource and prompt tools carry their run.** `featureTools` gets the listing's sampler and wraps each call in an `activeCall` like a tool call; `connection.request` sets the connection's call from its context for the request's length. A run's `resources/read`, `prompts/get`, list and subscribe tools therefore sample with the run's model (before: refused). Elicitation during them now asks the run's user (before: cancelled). Requests with no run (the user's own resource and prompt requests, a resubscribe or log level outside a call) leave no call, so sampling is refused and elicitation cancels, as before.
- **Clear errors, no budget used.** `errSamplingWithoutCall` ("this client cannot sample right now: it samples only for a run's tool, resource or prompt call in progress on this connection, and none is") and `errSamplingWithoutModel` ("... the call in progress has no model to sample with", e.g. agent toolset servers). The old prefix is kept. Text-content validation now runs before the budget is counted, so no refusal uses `max_requests`. Schema descriptions of `sampling` and `elicitation` (`sample/schemes/mcp-server.schema.json`) and code comments updated.
- **Tests.**
  - mcp (`sampling_owner_test.go`): a hand-written stdio fixture on protocol 2025-06-18 that sends `sampling/createMessage` on its own (during a call, during a resource read, or later on a file trigger).
    - `TestLegacySamplingIsAnsweredForTheRunsCallAndResourceReadOnly`: a run's call and a run's resource read are answered by the run's model. The user's `ReadUserResource` is refused with `errSamplingWithoutCall`, and a `LoadTools` listing with no model with `errSamplingWithoutModel`.
    - `TestLegacySamplingOutsideACallIsRefusedWithoutUsingTheBudget`: with `max_requests` 1, two requests after the call ended are refused with the clear error, then the run's next call still samples, and the one after is over budget.
    - `TestLegacySamplingSentOnItsOwnDuringAnUnrelatedCallGoesToThatCall`: the limit above.
    - `TestSampleRefusalsLeaveTheBudget`: unit test of the refusal paths and the call/manager sampler order.
  - app: `TestMCPResourceReadSamplesForTheRunThatReadsAndNotForTheUser`. A run with `openai/small` reads `doc://ask` (the fixture's new 2026-07-28 input-request resource) through its resource tool, answered by model-small. The user's `ReadMCPResource` is refused; control: with a sampler set on the shared manager the same read is answered.
  - `mutate-check.sh`, each a real test failure in the log: the feature-tool `activeCall` removed (caught in app and mcp); the `request` call set removed; the two errors merged; the budget counted before the content check; counted before the sampler check; the sampler not passed to `featureTools`. 7 caught. One mutation (count twice with a shifted limit) was equivalent and is not counted.
- **Race.** `-race -count=3` on mcp sampling, client-feature, elicitation, resource and prompt tests, and app sampling, MCP-resource, toolset sampler, narrowing and confined groups. No data race.
- **Open.**
  - The older-protocol limit above.
  - The `prompts/get` tool is not tested on its own; it goes through the same `featureTools` wrapper and `connection.request` as `resources/read`.
  - Elicitation during a run's resource or prompt tool is not tested; same code path as sampling.
  - The user's MCP prompt requests (`GetUserPrompt`) have no run, so sampling during them is refused (by code; the user's resource read is tested).

## MCP sampling fails closed when it cannot be attributed to a request of the client (T-008 security follow-up) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Decision:** a server's `sampling/createMessage` is answered only when it provably belongs to a request the client sent. Otherwise it is refused (`errSamplingUnattributed`) before any model, the manager's sampler or the per-connection budget is touched, whatever call is in progress. This replaces the earlier rule of giving it to the connection's call in progress (`owningCall`), which let an older-protocol server's unprompted request use an unrelated run's model and credential.
- **Signal (SDK v1.8.0, verified in its source):** `connection.callTool` and `connection.request` put an `inlineRequest` mark (the run's call, or none for the user's own requests) on the context of the request they send. The SDK's client multi-round-trip middleware fulfils a result's input requests (`fulfillInputRequests` → `client.createMessage` → `CreateMessageHandler`) with that same context. A request the server sends on its own is dispatched by `internal/jsonrpc2` with the connection's context (the connect context in `notDone`), which never carries the mark; over stdio and streamable HTTP alike. A context value is not something a server can set, so the mark is trustworthy. If a later SDK fulfilled input requests with another context, attributed sampling would be refused (fail closed) and the attributed tests below would fail.
- **Precedence among attributed requests is unchanged:** the call's listing sampler, else the manager's (an isolated run's own servers), else refused (no run made the request: `errSamplingWithoutCall`; a call with no model, an agent toolset server: `errSamplingWithoutModel`). All refusals reach no model and use no budget.
- **Compatibility:** servers on protocols before 2026-07-28 (and any server sending `sampling/createMessage` on its own) get no sampling from this client at all, also during the run's own call and on an isolated run's own servers. Documented in `sample/schemes/mcp-server.schema.json` (`sampling`) and the code comments (`attributedCall`, `sample`, `SetSampler`, `callTool`, `connection.request`).
- **Tests:** `TestLegacySamplingSentOnItsOwnDuringAnUnrelatedCallIsRefused` (replaces the pin `...GoesToThatCall`; counting samplers on both runs and the manager answer 0 times, budget unused with `max_requests` 1), `TestLegacySamplingIsRefusedEvenDuringTheRunsOwnCallAndResourceRead`, `TestLegacySamplingOutsideACallIsRefusedWithoutUsingTheBudget`, `TestSampleRefusalsLeaveTheBudget` (unit: unattributed with a call set and a manager sampler; no run; no model; image; call model; manager fallback). Attributed (2026-07-28 input requests) still answered: mcp `TestSamplingIsAnsweredByTheSamplerOfTheCallsListing`, `TestConcurrentCallsOfDifferentListingsSampleWithTheirOwnModels`, `TestSamplingBudgetIsPerConnectionAcrossListings`, `TestMCPClientOffersRootsSamplingElicitationAndLogs`, and the app sampling and resource-read tests. `mutate-check.sh`: 5/5 caught with real test failures (refusal disabled; mark always present; `owningCall` used instead of the mark; mark removed in `callTool`; mark removed in `connection.request`, caught by the app resource-read test).
- **Open:**
  - ~~**Elicitation** still uses the call in progress ...~~ **Closed** by "MCP elicitation fails closed when it cannot be attributed" below.
  - **No opt-in** to keep older-protocol sampling for single-run managers (isolated runs): deliberately not added (fail closed, no new setting); would need a decision and a schema key.
  - **`prompts/get` input-request sampling** is covered only through the shared `connection.request` path (the resource-read tests), not by its own test.

## MCP elicitation fails closed when it cannot be attributed to a request of the client (T-008 follow-up) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Confirmed first.** The legacy fixture (`sampling_owner_test.go`, protocol 2025-06-18) now also sends `elicitation/create` on its own (`kind: "elicit"`, `doc://elicit`). On the old code, a question it sent while an unrelated run's `hold` call was in progress was shown to that run's user, who accepted it (`elicited accept {"color":"red"}`).
- **Fix.** `elicit` uses the same signal as sampling: it answers only when `attributedCall(ctx)` finds the mark that `callTool` and `connection.request` put on their own request context, which the SDK v1.8.0 passes to the input requests of that request's result (`mrtr.go fulfillInputRequests`; the URL-elicitation-required retry also uses the request's context). A request the server sends on its own reaches the handler with the connection's context, so it is refused with `errElicitationUnattributed` ("this client cannot show this question: ... an elicitation/create the server sends on its own names no request of the client, so it is refused") as a JSON-RPC error, whatever call is in progress, and no user sees it. Attributed behaviour is unchanged: the run's user of that request is asked with the same draft, timeout and draft limits; an attributed request no run made (the user's own resource or prompt request) still cancels; URL mode still declines.
- **Dead state removed.** Nothing read the connection's call in progress any more, so `clientState.call`, `setCall`, `currentCall` and `owningCall` are gone; `callMu` still runs a connection's calls one at a time. Test assertions that only checked that state was cleared were removed.
- **Compatibility.** Servers on protocols before 2026-07-28 get no elicitation (as for sampling since the security follow-up): their questions get the error instead of reaching a user. Documented in the `elicitation` description of `sample/schemes/mcp-server.schema.json` and the code comments.
- **Tests (mcp):** `TestLegacyElicitationSentOnItsOwnDuringAnUnrelatedCallIsRefused` (counting askers on both runs: 0), `TestLegacyElicitationIsRefusedEvenDuringTheRunsOwnCallAndResourceRead` (own call, own resource read, the user's read, after the call), `TestElicitAsksOnlyForAnAttributedCall` (unit), `TestElicitationInAResourceReadAsksTheRunsUserOnly` (2026-07-28 resource read asks the reading call's user once, with its call ID; the user's read cancels; new `doc://elicit` resource on the probe fixture), `TestConcurrentCallsAskTheirOwnUsers` (8 concurrent calls, each asked once with its own call ID); `TestMCPClientOffersRootsSamplingElicitationAndLogs` still passes. `mutate-check.sh`: 5/5 caught with real test failures (the refusal removed; unattributed accepted; mark dropped in `connection.request`; mark dropped in `callTool`; handler given a context with no call). Two first attempts of the mark mutations did not compile and were redone.
- **Checks.** Full mcp tests pass; `-race -count=3` on the mcp elicitation, legacy, client-feature, sampling, concurrent, resource and prompt tests; `verify-go.sh` exit 0 (gofmt, vet, test, diff check).
- **Open:**
  - **`prompts/get` elicitation** is covered only through the shared `connection.request` path (the resource-read test), not by its own test.
  - **No opt-in** for older-protocol elicitation (or sampling) on single-run managers; deliberately not added (fail closed).
  - **App level:** no app test drives an elicitation; app code passes `RequestInteraction` unchanged and was not modified.

## Unified agent runs R4a: catalog assembly split from acquisition (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Done.** `buildRegisteredCatalog` is now `acquireCatalogParts` then `assembleRegisteredCatalog` (`internal/app/catalog_assembly.go`).
  - **Acquisition** (resolver method) holds every side effect of a catalog build, in the old order: the shared task and records stores, the native catalog (subagent manager, async host registration), the profile's MCP manager (shared, or the narrowing's) with wrapper and route key set and servers started and listed with the build's sampler, then each agent toolset's manager and servers. It returns `catalogParts`.
  - **Assembly** (plain function, no resolver) joins the parts: lazy bind, the parent's gated and hooked MCP copy, the child `load_tool`, `SetLazy`, `SetRunMCP`, `BindToolsets`, `Redescribe`, merge, hook-match check (warn passed in; the resolver's logger stays in `buildRegisteredCatalog`). It starts no server, sets nothing on a manager, opens no store; it changes only the build's own lazy set and subagent binding, never the listed tools.
  - `ListTools`, `buildToolCatalog`/`prepareRun` and remote `StartSubagent` still call `buildRegisteredCatalog`, unchanged. The two configs of T0 (run config, toolset config) are untouched: assembly takes the profile config as before; toolset tools arrive as acquired `ToolsetMCP` with their own hooks.
- **Behaviour.** Same calls with the same arguments. Observed: the registered, exposed and hidden listing of a fixture with lazy MCP, `load_tool`, hooks, a toolset agent with its own server and an allow-list agent was byte-identical before and after (temporary dump, not kept). One order changed: the parent's MCP catalog is now built after the toolsets' servers are loaded, not before. It differs only if `tools.NewCatalog` refused the MCP listing (missing id, name, validator or executor, or a duplicate name), which an MCP manager listing does not produce; then the toolset servers would already have started.
- **Tests (app, `catalog_assembly_test.go`).**
  - `TestCatalogAssemblyStartsNothingAndLeavesItsAcquiredPartsAlone`:
    - after acquisition, assembly calls no tool (counting wrappers on the owner's and the toolset's tools), starts no server (start log stays at 2), leaves the resolver's MCP manager keys and the listed definitions unchanged, and warns nothing;
    - its listing equals the whole build's, and the whole build over the warm managers starts nothing;
    - the parent's lazy MCP tool is gated (`lazy_tool_not_loaded`, 0 calls);
    - the agent list is redescribed after binding (an MCP-only agent is marked as changing files).
  - `TestCatalogAssemblyChecksTheHooksMatches`: a hook on a disabled server warns through the passed callback; a hook on no registered tool refuses.
  - The source-order pin `TestResolverGivesTheSubagentItsLazySetBeforeItBindsMCPTools` now reads `catalog_assembly.go`.
  - `mutate-check.sh` 7/7 caught with real test failures: lazy bind dropped, gating dropped, `Redescribe` dropped, warn not passed, a listed definition changed in assembly, `SetRunMCP` dropped (caught by `TestIsolatedSubagentCallsItsMCPToolOnAServerInItsWorktree`), parent hooks dropped (caught by `TestRefusedLazyMCPCallFiresItsHookOnce`). A first batch reported all "not caught" because the wrapper's pipe hid the exit code; rerun with `pipefail`.
- **Checks.** Full `internal/app` tests pass; `-race -count=3` on the assembly, lazy MCP, sampling, model-choice, confined, isolated sub-agent MCP, toolset, child-hook, refused-lazy-hook and run-MCP-loader tests: no data races; `verify-go.sh` exit 0 (gofmt, vet, tests, diff check).
- **Open (next increments, not done here):**
  - **Children are not assembled by this function.** Each agent's catalog is still built inside the native subagent tool (`bindMCP`, `GateFor`, `buildAllCatalogs`) from the raw MCP tools. Making a child build use the same assembly needs a native API that builds one agent's catalog from parts (its config, the owner's lazy set and load_tool, its MCP copy and hooks); that is R4b. (R4b, below: the MCP copies are now shared; the composition of a child catalog stays in native, with the blocker recorded there.)
  - **Parts are single-use.** The lazy set and the subagent binding are per build and assembly binds into them; assembling the same parts twice is not supported, and parts are not shared between runs.
  - **Child catalogs not compared directly.** The agent list output does not name each agent's tools, so the before/after comparison covers the owner's catalog; child catalogs rest on existing behavioural tests (lazy child gating, toolset hooks, isolated sub-agent MCP), which pass.
  - **No benchmark.** Assembly does the same calls once each as before; nothing was added to the build path.

## Unified agent runs R4b (partial): one MCP copy per build, shared by the owner and its children (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Status: partial, not complete.** Only the MCP copies are shared. The composition of child catalogs is still separate from the owner's (see "Not unified" below); R4b stays open until one shared assembly builds both (R3a section below). (Since "R4b remainder" below: one assembly step builds the owner's and every child's catalogs from the same parts, each once; the two compositions stay apart, with the evidence there.)

- **Done.** A catalog build now gates and hooks each listed MCP tool once, and the owner's catalog and every child catalog of that build hold that one copy.
  - `native.NewMCPCopies(session, toolsets, lazy, hooks, apiKeyEnv)` (`internal/tools/native/subagent.go`) builds `MCPCopies`: each session tool gated with the owner's lazy set (`LazySet.GateFor`) and hooked with the profile's hooks, each toolset tool (by `ToolsetMCPKey`) gated with the same set and hooked with its toolset's hooks. It starts nothing and changes neither the set nor the listed tools.
  - `assembleRegisteredCatalog` builds the owner's MCP catalog from `copies.Session()` and binds the same copies into the subagent tool (`SubagentMCP.BindCopies`). `bindMCP` now only selects the copies an agent's filter shows; it no longer gates or hooks. Before, the owner gated with the one-shot `Gate` and hooked its copy, and `bindMCP` gated (`GateFor`) and hooked a new copy per agent; agents of one toolset each got their own copy.
  - `BindToolsets(raw, toolsets)` stays for callers with raw tools (native tests): it builds the copies from the set `SetLazy` gave (read under the tool's lock) and calls `BindCopies`.
  - Removed: `native.GateLazyTools` (its only caller was assembly), `SubagentMCP.hookWith` (only `hookTool` is left, for the nested subagent copy), and the source-order pin `TestResolverGivesTheSubagentItsLazySetBeforeItBindsMCPTools`. The copies are gated before they are bound, so the order of `SetLazy` and the binding no longer decides whether a child copy is gated; `TestMCPCopiesGateAChildWhateverTheBindOrder` checks the reversed order, and the behavioural `TestLazyMCPProfileGivesTheChildItsLazySetBeforeBindingMCP` stays.
- **Gate.** The copies use `GateFor`, never the one-shot `Gate`. With `Gate`, the toolset's copy of an ID the owner already gated would come back ungated (the same-ID case of `TestToolsetChildKeepsItsOwnCopyOfALazyOwnerServer` and `TestToolsetChildOfALazyOwnerServerKeepsItsOwnCopyAndHooks`), and a second build from one set would gate nothing. `Gate` keeps its one-shot contract for the owner's extension tools (`gateLazy` in `buildNativeTools`), whose copies children already shared through `childNativePool`. `Gate` returned `GateFor` of the same tool, so the owner's copy is the same wrapper as before.
- **Unchanged.** The definitions and order of every catalog, hook owners (owner hooks on a session copy, toolset hooks on a toolset copy, hooks around the gate), lazy refusals, `load_tool`, the agent flags (`mcpBound`, background, `NoChangeTools`), the per-agent choice/depth catalog cache, toolset keys, sampling (the sampler travels in the listed tool, T-008), MCP scoping and the two T0 configs. Golden parity: these passed before the change and pass after it, with no golden file rewritten: `TestChildCatalogsAreUnchanged` (`child_catalogs.txt`: 6 agents × 5 choices × 2 depths, definitions and fingerprints), `TestChildCatalogHookOwnersAreKept`, the app `TestRunBaseline*` goldens, the mixed-chain and profile sandbox-choice goldens, and the lazy, toolset, deny and profile-tools groups.
- **Tests (native, `subagent_mcp_copies_test.go`).**
  - `TestMCPCopiesAreSharedByTheOwnerAndEveryChild`: the session children hold the owner's copy (same executor closure); two agents of one toolset share the toolset's copy, which is apart from the owner's copy of the same ID; in each agent's own, deepest-level and sandbox-choice catalog the lazy tool is refused; the hooks fire once per refused call (owner 6, toolset 6) and no server runs; a `load_tool` run reaches the toolset's connection once.
  - `TestMCPCopiesGateAChildWhateverTheBindOrder` and `TestNewMCPCopiesLeavesTheOneShotGateToTheOwner` (two builds from one set are both gated; the set's `Gate` still gates once, then refuses; without a set or hooks the copy is the listed tool).
  - `mutate-check.sh` 6 of 7 caught, each a real test failure: re-hooking in `bindMCP`, `Gate` instead of `GateFor`, no hooks in the copies, `BindToolsets` without the set, building the copies before `lazy.Bind` in assembly, the owner catalog from the raw tools. Not caught: assembly calling `BindToolsets(raw)` instead of `BindCopies(copies)`. That fallback behaves identically and only builds a second copy per agent; the identity is checked in native only, because `tools.Catalog` exposes no tool to the app package.
- **Checks.** Full `internal/tools/native` and `internal/app` tests pass. `-race` passed on the copies, child-catalog, toolset, `SetLazy`, sandbox-choice-cache, deny-ceiling and nested-hook native tests (×3), and on the app assembly, lazy child, toolset, sampling, narrowed background-child, run-baseline, toolset-MCP, parity and profile-deny tests (×2), with no data races. `verify-go.sh` exit 0 (gofmt, vet, tests with 45 packages ok, diff check).
- **Cost.** `TestReportRegisteredCatalogBuildCost` (env-gated, asserts nothing) over warm managers: 11,474 → 11,454 allocations per build, about 2.9 ms either way. `BenchmarkSubagentToolPrepare`: 2,113 → 2,093 allocs/op, ~330 µs either way. The gain is small for these fixtures; it grows with the number of agents × MCP tools (one gate and one hook wrapper per tool instead of per agent).
- **Not unified, and why (blocker, evidence in code).** The composition of a child catalog stays in the native subagent tool. Moving it to the owner's assembly would change behaviour:
  - The owner's registered catalog is narrowed per run (`applyProfileTools` in `buildToolCatalog`, plan mode, `Only`, `WithoutDenied`), while a child's is narrowed by its agent filter when it is built. The owner's allow list does not narrow children (`TestProfileToolsHideAToolFromTheParentButNotFromAChild`), but its deny does.
  - The owner refuses an unknown tool entry (`checkProfileToolEntries`). A child drops an explicit entry the deny covers (`TestSubagentToolsetIsStillSubjectToProfileDeny`) and checks MCP entries against its pool (`checkMCPEntries`).
  - Child catalogs are built per sandbox choice and depth class on demand, under the subagent tool's lock (`childCatalogSet`), with description variants (`describeAgentSandbox`) and the owner's hooked subagent copy (`nestedSelf`).
  - A toolset child's native tools come from the toolset's derived config (T0: it cannot be the run config).

  Both are "native list, then MCP copies" (`MergeCatalogs` vs `childCatalogTools`), so one composition function over them now would be a nominal wrapper.
- **Proposal (R6).** One composition `catalogFor(template, filter)` over the shared parts (native instances, `MCPCopies`, the owner's `load_tool` and nested subagent), used by the owner (filter = its profile tools, strict entries) and by each child (filter = agent filter). U3 is decided (the deny ceiling is inherited, the allow list is not), and the composition must keep the current strictness: the owner refuses an unknown entry, a child drops an entry its deny covers. It still needs a template config for toolset agents, which R3a found cannot be one config (next section).
- **Open.**
  - (Closed for the resolver's builds by "R4b remainder" below: they build each once.) The subagent tool still builds each agent's catalogs three times per prepare: at construction, again when `SetLazy` gives a `load_tool`, and again in `BindCopies`. With the copies gated up front the order is free, so the `SetLazy` rebuild could be dropped for the assembly path. This is not done here: `TestSetLazyWithoutALoadToolKeepsTheCatalogsTheFirstOneBuilt` and `TestSetLazyTwiceLeavesOneLoadTool` pin the rebuild rule, and the measured cost is small.
  - `SubagentMCP.Bind` has no caller left (it was already unused before R4b); it is kept.
  - `docs/design_unified_agent_runs.md` still names `hookWith` among the current hooks (sections 2 and 3.6); the design text was not updated.

## Unified agent runs R3a: not implemented; an agent's run and tools need two configs (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Corrected by the R3a follow-up below.** The prepare-time finishing steps and the launcher share one input, the owner run's config; only a sub-agent call's own `model` argument is later. The two prepare-time steps are now one derivation.

- **Outcome.** No production change. A shared template config, either a caller-facts overlay on the toolset config or the toolset layered on the run config, would change observable behaviour, and a function that only returned today's two configs would be the nominal wrapper the task excludes. R4b stays partial (section above).
- **Evidence: `TestAgentConfigFieldsAreClassifiedForTheRunAndTheTools` (`internal/app/agent_config_fields_test.go`).** It classifies all 77 `SessionConfig` fields and fails on a field added to or removed from the struct. Its fixture: a toolset agent with its own model, a caller that selected `openai/cheap@high`, and a profile toolset with a hook and a state context.
  - **Layer (43):** root, session and caller-profile settings. They are equal in the caller's config, the run config (`childConfig`) and the tools config (`AgentToolsets[key]`, plus the model `buildAgentToolsets` gives it).
  - **Caller only (11):** profile identity, the model selection, warnings. The run keeps the caller's values; the agent's tools do not read them.
  - **Tool surface (19):** native and extension tool settings, MCP servers, `AgentToolsets`. The child's catalog is built from the tools config at the owner's prepare; the run carries the caller's value and does not read it. A toolset child takes the owner's `profile_message` tool.
  - **Conflict (4): read by both sides with different values.**
    - `Hooks`: the run fires the caller's `subagent_stop`; the tools are hooked with the toolset's `pre_tool`/`post_tool`.
    - `NativeSubagent`: the run needs the caller's section for the transcript folder; the toolset has none.
    - `StateContext`: the run gives the caller's block; compose deletes it for a toolset because its providers read the session's tools. Keeping it fails the load ("statecontext provider async … requires tools.native.async").
    - `Model`: the run uses the agent's own model (`AGENT_KEY`); the tools hide the caller's model key (`CALLER_KEY`).
  - `mutate-check.sh`: 4 of 5 caught, each a real test failure (a field left unclassified; the statecontext deletion removed; `childConfig` taking the toolset's hooks; `childConfig` ignoring the agent's model). Not caught: removing `derived.NativeSubagent = nil` from `loadAgentToolsets`. The fixture's subagent section is in the profile toolset, which the agent's toolset replaces, so the section is already absent; the drop matters only when the section is in the session or profile settings.
- **Why the consolidation sites cannot merge now.** The tools config is finished in three places with inputs from different stages:
  - `loadAgentToolsets`, at load: drops the subagent section, copies `ReadOnlyPaths`, applies the plan sandbox.
  - `buildAgentToolsets`, at the owner's prepare, per toolset key: sets the caller's model, drops async without a host.
  - `toolsetMCPUses`, at the owner's prepare, per `ToolsetMCPKey`: puts the agent's sandbox in when it covers mcp.

  The run config is built per run (`childConfig`, with the caller's per-run selection, such as a `profile_message` model choice). A template built once would not see the per-run selection, and one built per run would not be where the tools are built.
- **Behaviour kept.** No change to `childConfig`, `loadAgentToolsets`, the catalogs, fingerprints or goldens. T0 tests #384/#385, `child_config_test.go` and the R0 goldens are unchanged.
- **Proposal (closes R3a and R4b together).** Introduce `AgentTemplate{Agent, Run, Tools}` when children build their catalogs per run from shared parts (the R6 composition in the R4b section). At that point the tools config is consumed per run, so the three finishing steps move into one constructor beside `childConfig`. The two configs stay separate fields, so the four conflict fields keep their current sources; the classification test is the guard. *Superseded (2026-11-11): see "Unified agent runs: completion assessment and accepted departures (T-007)".*
- **Observation, not filed as a bug.** A child with its own model runs tools that hide the caller's model key env, not its own (conflict `Model`). The shells pass only allow-listed variables and configured `env`, so this is exposed only when `env` names that key; it is unchanged. (Closed by T-009 for native child processes.)
- **Checks.** The new test passes on its own and in the full `internal/app` package. `-race -count=2` passed on it with the T0 and `childConfig` tests, with no data races. `verify-go.sh` exit 0 (gofmt, vet, tests with 45 packages ok, diff check).

## Unified agent runs R3a follow-up: the tool side of an owner run's agents is one derivation (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Review claim, checked against the code: correct for the tool side.** At the owner's prepare, `acquireCatalogParts` passes one config to `subagentLauncherFor` (the launcher's `parent`), to `BuildCatalogWithAsync` (→ `buildAgentToolsets`, which gave each toolset `config.Model`), and to `loadAgentToolsetMCP` (→ `toolsetMCPUses`). `bound_runner` hands the same `r.config` to `runMCPLoader`. A profile_message model choice is already in that config, so the R3a claim that a template "would not see the per-run selection" was wrong: prepare is per owner run. Nested children call the owner's subagent tool (their catalog is built from it), so every descendant's run base is the owner's config too.
- **Changed.** `native.NewAgentToolConfigs(owner)` (`tools/native/agent_tool_configs.go`) is now the one derivation of the tool side: `Native` by toolset key (loaded toolset + owner model; async dropped when the owner has no `tools.native.async`, which is exactly when there is no async host, since opening one either succeeds or fails the catalog) and `MCP` views by `ToolsetMCPKey` (that same config, in the agent's sandbox when it covers mcp). `buildAgentToolsets`, `loadAgentToolsetMCP` and `runMCPLoader` consume it; `toolsetMCPUse`/`toolsetMCPUses` are removed. `runMCPLoader` derives once per loader instead of on every request.
- **Value differences, and why they are not observable.** An MCP view now carries the owner's `Model` and, without the owner's async section, no `NativeAsync`. The toolset MCP path reads only `Sandbox`, `WorkingDir`, `MCPServers`, `Hooks` (`mcpSandboxWrapper`, `runServerSandbox`, `LoadTools`/`LoadStdioTools`, `ToolsetMCP.Hooks`); toolset servers still get no sampler (`LoadTools` / `request.Key != ""`), so T-008 is unchanged. No golden was edited or rewritten; `child_catalogs.txt`, the run-baseline and admission goldens and the R3a field classification pass unchanged.
- **Not moved into a template, with evidence.**
  - **Run config.** `childConfig` stays at child start: the call may name a model (`withCallModel`, `subagent_model.go`, sets `ModelPath`/`ReasoningEffort` per call), and `WithModel` reads the agent's model file, whose errors today surface as that call's failure, not the owner's prepare. A `Run` field holding only the owner config would duplicate the launcher's `parent`.
  - **Load-time step.** `loadAgentToolsets` (compose, checks, `ReadOnlyPaths`, plan sandbox) stays at load, keeping error timing.
  - **Once per prepare.** The derivation is pure and cheap; native and app each call it on the same config (and `runMCPLoader` once per loader) instead of threading a value through `BuildCatalogWithAsync`'s 13 call sites.
- **What this unblocks (breaks the R3a/R4b deferral).** Children's per-run catalogs (R4b remainder / R6) can take their toolset configs from `NewAgentToolConfigs` with no further config work; the open R6 work is the catalog composition only.
- **Tests.** `TestAgentToolConfigsAreOneDerivationFromTheOwnerRun` (native): exact native and MCP configs, sandbox narrowing only for an mcp-covering agent sandbox, async drop, owner map untouched, no agents/no toolsets. `TestToolsetMCPServersStartInTheAgentSandbox` and `TestAgentConfigFieldsAreClassifiedForTheRunAndTheTools` now use the real derivation (the latter also asserts the MCP view equals the native tools config). `mutate-check.sh`: 6 of 6 caught, each a real `--- FAIL` (model, async, MCP from the raw toolset, sandbox narrowing, loader key lookup, loader settings).
- **Open.** (Closed by T-009: the child's own model key is now hidden too; see "Model key environment filter is run-scoped (T-009)".) R4b remains partial pending shared child catalog assembly (R6); see "R4b remainder" below.

## Unified agent runs R4b remainder: one assembly step builds the owner's and the children's catalogs (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Status: superseded by "R4b completed" below** (one composition, `native.CatalogSections`). Kept as written at the time: the assembly step now builds both kinds of catalog from one set of parts, but the owner's and a child's composition stay two functions (`MergeCatalogs` in `assembleRegisteredCatalog`, `childCatalogTools` in the subagent tool). The evidence for keeping them apart is below; the plan that would merge them is R6.
- **Done.**
  - `native.NewAssembledSubagentMCP` (`internal/tools/native/subagent.go`) makes the subagent tool's handle for a build that assembles its children itself. `newSubagentToolDescribed` then resolves the agents (native pool, agent filter, flags, description) and builds no child catalog.
  - `SubagentMCP.AssembleChildren(native.ChildParts{Lazy, LoadTool, RunMCP, MCP})` sets the owner's lazy set, the child `load_tool`, the isolated-run MCP loader and the build's `MCPCopies` under the tool's lock, and builds each agent's own and deepest-level catalogs once (`bindMCPLocked`; `bindMCP` is now a locking wrapper of it).
  - `acquireCatalogParts` uses `NewAssembledSubagentMCP`; `assembleRegisteredCatalog` calls `AssembleChildren` with the copies its own MCP catalog holds, replacing `SetLazy`, `SetRunMCP` and `BindCopies`.
  - So a resolver build (prepare, `ListTools`, remote start) builds each child catalog once instead of up to three times (construction, `SetLazy` with a `load_tool`, `BindCopies`). The construction build only ever saw the native pool, and its result was thrown away by the later builds.
- **Unchanged.**
  - Callers without an assembly (native tests, `BuildCatalogWithAsync` with no handle) keep the incremental path, including the `SetLazy` rebuild rule (`TestSetLazyWithoutALoadToolKeepsTheCatalogsTheFirstOneBuilt`, `TestSetLazyTwiceLeavesOneLoadTool`).
  - Lazy gates (copies gated with `GateFor`), hook owners, flags (`mcpBound`, background, `NoChangeTools`), the choice and depth catalog cache (choices still built on first use), toolsets (`NewAgentToolConfigs`), MCP state and scoping, T-008 sampling, and both T0 configs.
- **Parity.**
  - `TestChildCatalogsAreUnchanged` and `TestChildCatalogHookOwnersAreKept` now run on both paths (incremental and assembled) against the same `child_catalogs.txt` golden: 6 agents × 5 choices × 2 depths, definitions, routes, fingerprints and catalog identity.
  - The app `TestRunBaseline*`, mixed-chain, profile sandbox-choice and admission goldens pass. No testdata file was written (checked with `find -mmin`).
- **Tests (native, `subagent_assemble_children_test.go`).**
  - `TestAssembleChildrenBuildsEachChildCatalogOnceFromEveryPart`: no agent has catalogs before `AssembleChildren`. After it, each agent has exactly its own and deepest-level catalogs (one for an agent that does not nest), and they equal the incremental build's definition for definition. The subagent description is equal too.
  - `TestAssembleChildrenRefusesWhatTheIncrementalBuildRefuses`: a missing MCP entry fails with the incremental build's error text; a nil handle and a handle with no tool assemble nothing.
- **Mutations.** `mutate-check.sh` 4 of 5 caught, each a real test failure in the log:
  - construction building anyway;
  - `AssembleChildren` dropping the `load_tool`;
  - assembly dropping the run MCP loader (`TestIsolatedSubagentCallsItsMCPToolOnAServerInItsWorktree`);
  - assembly skipping `AssembleChildren` (child lazy/load_tool and hook tests).

  Not caught: the resolver using `NewSubagentMCP` instead of `NewAssembledSubagentMCP`. That restores the old extra builds with the same result, and the build count is visible in native only.
- **Cost.**
  - `BenchmarkSubagentToolPrepare`: incremental 2,093 allocs/op, ~320 µs; assembled 1,938 allocs/op, ~282 µs.
  - `TestReportRegisteredCatalogBuildCost` (env-gated): 11,454 → 11,398 allocations per app build, about 2.8 ms.
- **Error timing (error path only).** A child catalog that cannot be built (`tools.NewCatalog` refusing a duplicate name) now fails the build in assembly, after the MCP servers were listed, instead of at the native construction. The text is the same (`ConfigError` "<setting>: <err>").
  - When an agent also has a bad MCP entry, the MCP entry error now wins (`checkMCPEntries` runs for all agents first).
  - A pool from `childNativePool` plus `nestedSelf` and `load_tool` has no duplicate name in any fixture or loader-accepted config found; this ordering was not tested.
- **Why the two compositions stay apart (code evidence).**
  - **Order.** The owner's list is native …, `subagent`, `profile_message`, `load_tool`, MCP (`BuildCatalogWithAsync` appends `profile_message` after the subagent tool). A child's is native … with `profile_message` last in its pool, then `subagent` (`nestedSelf`), `load_tool`, MCP (`childCatalogTools`, pool from `childPool`). One composition would reorder one side's tools array, which changes the provider request and the goldens.
  - **When the filter applies.** The owner's registered catalog is unfiltered. `ListTools` reports the hidden tools from it, and `applyProfileTools` (strict entries, allow plus deny) narrows it per prepare, then plan mode, `Only` and `WithoutDenied` per run. A child's filter (session deny, agent deny and allow) applies when its catalog is built, and an entry its deny covers is dropped (U3: deny inherited, allow not).
  - **Variants.** A child has leaf and sandbox-choice variants (no subagent tool; re-described native tools) built on demand under the tool's lock. The owner has none.
- **Plan for R6 (not circular).** The parts and configs are now one source: `NewAgentToolConfigs` for the tool side, `MCPCopies` and the lazy set for MCP, and one assembly step. Merging the compositions is therefore a behaviour decision only:
  1. Decide whether the owner's tool order may change. If not, the composition takes an explicit order list per side.
  2. Move `childCatalogTools` beside the owner's merge as `compose(parts, side)`, where side gives the order, the filter and the strictness.
  3. Keep the golden harness on both paths as the guard.
- **Open.** R4b stays partial (above). `SubagentMCP.SetLazy`, `SetRunMCP`, `BindCopies` and `BindToolsets` now serve only native tests and handles made without an assembly; they are kept for those callers.

## Model key environment filter: one key name per catalog, the owner run's (T-007 observation) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Status: closed for native child processes by T-009** (see "Model key environment filter is run-scoped (T-009)" below); MCP and LSP servers are still open there. Recorded as a bug report ("Shells and hooks hide only the owner run's model key"). This section describes the state before T-009.
- **The mechanism.** `buildNativeBashEnvironment` (`internal/tools/native/shell_run.go`) gives a tool's child process:
  - inherited variables from an allowlist only (`PATH`, `HOME`, locale, temp dirs and the Windows equivalents);
  - plus the configured `env` and `env_file` values;
  - minus `JAD_API_TOKEN`, the one name `apiKeyEnv`, and `env_deny`.

  bash, exec (through `shellChildEnvironment`), tool_smith and the hooks (`runHookChildOutput`) all use it. A process-environment key therefore reaches a shell only through configured `env` or `env_file`. That includes the setting's top-level `env_file`, which is applied to toolsets' `exec` and `tool_smith` by default (`withDefaultEnvFile`, `envFileTools`, `internal/sessionfs/layout_load.go`).
- **Which name each surface hides:**
  - **Owner run (profile):** its native tools and hooks are built from the run config, so they hide the run's model key, including a `profile_message` model choice (prepare runs per run). Persistent run-event hooks use `hookAPIKeyEnv`, the run's model.
  - **Plain agent child:** its native tools are the owner's instances (`childNativePool`), so they hide the owner run's key. The child's own model key is not hidden: its `model` field, or a call's `model` argument (`withCallModel`).
  - **Toolset agent child:** `NewAgentToolConfigs` gives the toolset config `Model = owner.Model`, so its native tools hide the owner run's key, not the agent's own.
  - **Hooks around child tools:** the session and toolset MCP copies (`NewMCPCopies(…, config.Model.APIKeyEnv)`, toolset copies with the toolset's hooks) and the nested subagent copy (`nestedSelf`, owner handle) all pass the owner run's key name. `subagent_stop` fires with `spec.Template.Base`, the caller's config, so the caller's key.
  - **MCP stdio servers:** no model key filter at all. Their environment is the `mcp` allowlist (`defaultEnvironment`, `internal/tools/mcp/environment.go`) plus the server's configured `env`.
- **Effect.** When a configured `env` or `env_file` holds the key of a model other than the owner run's, model-driven processes see it:
  - a child with its own model, whose provider's key is in the `.env`, can read that key in its shells and hooks;
  - the owner's shells can read the agent's key;
  - any shell can read the key of a model that is not running.

  The provider request itself is unaffected. `env_deny` is the existing control and must list every key name. The exposure is to model-driven code inside the configured sandbox, not a sandbox escape.
- **What would close it.** A run-scoped hide: carry the running model's key name on the run (for example in `ExecutionContext`, set by `runEphemeral` and `runLocked`) and have the shell, exec, tool_smith and hook environments drop it beside the catalog's. Alternatively, or additionally, hide every model key name the session can use (the profile's models, the agents' models, `model_fallback`). Either needs a test per surface (plain, toolset, hook, call `model` argument) that names the agent's key in `env`.

## Unified agent runs R4b completed: owner and child catalogs composed by one ordered step from shared sections (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Status: R4b done.** The "R4b remainder" section above called a single composition a nominal wrapper because the two sides order `profile_message` differently. That was wrong: both orders are one sequence (native, `subagent`, `profile_message`, `load_tool`, MCP). A child just has `profile_message` inside its native pool and an empty `profile_message` section. Each side's provider-visible order is unchanged.
- **Done.**
  - `native.CatalogSections{Native, Subagent, ProfileMessage, LoadTool, MCP}` (`internal/tools/native/catalog_sections.go`): `Tools()` is the one order, `Compose()` the one catalog build. Each side's policy is which tools fill a section, decided before composing. A child is filtered by its agent (inherited deny plus its own tools) when its pool and MCP tools are bound, and `load_tool` only when its filter shows it. The owner is unfiltered at composition and narrowed per prepare by `applyProfileTools` (allow, plan mode, strict entries). U3 is unchanged: the deny ceiling is inherited, the allow list is not.
  - The owner side: `buildCatalogSections` replaces the body of `BuildCatalogWithAsync`, which now composes its result (its 13 callers are unchanged). The new `BuildCatalogSections` gives the resolver the sections uncomposed, after checking them as a catalog so native errors appear where they did. `assembleRegisteredCatalog` adds the MCP copies as the MCP section, redescribes the subagent section (`SubagentMCP.RedescribeSections`, on a copy, so the parts are untouched) and composes once. Before, it built three more catalogs: the MCP catalog, the `Redescribe` rebuild and `MergeCatalogs`.
  - The child side: `childCatalogSections` (formerly `childCatalogTools`) fills the same sections, and `childCatalogLocked` composes them.
  - Shared resources: children get the owner's own `load_tool` (`ChildParts.LoadTool = sections.LoadTool`). `native.ChildLoadTool` built a second, identical tool and reread and parsed every tool-definition manifest per build; it had no other caller and is removed. MCP copies were already shared (R4b).
- **Parity.** No golden file was written (none newer than the change); the run-baseline, mixed-chain, sandbox-choice and `child_catalogs.txt` goldens pass. New tests:
  - `TestCatalogSectionsHaveOneOrder` checks the order, empty sections and a duplicate name across sections.
  - `TestOwnerAndChildCatalogsAreComposedFromSharedSections` (native) checks:
    - `BuildCatalogSections` composed equals `BuildCatalogWithAsync`;
