    - the owner composed once equals the native catalog, redescribed and merged with MCP, the old mechanics;
    - each child's order for own and leaf, including an agent that does not nest;
    - each child holds the owner's `load_tool` and MCP copy.
  - `TestCatalogAssemblyStartsNothingAndLeavesItsAcquiredPartsAlone` (app) now also checks that the owner's order is the native sections then the MCP tools as listed, and that the parts' subagent section is not redescribed in place.
- **Cost.** The registered-catalog build of the assembly fixture went from 11,398 to 8,421 allocations (2.3 ms); most of the saving is the manifest reread. The native prepare benchmark is unchanged, about 1,938 allocs per op (it does not use this path).
- **Error-path order only.** A duplicate name among the profile's MCP tools is now reported after the children are assembled, not before (same text). Native names are pinned by `requireDefinition`, so the check kept in `BuildCatalogSections` is defensive and has no test that reaches it.
- **Open.**
  - The tool_smith bridge is bound with `sections.Tools()`, the same list as before, so scripts can still call `profile_message`. A mutation that binds only the early native list is not caught by any test, because no test reaches `profile_message` from a script. This coverage gap predates this change. Closing it needs a catalog-level test with tool_smith and profile_message that inspects the bridge's tools.
  - The owner's subagent tool and each nesting child's `nestedSelf` are still two hooked wrappers of one tool, because their descriptions differ: the owner's keeps the manifest text, the child's is the code's text, and both are pinned by goldens.
  - Children's catalogs are still built at the owner's prepare and cached per choice and depth. Building them per run from a template config remains R6.
- **Test fixture fix.** `newLayoutFixtureWithBudget` (`internal/app/layout_integration_test.go`) read `len(f.models)` outside its lock to number the response id. Under `-race` this failed `TestABackgroundSubagentOfANarrowedRunKeepsItsMCPServersUntilItEnds` (T-007, a parent and its background child are served at once). It now reads it under the lock. Test only.

## Model key environment filter is run-scoped (T-009) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Confirmed first.** New app tests (`internal/app/model_key_env_test.go`) put all three fixture models' key variables in the configured `env`. On the old code, a plain agent's exec, a toolset agent's exec, a child's `pre_tool`/`post_tool` hooks, the child of a call that chose `model`, and each of two sibling children on different models all showed the child model's key (`C=[child-in-env]`). The owner's exec hid only its own key.
- **Fix.** `tools.ExecutionContext.ModelKeyEnvs` (mirrored in `CallerContext`; `ForNested` carries it) lists the key variables of the models that may answer the call's run and every local sub-agent run above it.
  - The bound runner sets it on every run to `runModelKeys(config)`: the run's model key plus each `model_fallback` model that loads. A `profile_message` target or remote run starts its own list.
  - `runEphemeral` adds the child's keys (its agent's model or the call's `model` choice, plus fallbacks) to the caller's list with `JoinDeny`, which copies, so a caller's list never changes.
  - Every native child process of a call drops them beside the build-time `apiKeyEnv`: exec and tool_smith, fresh and standby (`callModelKeys` in `runShellChildDetailed`, `takeExecStandby`, `takeToolSmithStandby`), and `pre_tool`/`post_tool`/`post_edit` commands (`hookChild.call`).
  - Run-event commands drop `RunEvent.ModelKeyEnvs` (not in the payload, `json:"-"`): `fireSessionHookWithKey` adds the run's `runModelKeys` when run events are active, and `subagent_stop` adds the ended child's list.
- **Per-run isolation of shared tools.** The key list is read per call, not captured in the tool, so one exec instance shared by runs on different models hides from each call its own run's keys and not the other run's (sibling and 16-way concurrent tests). A standby's key includes its environment (`standbyKey`), so a standby warmed by one run is not taken by a run on another model (shim, named-pipe and tool_smith standby tests).
- **Unchanged.** The owner's build-time key, `env_deny`, `JAD_API_TOKEN`, sandboxes and configs. Another model's key that no run in the chain uses is still passed when `env` sets it: the policy is "the keys of the models that may answer this run", not "every key the session knows". `extraEnv`/`prependEnv` are still appended after the filter; they are the tool's own variables (exec helper paths, the R profile, tool_smith result/input/socket/token paths), never configured ones.
- **Docs.** `env_deny` in `sample/schemes/setting.schema.json` and `design_bash.md` now say which keys are always removed.
- **Open: MCP stdio servers.** Their environment is the MCP allowlist plus `env_from` and literal `env` (`internal/tools/mcp/config.go` `normalizeStdio`); no model key is removed. A server is shared by the runs of its manager and started once, so a per-run filter cannot apply. A server file that names a model key in `env_from` or `env` gets it on purpose, so stripping it would break intended configs. Closing it would need a policy decision: a load-time warning, or refusing model key names unless an explicit opt-in is set.
- **Open: LSP servers.** `lsp_client.go` appends the configured server `env` to `environmentWithoutServerToken()` with no denial. Same reasoning as MCP: shared per session, configured on purpose.
- **Open: profile_message targets** did not inherit the caller's keys. (Closed by "T-009 follow-up: profile_message targets hide the caller's model keys" below.)
- **Open: harness git.** `holderLauncher` (`sandbox_isolated.go`) runs git in an overlay holder with the full `os.Environ()`, as host-side collection does. It is not model-driven code, but repository config can run commands. Not in this task's scope; not changed.
- **Not covered by a test** (the remote-start part is closed by the follow-up below). A remote-started child with `model_fallback`: `runEphemeral`'s use of `runModelKeys` rather than only the child's key is redundant when a local bound runner already listed the fallbacks. The mutation to only the child's key was not caught by the local tests. `env_file` values are merged into `Env` at load (`loadConfiguredEnvFile`), so they take the tested `env` path; no separate `env_file` test was added.

## T-009 follow-up: profile_message targets hide the caller's model keys (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Gap confirmed by test.** `TestAProfileMessageTargetsToolsAndHooksHideTheCallersModelKey` (`internal/app/model_key_env_profile_message_test.go`): dev/coder runs `openai/small` on `CALLER_PROVIDER_KEY` and sends a `profile_message` to review/reviewer (`openai/large`, `FIXTURE_KEY`), whose exec `env` and hook `env` set `CALLER_PROVIDER_KEY`. With the plumbing removed (mutations below), the target's exec and its child's exec showed `C=[caller-in-env]`, and so did its `run_start` command.
- **Fix.** The run chain policy now crosses a local `profile_message` the way `Deny` (U3) does:
  - `profileMessagePlan.modelKeys` takes `CallerContext.ModelKeyEnvs`; `targetRunner` puts it on `profileDelegation.modelKeys` of that run's own runner copy.
  - The bound runner sets `ToolExecution.ModelKeyEnvs = JoinDeny(inheritedModelKeys(), runModelKeys(config))`, so the target's tool calls, its `pre_tool`/`post_tool`/`post_edit` commands, its children (`runEphemeral` joins to it) and further `profile_message` targets (through `Caller()`) all hide the caller's keys.
  - Every run event of the bound runner (`run_start`, `run_end`, `stop`, `notification`, `prompt_submit`, `session_start`, automatic `pre_compact`) goes through the new `boundRunner.fireHook`, which joins `inheritedModelKeys()` to the event. `subagent_stop` already uses the run's execution list.
- **Isolation.** Nothing global changes: the profile's settings, its cached tools and its own runs are untouched (the test's later direct run of the target still sees `C=[caller-in-env]`, as no model of that run uses it). A remote `profile_message` start passes nil: the caller's keys are on another server, as `Deny` does not cross the hop. A runner that is not a `boundRunner` (tests only) builds no tools from settings, so `targetRunner` does not refuse it for keys, unlike for `Deny`.
- **Remote-start fallback (former mutation gap).** `TestARemoteStartedChildHidesItsFallbackModelsKey`: a sub-agent started over the remote API, whose profile has `model_fallback` `openai/spare` (`SPARE_PROVIDER_KEY`), hides that key in its exec; it has no local caller list, so only `runEphemeral`'s `runModelKeys` names it. The mutation to only the child's own key is now caught.
- **Verified.** `mutate-check.sh` 6 of 6 caught with real test failures (bound runner join, `fireHook` join, plan field, delegation field, queue pass-through, `runEphemeral` fallback). Full `internal/app` tests pass; `-race -count=2` on the model-key, profile_message, deny-ceiling, target-runner, worktree, MCP-wrapper, remote-start and hook groups found no races.
- **Open: not each run event tested on a target.** Only `run_start`, `pre_tool` and `subagent_stop` are checked on a target run; `run_end`, `stop`, `notification`, `prompt_submit`, `session_start` and automatic `pre_compact` share `fireHook` and are covered by code reading only. Manual compaction (`maintenance.go`) is a user action with no caller and is unchanged.
- **Open: two profile hops.** A target that messages a third profile hands the joined list on through `Caller()`; this is by construction, not tested end to end.
- **Unchanged and still open:** MCP stdio and LSP server environments (configured on purpose, shared per manager/session) and harness git, as recorded in the T-009 section above.

## Shared run tree: one live registry counts both kinds of run for the run caps (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Decision (design §3.5 "run counts", §3.7 "one run tree registry"; U11 as ruled).** `native.RunTree` is a live node registry owned by the resolver (`Resolver.runTree`) and shared by every `SubagentManager` (`SetRunTree` in `finishSubagentBuild`, before the manager is published) and every local `profile_message` run. A node has a process-unique id (`run_N`, not an external id), its parent, its root, the session that executes it, its kind (`subagent`, `remote_subagent`, `profile_message`), its state (`queued`, `running`) and the root ceiling it passes on; `Release` takes it out once. The external run ids (`sub_…`, manifests' `root`, `RootRun`, turn ids) are unchanged.
- **Rules.**
  - A start's parent is the calling run's node, carried as `ExecutionContext.RunNode` (and `CallerContext.RunNode`): set by `SubagentManager.start` for a child, by `httpapi.ProfileRunRequest.RunNode` → `activeRun.runNode` → `executor` for a message's target run. A user's run has none, so its starts are roots: counted, never refused by the caps (top-level semantics kept). A run started over the remote API is a root on that host (remote boundary kept).
  - `max_runs_per_root` counts the live runs below the root (the root itself not counted, as `byRoot-1` did). The root's value is the tree's ceiling; each nested start is bounded by the lowest value on its path (`narrowCap`), so a caller can narrow it and a target whose config allows more cannot widen it.
  - `max_runs_per_session` is checked on the session that executes the new run: the caller's for a sub-agent (local or remote), the target's (`plan.key`) for a message. It counts across every manager and both kinds. *Corrected by the review follow-up below: the value is that executing session's own, not the caller's.*
  - Without a `tools.native.subagent` section a `profile_message` uses the defaults (16, 32) through `RunMaxRunsPerRoot`/`RunMaxRunsPerSession`, as `RunMaxDepth` does for the depth.
  - A queued message holds its node until it ends; a message whose target run started holds it until that run released the target's transcript (the watch in `attach`, after `released`). A message the pump is starting holds it until the start ends (`beginStart`/`endStart`; a finish meanwhile leaves it to `attach` or the failed start); a head that already finished is skipped instead of started.
  - Fail closed: a nested call (AgentDepth above 0) without a node, or with a node that is not live, is refused `ErrRunTreeParentGone` (`subagent_unavailable`, `profile_unavailable`) instead of starting an uncounted tree.
- **Order kept.** Sub-agent admission is unchanged: closed, depth gate, caps, slot or queue (the admission golden is byte-identical). A message: Prepare's refusals (cycle, chain, same transcript, sandbox, model), then `max_depth`, then in `Start`: for a target whose line is pumping, the full line and the wait cycle, then the caps; for a target that looks free, the caps before the start is tried (a wait cycle that would have been found on a busy start keeps its precedence when the message could queue).
- **Lock order.** `RunTree.mu` is a leaf: taken under `SubagentManager.mu` (admission, state) and under `profileQueueSet.mu` (a message's admission), never held while anything else is called. `profileMessageRun.mu` is never held across a tree call.
- **Behaviour changes, each isolated in a test.**
  - The sub-agents of a profile target are nested starts of the caller's tree and may be refused `subagent_limit_reached` (`TestRunTreeRootCapAcrossAProfileHop`, `TestAStartFromAProfileTargetIsCappedInItsCallersTree`; before, a profile hop started a tree of its own).
  - A message run is counted in its target's session, so a later nested start there may be refused (`TestRunTreeSessionCapCountsTheMessageRunInItsTargetsSession`).
  - A message itself may be refused `profile_limit_reached` (`TestProfileMessageIsRefusedAtTheRootCeilingOfItsCallersTree`, `TestProfileMessageSessionCapAndParentAcrossTrees`, `TestProfileMessageWithoutASubagentSectionUsesTheDefaultRootCap`).
  - A nested remote sub-agent start from a profile target (which now has a node) holds a place on this host, as one from a sub-agent did.
  - A session's count spans storage folders (`TestManagersWithTheSameRunIDsShareOneTree`); before, each manager counted its own.
  - A root whose own run ended no longer frees a place for its descendants: the count is of the runs below it, which is what the setting describes (`byRoot-1` undercounted then).
  - Unchanged: `server.max_concurrent_runs`, slots and queues, the per-target message queues and their order, isolation, cancellation and the lineage cascades, keep_finished (finished runs are never nodes) and recovery (the tree is in memory; a restart starts it empty, as the counts were).
- **Tests.** Q0 characterisation first, passing on the old code: `TestEveryLocalRunEndGivesBackItsRunCapPlaces` (done, failed, launcher panic, panic after the launcher, stopped running and queued, closed between handle and run, manager closed, refused for a full queue and for no slot, nested starts in turn) and the two mixed-chain cap tests, which recorded the old behaviour and were then flipped. New: `run_tree_test.go` (counts, ceiling, session cap, once-only release, 64 concurrent starts at the last place, two managers with the same run ids, fail closed locally and remotely), `run_tree_caps_test.go` (mixed chain caps and ceilings across differing settings, every message path: answered, queued then stopped, queued behind the head, queued then run, queue wait ended, busy without a queue, full line). Existing tests that hand-built a nested call now give it a real node (`seedRunRoot`, `nestedExecution`); the R6 test of a start with chain depth but no node is renamed `TestAStartWithNoRunNodeIsGatedAndFailsFastButNotCapped`. No golden changed.
- **Open.**
  - **Not covered by a test:** the release in `attach`'s late branch (a message that finished while the pump was starting it, whose run then started) and the deferred release in `recoverRun` (a panic inside `finish`). Both are race or panic windows; `mutate-check.sh` cannot reach them deterministically. *Closed by the review follow-up below.*
  - **Remote `profile_message`** (to a remote target) takes no node, as before; only nested remote sub-agent starts hold a place on this host.
  - **Q3 not done (by plan):** stop/reset/delete fan-out, handle ownership and the background-writer places still live in the managers and the lineage cascades; the tree is used for the caps only. *See "Run tree Q3": writer places moved to the tree; the fan-outs stay, by recommendation.*
  - **In memory only:** nodes do not survive a restart (a queued message does not either).
  - **Build cache:** `/home/www/.cache` (a 16 GB tmpfs) filled during this work; the checks ran with `GOCACHE=/tmp/t007q/gocache`. The machine's default cache needs cleaning before builds there succeed. *Seen free again (2% used) at the review follow-up; that run used the default cache.*

## Shared run tree review: executing session's own session cap, ended parents, release gaps closed (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Session cap, corrected.** `max_runs_per_session` is now the value of the session that executes the new run, not the caller's. For a sub-agent (local or remote) that is the same thing as before: the subagent tool belongs to the caller's config and the run executes in the caller's session. For a `profile_message` run it changes: the messenger reads the target's own `NativeSubagent.RunMaxRunsPerSession()` from the resolved target config (`targetMaxRunsPerSession`; 32 when the target has no subagent section or its settings are not a `boundRunner`'s). `ProfileMessageRequest.MaxRunsPerSession` and the tool's `maxPerSession` are removed (the caller's session cap was the wrong input); `max_runs_per_root` is still the caller's, narrowed by the tree's ceiling. Behaviour change against the earlier T-007 step, isolated in `TestRunTreeSessionCapIsTheExecutingSessionsOwnAcrossAProfileHop` (one run of another tree executes in the reviewer's session: coder 8 / reviewer 1 refuses the message `profile_limit_reached`; coder 1 / reviewer 8 admits it and the reviewer's child) and in the reworked `TestProfileMessageSessionCapAndParentAcrossTrees` (refused at the target's own cap). Schema, settings comment and design §3.5 updated.
- **Stale parent found and fixed.** A live descendant *run* never depended on its parent's node: its calls carry its own node, and `Reserve` only needs the direct parent (root and ceiling are copied into each node). `TestALiveDescendantStartsChildrenAfterItsParentsNodeIsGone` shows a profile target's background sub-agent starting a child after the target's node was released, under the caller's root and ceiling, refused past it, and nothing left after. The real gap was work that is not a run: a profile_message target's handles are owned by the target's session and outlive its run (a tool_smith script runs as a handle and its bridge may call `profile_message`). Such a call carries the ended run's node, which the earlier step had released, so it failed closed (`profile_unavailable`) where before the tree it ran. Fix: `RunNode.End` gives back the places (counted nowhere, listed as `ended`) and keeps the node as a parent; the message run ends its node (`endNode`) once its target run released the transcript, and `Resolver.releaseNodeAfter` releases it when nothing is live under the message's lineage key, by the same rule and end callbacks as a narrowing's MCP manager (`runNodeDrains`; the managers' callback is now `lineageWorkEnded`, which runs `checkMCPDrains` and `checkNodeDrains`). A message whose target run never started still releases at once; sub-agent nodes release at once (a sub-agent's handles are owned by its run id and swept at its end). A node released or never minted still fails closed. Test: `TestAnEndedMessageRunStaysTheParentOfTheWorkItLeft` (a handle registered under the run's lineage; the late message from the ended node queues below it with its root and ceiling, the ended node stays while the handle goes, the tree is empty once it ended, no drain pending).
- **Release gaps closed.** `TestAMessageThatEndsWhileItsStartIsOnItsWayLeavesNoNode` stops a queued message from inside the pump's start (a wrapping `ProfileRunStarter`), checks the node stays while the start is on its way, and that the late branch of `attach` gives it back after the run released the transcript. `TestAPanicInsideFinishGivesBackTheRunsNode` panics inside `finish` after the manifest save and before the node release (new test seam `SubagentManager.inFinish`, like `afterLaunch`), and checks the call returns, the tree is empty and a later start finishes.
- **Lock and node lifetimes.** `RunTree.mu` and `runNodeDrains.mu` are leaves; `lineageLive` and `RunNode.Release` are called outside `runNodeDrains.mu`. A sub-agent node: reserved in `admitLocked` under `SubagentManager.mu`, released in `finish` (under `mu`), `undoReservationLocked`, the admission refusals or `recoverRun`. A remote place: `releaseRemote` (once). A message node: reserved under `profileQueueSet.mu`; released by `Start`'s deferred release when not handed out, by `finish` when no run or start holds it, by the pump on a failed start, or ended by `attach` (both branches) and released after the lineage drained. Every release is once-only and none holds `profileMessageRun.mu`.
- **Checks.** `mutate-check.sh`: 9 caught, each with a `--- FAIL` in the copied log (target cap ignored, finish ignoring `starting`, late branch without release, normal attach releasing instead of ending, drain not releasing, end callback not draining nodes, `Reserve` refusing ended parents, `recoverRun` without release, `SetState` reviving an ended node); one equivalent mutation discarded. Full `native` and `app` packages pass; `-race` on the run tree, lifetime, release, cap, message, MCP scope and lineage groups.
- **Open.**
  - **No end-to-end tool_smith test:** the stale-parent fix is tested with a registered handle under the run's lineage, not a real TypeScript script calling `profile_message` through the bridge; the bridge passes `ForNested` (which keeps `RunNode`), checked by reading only. *Closed by the follow-up below.*
  - **Panic inside finish leaves the async handle open:** with the panic before `run.async.end`, `recoverRun` closes `done` and gives back the node but the handle row of a background run is not ended (unchanged, pre-existing; seen by reading `recoverRun` and `finish`, not by a test). Filed as a bug record, not fixed. *Fixed by the follow-up below.*
  - **Ended nodes are in memory only** and live as long as the lineage they wait for; a lineage that never drains before shutdown keeps its node until the process ends (bounded by the live work).

## Shared run tree follow-up: a panic inside finish ends the run whole; tool_smith late-call regression (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Fix.** `SubagentManager.finish` now records the end and calls `endRun`, which does the rest in order: node, finished-list place (with the `keep_finished` trim), writer place, async handle, `done`, run-end notification. Each step is marked on the run before it runs (`listed`, `writerReleased`, `asyncEnded`, `doneOnce`), so `recoverRun`, after a panic once the end was recorded, calls `endRun` again and does exactly the steps not yet begun; a step that panicked is not retried, so a second panic cannot come from it inside the recover. Before, `recoverRun` only closed `done` (and gave back the node): a background run's handle stayed `running` for `async`, its writer place stayed taken, and the run was never in the finished list (so `keep_finished` never trimmed it). The handle ends with the state and answer `finish` recorded (`run.full` for an external run, else the stored, cut result). Normal ends are unchanged: same steps, same order.
- **Tests.** `TestAPanicInsideFinishOfABackgroundRunEndsItsHandleAndGivesEverythingBack` (background writer, panic in the `inFinish` seam after the manifest save): `async wait` reports the handle `done` with its answer; writer place, slot (`running` 0) and tree node are given back; the run is in the finished list; a later handoff of the same session runs; no goroutine growth. `TestALateProfileMessageFromATargetsBackgroundScriptJoinsItsTree`, end to end with the real interpreter (bun, or node with type stripping; skipped without one, as the other tool_smith app test): dev/coder messages review/reviewer, whose run starts a tool_smith script as a handle (`block_ms` 0) and ends; the script waits for a gate file and then calls `profile_message` to dev/coder through the bridge. The reviewer's node is ended (not counted) while the script goes, the late call is answered, and the tree is empty once the script ended. With the node released instead of ended, the late call fails `profile_unavailable` ("the run this call belongs to is not going any more"), confirmed by `mutate-check.sh`.
- **Checks.** `mutate-check.sh`: 5 caught with `--- FAIL` in the copied log (`recoverRun` back to closing `done` only; the handle, writer and finished-list steps each skipped; the message node released instead of ended). `TestAnEndedMessageRunStaysTheParentOfTheWorkItLeft` was flaky under `-race` (the late message's node goes just after `Done`, once its run released the transcript) and now polls for it. `-race` on the finish, background writer, goroutine, run tree, tool_smith, MCP scope and message groups (app ×5): no data race.
- **Open.** A panic inside a step of `endRun` itself (the trim's `removeDropped`, the handle's result write) leaves that one step undone, by design (not retried); the others still run in the recover. Not tested. *Superseded by "Run end steps" below: each step is now guarded on its own and two of them are tested.*

## Run end steps: a panic inside one cleanup step of a sub-agent run's end (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **What was wrong (tested before the fix).** A panic inside a step of `SubagentManager.endRun` went up to `recoverRun`, which called `endRun` again. Two failures were observed with the new tests: (1) the `keep_finished` drop callback (`onDropped`, the app's `remoteRuns.forget`) panicking skipped the removal of the dropped run's manifest and transcript folder, and of every later dropped run, for good (the drop list was not built again); (2) the run-end notification had no mark, so after it panicked the recovery called it again. Found by reading the code, not tested: a panic in a step during the recovery's second `endRun` (for example the notification panicking every time) went up out of the deferred `recoverRun` and ended the server, and a panic inside the `mu` section (trim) would have left `mu` locked.
- **Fix (`subagent_manager.go`).** Each step goes through `endStep(runID, step, mark, fn)`. It takes the step's mark first, so a step that panicked is never tried again, and recovers and logs the panic (`slog.Error`, "sub-agent run end step failed inside the server", with the run, the step and the stack). The steps are `finished_list`, then each dropped run's `dropped_callback` and `dropped_files`, then `writer_place`, `async_handle`, `done`, and `run_end_notify`. `finished_list` (node release, list, trim) unlocks `mu` in a defer. The notification has a new mark (`notified`). In `removeDropped` (also used by the startup trim) each dropped run's callback and file removal are separate steps, so a panicking callback still lets its files go, and the other runs too. When nothing panics, the order and the work are unchanged.
- **Tests (`run_end_steps_test.go`).**
  - `TestAPanicInsideTheDropStepOfARunsEndStillRunsTheLaterSteps`: keep 1, the second run's trim drops the first and the callback panics. It checks:
    - the callback ran once and the first run's manifest was still removed;
    - the second run's handle is terminal with its answer, and its writer place, slot and tree place are given back;
    - the second run is the only one listed and `done` is closed;
    - one notification per run, and the panic is logged with step and run.
  - `TestAPanicInsideTheLastStepOfARunsEndIsNotRetried`: the second run's notification panics. It checks that it is not retried, that everything before it was given back, and that the panic is logged.
  - Both then call `endRun` again and check it repeats nothing (writer place, list, removals, drop callbacks, notifications).
  - `mutate-check.sh`: 4 of 5 caught, each a `--- FAIL` in its log. Caught: callback not guarded, notification without a mark, writer place without a mark, panic re-raised by the guard. Not caught: the async step without a mark. A second `end` of a terminal handle changes nothing a test sees, so I treated it as equivalent.
  - `-race -count=2` on the panic, background-writer, keep, drop, finish, run-tree and lineage tests: no data races.
- **Open: what the failed step held stays held, by design.** The step is not retried, because retrying it in the recovery could panic again and end the server. So, for the one step that panicked:
  - **`finished_list` (trim):** dropped runs already taken out of the list but not yet returned have their manifest and folder left on disk. The next server start loads them back and trims them (`recover`, by reading the code).
  - **`dropped_callback`:** what the app forgets for that run (its remote run record) stays in memory.
  - **`dropped_files`:** the manifest or folder stays on disk until a later trim or the next start.
  - **`writer_place`:** the owner keeps one background writer place taken, until the manager is rebuilt. *Since "Run tree Q3": until the process restarts.*
  - **`async_handle`:** the handle stays `running` for `async`; its waiters wait until their own timeout.
  - **`done`:** cannot panic (closes a channel once).
  - **`run_end_notify`:** the app does not look again for that run; it looks on the next run end.
  - Only the drop callback and the notification are tested (they are the steps a test can make panic without a new seam). The `mu` unlock in `finished_list` and the guards on `writer_place` and `async_handle` are checked by reading the code only.

## Run tree Q3: fan-out releases, writer places in the tree, what stays outside it (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Design §3.7 against the code.** The run tree (`native.RunTree`) holds nodes with id, parent, root, executing session, kind and state, and counts the caps. It holds no owner, lineage key or cancel function. Stop, reset and delete pick their targets elsewhere:
  - sub-agent runs by `run.owner` and `run.lineage` (`CancelOwner`, `CancelUnmanagedLineage`, `CancelUnmanagedOwnersWithPrefix`, through `liveRuns`);
  - handles (processes, `profile_message` and remote handles) in `asyncmgr` by owner and lineage;
  - user-started persistent runs in `liveRunStops`.
- **Fan-out tests (new, all passed on the code as it was; no regression found).**
  - `TestFanOutsReleaseTheEndedParentAndItsLiveDescendant` (stop, reset, delete): coder → explore → reviewer message, whose run starts finder as a handle and ends. Before the fan-out the tree holds the ended message node, finder below it (same root) and the reviewer's own finder (a root); the reviewer's session counts 2. After it, finder is stopped with the fan-out's reason, both chain nodes are gone (finder at its end, the message node once its lineage drained), the session counts 1, no drain is pending, and the reviewer's own finder still runs.
  - `TestFanOutsReleaseAQueuedOrRunningMessagesNode` (stop, reset, delete × queued, running): a message queued behind a held transcript, or running (fan-out from inside its model call), leaves the tree empty after the caller's fan-out; a stopped message reports `stopped`.
- **Writer places: one owner can span managers; fixed.**
  - **Reachable:** managers are keyed by `storage_dir`. A session that changes `tools.native.subagent.storage_dir` (or `tool_storage_dir`/`cwd`, which the default follows) while a background writer runs sends its next start through a second manager. Each manager counted its own writers, so the owner got a second background writer past `max_background_writers` 1. `TestBackgroundWriterCapIsTheOwnersAcrossManagers` showed it (the second call was handed off as `sub_…`, running). This predates T-007 (`writers` was per manager at HEAD); the checkpoint gate (`Resolver.BackgroundWriters`) already summed every manager, so the cap and the gate disagreed.
  - **Fix:** the places are counted in the run tree per owner (`RunTree.ReserveWriter`, `ReleaseWriter`, `Writers`). `SubagentManager.reserveWriter` checks and counts there under its own lock, the tree's lock being a leaf as before (a closed manager still reserves, so its start reports the closure). The manager's `writers` map is gone and `Resolver.BackgroundWriters` reads the tree once instead of summing managers. Same cap, same notes, same checkpoint gate; the only change is that the count is the owner's across managers, which is what the setting describes ("one session").
  - **Tests:** the app test above (now the second writer runs in its call with "Not handed off"); `TestBackgroundWriterPlacesAreTheOwnersInTheSharedTree`; `TestBackgroundWriterPlacesAcrossManagersAreAtomic` (64 concurrent reservations in two managers take exactly the cap of 3). `mutate-check.sh`: 6 caught with `--- FAIL` in the copied log (closed-manager force always on, release a no-op, resolver count 0, cap off by one, per-manager key, drain not releasing).
  - **Effect on the earlier "Run end steps" note:** a `writer_place` step that panicked now keeps the owner's place until the process restarts (the tree is the process's), not until the manager is rebuilt.
- **Remote top-level counts (characterised, unchanged).**
  - On the calling host, a top-level remote sub-agent start holds no node; a nested one holds one `remote_subagent` node below the caller, in the calling session, until the remote run ends (`TestRemoteStartsTopLevelHoldNoNodeNestedHoldOneBelowTheCaller`). A top-level local start is a root counted in its session; a top-level remote one is not, as at HEAD.
  - On the receiving host, a sub-agent run started over the remote API is one root node in the session it runs in, never refused by the caller's caps (they do not cross the boundary), and gone after a remote stop (`TestRemoteStartedSubagentIsARootOfThisHostsTree`).
- **Recommendation: do not move stop, reset and delete into the tree.**
  - It would remove no selector: handles are not runs and user runs are not nodes, so the `asyncmgr` and `liveRunStops` fan-outs stay. The tree would need owner, lineage keys and cancel functions copied from the run records, a third copy.
  - It would change counts: the fan-outs split handles (`asyncmgr`) from unmanaged runs so each stop is counted once; a tree-driven stop would have to keep that split.
  - Node release already follows every fan-out path (tests above), so the tree stays consistent without owning the stop.
  - What would make a move worth it: nodes for user runs and handles (one registry of all live work). That is the larger §3.7 redesign, not an incremental step.
- **Open.**
  - **Recovery:** the tree and the writer places are in memory; a restart starts both empty, as the per-manager counts did. Recovery stays with the per-folder manifests.
  - **Remote `profile_message` on the receiving host:** its target run carries no node, so its sub-agent starts are roots there. Not tested here.
  - **Test fixture note:** the running-message fan-out case answers its model call only after the message ended (bounded 5 s), because a fan-out does not wait and an answer could otherwise win against the stop (seen once in the first `verify-go.sh`, before that wait was added).
  - **Writer places in a manager without the shared tree** (a manager built outside the resolver, as in native tests) count in that manager's own tree, as before.

## Run tree Q3 follow-up: accepted split, asynchronous release, nested remote nodes on stop/reset/delete (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Decision (accepted by Master):** the run registry stays split. `native.RunTree` does admission only: nodes for `max_runs_per_root`/`max_runs_per_session` and the per-owner background writer places. The owner and lineage managers (`asyncmgr` for handles, the sub-agent managers for runs, `liveRunStops` for user runs, the lineage keys) do cancellation, handle ownership and persistence; recovery stays with the per-folder manifests. Design §3.7 now says this; §3.5 names the remote counts.
- **Release is asynchronous.** Stop, reset and delete only ask and do not touch the tree. Each node is released by its own run's end: a sub-agent node in `endRun`; a `profile_message` node once the target run released its transcript and its lineage drained; a `remote_subagent` node when the remote run ends (`run.Done`). Until then its places stay counted. A remote node therefore stays counted after its call was cancelled or its handle stopped, reset or deleted, for as long as the remote run goes; `remote_timeout_ms` (minimum 1 s, default 10 min) or the end of the connection bounds that.
- **Rule for new node kinds:** a new node kind, or a new path that reserves a node, must name the fan-out that stops its run, release its node exactly once on every end (done, failed, stopped, refused, panic, close), and have stop/reset/delete tests showing the release.
- **Nested remote node on stop/reset/delete, verified (no code change needed).**
  - `TestNestedRemoteHandleNodeIsReleasedAfterSessionStopResetDelete`: a nested remote start that became a handle, for each of `CancelOwner` (stop), `ResetOwner` (reset), `DeleteLineage` (delete), `DeleteOwnersWithPrefix` (a parent run's end sweep), with a remote that stops at once and with one that keeps going (test peer `ignoreStops`). The fan-out reaches the handle, the remote is asked to stop, the node and its session place stay while the remote run goes, and are released when it ends; no node is left after the remote goroutines return (also for a deleted handle record).
  - `TestNestedBlockingRemoteNodeIsReleasedAfterItsCallIsCancelled`: a blocking nested remote call (no handle) whose context is cancelled, as a session stop reaches a sub-agent run's calls, returns `context.Canceled` at once; the node stays while the remote run goes and is released by its end.
  - `mutate-check.sh`: 2 caught with `--- FAIL` in the log (releasing the node on the call's cancel; `releaseRemote` a no-op).
- **Open.**
  - These tests drive the `asyncmgr` and context calls that `Resolver.CancelSessionChildren`/`ResetSessionChildren`/`deleteDescendants` make; there is no app-level test with a real resolver session whose child calls a remote (no such fixture). That a session stop reaches a nested remote handle through the child run's end sweep or its lineage is checked by reading `resolver.go` and `subagent_remote.go` only.
  - A remote that never acts on the stop keeps the calling session's place until `remote_timeout_ms`; a lower cap for stopped remote runs would need a setting (not proposed).

## profile_message compact on every call (T-010) (Go, 2026-11-12)

- **Problem.** `context_trigger` took the per-(caller run, target) claim for compact as well as reset, so with `action: compact, after: 0` the second message of a caller run to a target never compacted (the claim was held until the run ended), a first message to an empty target spent the claim before the target had content, and a positive `after` compacted at most once per run. The tests, comments and schema described that as the contract; the user's contract is "compact on every call".
- **Decision.** A compact keeps no per-run state: `contextStep` evaluates it at every `BeforeRun`, i.e. at every message that actually starts a run of the target (a queued message when the pump starts it, a sub-agent's message too, an ended-caller-run call too). The transcript-empty rule and the token threshold are unchanged (empty/missing/blank transcript left alone with the Warn; a positive `after` needs strictly more tokens than the last completed response in `messages.jsonl`), so a target that grows past `after` again after a compaction is compacted again. A failed compaction is logged, the message is still sent, and the next message tries again (nothing is held).
- **Reset unchanged (superseded by T-011 below: reset is evaluated on every call too).** Reset keeps the once-per-caller-run-and-target claim (claim before the empty check at `after: 0`, claim only when the threshold is passed at a positive `after`, fail-closed when no running caller run, claim given back on failure, sub-agents share the root run's claim). `callerRuns` is therefore only used by reset now; the only code change is that `claim` is a no-op for compact. Remote targets are untouched: reset refused, compact sent with the note that it was not applied.
- **Active-tail behaviour (assessed, pinned by `TestCompactTriggerWithTheRealCompactionKeepsOnlyTheLastExchange`).** With the target's default compaction (assistant_final, keep 1 turn; the compaction summary this note once mentioned was removed by T-013) a compact before every message at `after: 0` drops the older history at the first message and afterwards leaves the target only its previous exchange plus the new message (the retained turn lives in the compaction cache, so `messages.jsonl` holds just the exchange since). That follows from "compact every call" with that default, not a defect; a target that should remember more raises `after` or its `keep_turns`, or enables the compaction summary. The schema description says so.
- **Concurrency.** The step runs with the target's transcript held and the run registered, so concurrent messages to one target queue on the transcript and their compactions never overlap (`TestCompactTriggerConcurrentCallsAreSerializedPerTarget`); no new lock or state was added.
- **Open: no end-to-end test of a compaction that fails inside the real summarizer.** A failing compaction is covered with a stubbed `compactProfile`; the real `Session.Compact` error paths (summary model failure under its failure rule, `pre_compact` hook blocking) are covered by their own maintenance tests but not through `profile_message`. Closing it needs a fixture whose summary model fails.
- **Open (closed by T-013, which removed `compaction.summary`): a compaction per message costs a summary model call per message when `compaction.summary` is on.** Documented in the schema; there is no rate limit or dedupe beyond `after`. Closing it would need a cooldown setting, which was not asked for.

## profile_message reset on every call (T-011) (Go, 2026-11-12)

- **Decision (user-authorized).** `context_trigger` `reset` is evaluated at every `BeforeRun`, like `compact`: at every message that actually starts a run of the target (a queued message when the pump starts it, a sub-agent's or nested sub-agent's message too). At `after: 0` a target whose `messages.jsonl` has content is reset at each call; a missing/empty/blank transcript is left alone and spends nothing (both actions log the Warn `messages.jsonl is empty - nothing to compact|reset`; reset used to log Debug only, changed on request so the two actions are consistent), so an empty first call no longer suppresses a later one; a positive `after` reads the last completed response's input tokens at every call and resets only when strictly greater, so a target that crosses it again is reset again. The threshold semantics, the strictly-greater rule and the empty-transcript rule are unchanged.
- **Destructive at every qualifying call.** A reset now drops what the messages before it wrote, including earlier messages of the same caller run: with `after: 0` a target answers every call from a clean history, and its previous exchange is gone. The reset also stops the target's running async handles and sub-agents and drops their unread completion signals at every call (`resetResolved`), so a child the previous message started on the target is stopped by the next message. That is what "reset every call" means; the schema description says so and tells users to reserve it for a target that must answer from a clean history. Nothing asks for a limit, so there is none.
- **Infrastructure removed.** `callerRunTargets` (`begin/claim/release/forget`), `Resolver.callerRuns`/`callerRunSeq`, `callerRunKey`, the `boundRunner.Run` begin/forget, `withCallerRun` in the sub-agent launcher and the `callerRun` parameter of `contextStep` had no other user and are deleted. With them go the special cases they needed: a due reset from a call with no running caller run (no id, ended run, background sub-agent outliving its run) is no longer refused with "no running caller run"; it is evaluated like any call. `CallerValues` still carries the cost meter and hook reporter to sub-agents.
- **Failures.** Unchanged and still fail-closed for reset: a transcript that cannot be located or read, a token count that cannot be read, a reset that fails and one published but not confirmed durable end the step with a `*native.ContextTriggerError`; the message is not sent, `context_trigger_failed` is returned. Nothing is held on failure, so the next message tries again (and, once it succeeds, the one after it resets again). A failed compaction is still logged and the message sent.
- **Concurrency and queues.** Unchanged: the step runs with the target's transcript held and the run registered, so concurrent or queued messages to one target are serialized and their resets never overlap, and a queued message resets when the pump starts it, after the messages before it were served. No new lock or state.
- **Remote.** Unchanged: a remote target is never reset or compacted; reset is refused with `context_trigger_unsupported`, compact is sent with the note.
- **Tests.** New `profile_message_reset_every_call_test.go`: three messages of one run reset three times (each request carries only its own message, and `messages.jsonl` holds only the last), empty first then content, positive threshold re-crossing (tokens 50,50,10,3,50 at `after: 10` reset at 0,1,4), failure then retry then reset again, two queued messages each resetting at their turn (served counts 0,1), six concurrent messages with no overlapping reset, a sub-agent and a nested sub-agent each resetting, and a call without caller-run state. The former once-per-run tests were rewritten (`...ResetPositiveThresholdFollowsTheTranscript`, `...ResetFailureFailsTheMessageAndTheNextOneRetries`, `...ResetKeepsQueuedMessages`, the compact/reset parity tests) or deleted with the code they pinned (`TestCallerRunTargetsForgetDropsTheEntry`, `TestWithCallerRunCopiesTheIdAndKeepsTheChildsOwnContext`, the no-caller-run and ended-caller-run refusal tests, the once-per-run sub-agent test). Nine of the new tests failed against the claim code before the change.
- **Open: users with `reset` configured lose the previous exchange at every call.** This is the requested behaviour, but a configuration written for the old once-per-run meaning (a reset to start each run clean, later calls building on one another) now changes silently. There is no migration or warning; closing it would need a new setting (for example an explicit `every_call` flag), which was not asked for.
- **Open: a reset stops the target's children at every call.** A background sub-agent or handle the target started during one message is stopped by the next message's reset, even from the same caller run. Documented, not limited.

## Unified agent runs: completion assessment and accepted departures (T-007) (Go, 2026-11-11)

- **Outcome.** The redesign in `docs/design_unified_agent_runs.md` is **partly implemented, not complete**. Built: R0, R1, R2, R4a/R4b, R5 (one admission check, lineage, `native.RunTree`), R6 depth and U3. The rest is an accepted departure (below), settled as current behaviour (U5, U6), or deferred and not approved (U1, a higher U7 maximum). The design now opens with this status, and each section of §3, §4, §5 and §6 has a status note.
- **Decider's decisions (2026-11-11), checked against the code. The executor agrees with all seven.**
  1. **Two configs stay:** `childConfig` per call for the run, and `native.NewAgentToolConfigs` per owner prepare for the tools. Evidence: `agent_config_fields_test.go` finds four fields read by both sides with different values (`Hooks`, `NativeSubagent`, `StateContext`, `Model`). The run config also takes the call's `model` argument after the tools config is built, and a toolset error is raised at load while a model error is raised at the call. Design §3.1/§3.2 and the R3a `AgentTemplate` proposal are therefore not built.
  2. **The `leaf` catalog stays, beside the call-time depth gate.** The gate (`depthExceeded` / `depthExceeds` on `RunDepth`) is checked before any local, remote or `profile_message` start. The leaf is pinned by `nested_tree_tools.txt` and `TestNestedSubagentThroughTheRealLauncherStopsAtMaxDepth`: no `subagent` tool at the deepest level. So `nestedSelf` and `hookTool` stay too (U8: keep).
  3. **The child runner stays apart from `prepareRun`.** `runEphemeral` has no runner cache, no transcript lock and its own prompt-cache scope (messages path plus agent name). Its catalog comes from the same acquired parts and the same `CatalogSections` order as the owner's (R4a/R4b).
  4. **The child catalog cache key stays (agent, sandbox choice, leaf).** Plan mode is a call-time refusal (`planModeRefusal`), and the caller's environment narrows a tool at dispatch (`callSandbox`), so neither needs a variant. A sandbox choice changes only descriptions. `TestSandboxChoiceCatalogsAreBuiltOnce` and `child_catalogs.txt` pin it.
  5. **`agent.json` stays, with its existing validation** (`paths`, `read_only` and unknown keys refused, as before T-007) and no new refusal. This is U2 as recommended.
  6. **The unified profile/agent loader and U1 are deferred** as a separate behaviour change. `selectAgent` looks names up in `agents` and `agents_dir` only.
  7. **U7 stays:** `max_depth` default 2, maximum 8.
- **Two departures the list does not name, recorded as they are (no disagreement on substance).**
  - **§3.4:** `RunSpec` has `RunTemplate{Base, Agent}` and no `RunTemplateRef`. `StartRun` runs neither config resolution, admission, worktree nor `prepareRun` (steps 1, 2, 4, 5). This follows from decisions 1 to 3. The bridging fields `Tools`, `Execution`, `CallerValues` and `Profile` stay.
  - **§3.5 chain:** only persistent nodes, (session, profile), are recorded (the httpapi registry's chain), and a sub-agent call names its session's profile as the caller. Cycle refusal is unchanged, because ephemeral nodes never close a cycle; `TestRunBaselineMixedChainCycleThroughSubagents` covers it with ephemeral levels in between. U4 went another way than the design's recommendation (R6 follow-up): `max_chain` is an additional cap, not an alias.
- **Changes in this pass.**
  - **One carrier for a local message's remote hops.** `native.WithRemoteHops` / `RemoteHopsOf` (a context value set only by `profileMessageTool.execute`, from `execution.RemoteHops`) are removed. `profileMessenger.Prepare` reads `request.Caller.RemoteHops`, which `ExecutionContext.Caller()` copies from the same field, so the value is the same.
    - New test `TestProfileMessageHandsTheCallersRemoteHopsToTheTargetRun` checks hops 0 and 2 reach the target run's `ProfileRunRequest.Hops`.
    - `mutate-check.sh` CAUGHT the plan taking 0.
    - No earlier app test pinned this value.
  - **Stale comments fixed.**
    - The `tools.CallerContext` doc said no run reads it, and named the caller run id, which T-011 removed.
    - `RunTemplate`, `RunSpec`, `RunSpec.Caller` and `RunSpec.Profile` said "R6 changes" or "until R6".
    - `childConfig` said "R6 replaces it".
  - **Schema text.**
    - "A child is just another profile" / "A sub-agent is just another profile" now says the tools are resolved like a profile's, and the subagent description adds that the run settings are the caller's, with the agent's own model, instructions and run limits. Changed in the `setting.schema.json` subagent and agent `tools` descriptions, and in `agent.schema.json`.
    - The subagent description no longer says children are narrowed "(and read_only)". `read_only` is a removed agent key, refused at load; the text was stale before T-007.
  - **Design doc:** a status header and status notes; the original plan text is kept.
  - **Superseded markers** on the earlier R0, R1, R3, R4, T0 and R3a open items that this decision settles.
- **Open (remaining real gaps).**
  - **Unread carriers.**
    - `SubagentRequest.Caller` and `RunSpec.Caller` are filled but read by nothing; an ephemeral run's scope comes from `Execution`. They are kept because deleting them rewrites the R0 inventory, the R1 propagation tests and the `RunSpec` field walk, with no behaviour change.
    - Still context values: the cost meter and hook reporter (`session` types), `callerMessagesPathKey`, `max_chain` (`WithProfileChainMax`) and the child-call mark (`WithChildCall`). The app tests use the last two as their interface.
    - **Decided (decider, 2026-11-11): kept reserved for U1.** The comments on both fields and on `tools.CallerContext` say they are not read today. If U1 is declined, removing both fields with their R0 inventory, R1 propagation and field-walk tests is a separate **R7 cleanup**; if U1 is approved, `runEphemeral` reads it, which needs the manager's narrowing to move.
  - **Run tree:** memory-only, as already recorded. Stop, reset and delete stay outside it by the Q3 decision.
  - **Design §6 tests not present:**
    - every nesting pair at every depth through a remote hop (only ephemeral→remote ephemeral at app level, and the remote `profile_message` hop at native level);
    - real bwrap at every level of a chain;
    - a manifest recorded before R3/R4 (resume is pinned through the fingerprint goldens only);
    - a remote caller on an older version.
  - **Settled, current behaviour kept (decider, 2026-11-11):** U5 (`subagent_stop` only for ephemeral runs) and U6 (ephemeral runs stay inside the caller's tool call). `run_start`/`run_end` for ephemeral runs and ephemeral runs in the run list/SSE stream are optional extensions, not built; they are not open decisions.
  - **Deferred, not approved:** U1 (a profile as an ephemeral run, with the unified loader) and a higher U7 maximum. Each needs a user decision before any work.
  - **No `messages-golden-diff` baseline build was run in this pass.** The code change touches no transcript or tool definition, and the R0 goldens (`TestRunBaseline*`) run in `verify-go.sh`.
- **Checks.**

## `compaction.summary` removed; `keepbackup.min_turns` replaced by `keepbackup.append_limit` (T-013, Go, 2026-11-11)

User request: remove `compaction.summary` entirely and replace `compaction.keepbackup.min_turns` with `compaction.keepbackup.append_limit`. The OAuth providers and the legacy adapter were explicitly out of scope and were not touched.

- **`append_limit`.** Integer 0..1000 (`maxKeepBackupTurns`), default 0 = no limit. It is parsed in `normalizeCompaction` beside `turns`, with the same error style (`compaction.keepbackup.append_limit must be an integer between 0 and 1000`; null means the default). It goes into `sessionfs.Compaction.AppendLimit`, `session.AutomaticCompactionSettings.AppendLimit` and `transcript.CompactionOptions.AppendLimit`, and from there through all four compaction paths: the run's automatic compaction (`boundRunner`), the overflow compaction (it uses the same options, `automaticCompactionOptions`), manual compaction (`boundMutation.Compact`, which is also what `profile_message` `context_trigger` compact and the profile compaction call) and the sub-agent settings (`compactionFor`, see the caveat below).
- **What it does.** Only with `backup_mode: "append"` and a limit above 0. `backupTranscript` builds the backup as before (existing backup, then the live `messages.jsonl`) and keeps the newest `append_limit` user turns of it, dropping the oldest whole turns. `replace` always overwrites and ignores the limit (the `min_turns` guard `keepsFullerBackup` is gone). `Reset` is unchanged: it still removes the backup.
- **Turn rule.** `scanBackupTurns` (it replaced `countUserTurns`, whose only use was `min_turns`) reads the files as they are on disk and starts a turn at each record whose top-level `role` is `user` and that is not marked `SessionInputSteerField: true`. A steering record continues the turn before it, so it is dropped or kept with that turn and never split from it. Every record of an input batch (shared `SessionInputBatchIDField`) is a turn of its own, as for `CompactHistory`.
- **Where it cuts.** With more turns than the limit, the backup starts at the record that starts the oldest turn kept: everything before it goes, including records in front of the first turn and steering records that preceded the cut. With no more turns than the limit nothing is cut, and records in front of the first turn stay as they are. A backup with no turn at all (zero turns) is appended unchanged. One batch with more turns than the limit keeps only its newest turns.
- **Memory and durability.** The scan keeps a ring of `append_limit` offsets (at most 1000 entries) and one line at a time, so memory does not grow with the backup. The cut is applied while the result is written to the same temporary file in the backup's directory, fsynced unless the journal durability is `process`, and renamed over the backup, with the directory sync after it: the same atomic and durable write as before. What was scanned is what is copied, bounded by the scanned size, so a file that grows meanwhile cannot shift the cut. The cost is one extra read of the existing backup and of the transcript per compaction when the limit is above 0; with limit 0 nothing is read twice and the bytes are exactly the old ones.
- **Malformed backup (limit above 0 only).** A line that is not a JSON object (checked strictly, as `json.Valid` does, so trailing text also counts) in the existing backup or in the transcript stops the backup, and with it the compaction, before anything is written. The error names the file and the byte offset (`backup transcript before compaction: <path>: record at byte N is not a JSON object`). The backup, the transcript and the compaction cache are left as they were. A manual compaction answers HTTP 500 (the server log has the text), a run's automatic compaction fails the run. The way out is to repair or delete the backup file, or set `append_limit` to 0, which carries a corrupt line along as before (it never parses). Blank lines are not records. A missing source file still leaves the backup alone.
- **Unterminated last line (no separator), validated and counted on the combined bytes.** The new content is built exactly as before: the existing backup, then the live `messages.jsonl`, with no newline added between them. If the existing backup's last line has no newline, that line is joined to the first line of the transcript, as it always was. With limit 0 this is carried on unchecked (the bytes are as before). With limit above 0 the check and the turn count run on the lines of those combined bytes, before any cut: the joined line (the unterminated last line plus the first line of the transcript) is one record, and it must be a JSON object, as every other record must. If it is not (for example two records glued into `{...}{...}`), the backup stops with `<backup>: record at byte N has no newline, so it is joined to the first line of <transcript>, which is not a JSON object`, before anything is written, and the backup, the transcript and the cache are left as they were. This holds even when the cut would drop the glued line (an earlier version of this change checked only a glued line the cut kept, and before that inserted a newline; both deviated from the specification and are removed). The glued line is read once: a blank part is fine (`"  "` plus a user record is one user record, one turn; a user record plus a blank first line is the same record), the turn starts at the start of the backup's last line, so a cut at that turn keeps the blank with the record, and the transcript's first line is not counted a second time. A transcript that is empty or missing joins nothing, and the unterminated last line is then read on its own. Same recovery as for a corrupt backup: repair or delete the backup file, or set `append_limit` to 0.
- **Turn counts differ between the limit and the web UI.** `keepbackup.turns` (display) is read by `readBackupTail`, which merges the records of one input batch into one turn and does not read the steering marker. `append_limit` counts every non-steering user record. So a backup trimmed to N turns can show fewer than N turns in the UI when it holds batches, and the two settings are independent: `turns` hides turns in the UI, `append_limit` deletes them from the file. `readBackupTail` and the record format are unchanged.
- **Sub-agent caveat.** The sub-agent turn store has no `MessagesBackupPath` (`app/subagent.go`), so a sub-agent compaction writes no backup and `append_limit` has nothing to act on there. `compactionFor` still carries the value, as it carries `backup_mode`, so the settings agree. No child backup was added.
- **`compaction.summary` removed.** The setting, its normalizer and defaults (`sessionfs/compaction_summary_settings.go`; the overflow settings moved to `compaction_overflow_settings.go` unchanged), the summary request and rendering (`session/compaction_summary.go`: `NewCompactionSummarizer`, `summarizeItems`, `summaryRequest`, `RenderItemsForSummary`, `CompactionSummarySettings`), `AutomaticCompactionSettings.Summary` and `OnSummaryError`, the manual summarizer (`manualCompactionSummarizer`, `failingStreamer`, `compactionSummarySettings`, `compactionSummaryLogger`), `transcript.CompactionOptions.Summarize` with its unlocked window, the dropped-turns digest guard and `ErrCompactionSkipped`, the schema object and the tests of all of these. `CompactHistory` now plans and rewrites under one hold of the store lock, with no window in which the lock is released for a model call. Kept, moved out of the summary files because other code uses them: `runnerModelSettings` and `overflowSettings` (`app/compaction_settings.go`), `promptMessageItem` and `responseOutputText` (MCP sampling, `session/complete_text.go`), `planCompaction` and `compactionPlan` (`transcript/compaction_plan.go`), and the test helpers `finalAnswerRound` and `itoa`. The manual compaction still loads the model (`WithModel`) as a validation, so an unusable `model.json` is still a 422 before the transcript is touched (`TestMaintenanceOnlyCompactNeedsAUsableModelFile`), the `pre_compact` hook still fires first and a blocking one is still a 409.
- **Old keys.** `compaction.summary` and `compaction.keepbackup.min_turns` in an existing `setting.json` are ignored, not refused and not applied: the loader never rejected unknown keys in `compaction` or `keepbackup`, and the schema has `additionalProperties: true` on both, so editors do not flag them either. No migration and no warning. Two consequences: a session that had the summary on now drops the turns without a summary; and a `replace` backup that `min_turns` used to protect is now overwritten.
- **Data already written.** A summary that an earlier version stored in a compaction cache stays in the history as an ordinary developer message (its header text is only text now). Nothing produces a new one, and nothing recognises or rolls an old one forward.
- **Superseded records.** The `min_turns` (2026-10-16) and `compaction.summary` (2026-11-05) entries, the R4 note on `countUserTurns`, and two T-010 notes about the summary are marked superseded in place. `docs/compaction-summary-redesign.md` and `docs/design_compaction_summary_chain.md` carry a banner saying the feature was removed; their text is kept as the record of a design that was not pursued. The audit files `audit_findings/q_compaction_backup.md` and `audit_findings/p8_r3.md` still mention `min_turns` as findings of their day and were not edited.
- **Tests.**
  - transcript (`backup_append_limit_test.go`): a table of 19 cases for each of two durability modes (limit 0; fits; no backup yet; cut in the existing backup; cut at the first turn of the transcript; limit 1; one batch over the limit; steering kept with its turn and not orphaned at the boundary; leading records dropped when cut and kept when they fit, also when the turns exactly fill the limit; zero turns; unterminated last line: joined blank line kept, limit 0 joined as before, empty transcript, a blank last line joined to a user record counted once and cut at its start, a user record joined to a blank first line; blank lines and CRLF; replace ignores the limit); the 2,4,...,12 batch rolling with limit 10; input batches; limit 0 byte-for-byte with corrupt data; eight kinds of corrupt record refused with file and offset (including an unterminated last record glued to the transcript's first line, kept whole, cut away inside the existing backup, or cut away with the whole backup), the files unchanged and no temporary file left; missing files; the turn rule and the steering marker; the bounded window over 5000 turns; `CompactHistory` rolling, unlimited, replace and the corrupt-backup abort leaving transcript and cache untouched; `Reset` removing the backup.
  - sessionfs: null, 0, 7, 1000 accepted; -1, 1001, 1.5, "3", true, [] and 1e400 refused with the message; `turns` and `append_limit` independent; removed keys ignored with no change to the settings; the schema has `append_limit` with the loader's default and bounds and has neither `summary` nor `min_turns`; the overflow settings tests kept without the summary arms.
  - session: the automatic and the overflow compaction roll the backup by the limit (limits 0, 1, 2, 3), and a corrupt backup fails the run with the file and byte and leaves the history.
  - app: manual compaction over HTTP rolls the append backup (default, 0, 3, 1) and replace ignores it; a corrupt backup is a 500 with the path and byte in the log and nothing changed; a setting.json with the removed keys loads, sends no provider request and overwrites a replace backup; the run's automatic compaction rolls the backup; `compactionFor` carries the value. The MCP sampling, overflow, invalid-model 422 and `pre_compact` tests are unchanged and pass.
  - Mutation checks: 13 mutations (the cut index, the exact-fit comparison, the steering exclusion, the mode check, the separator, the corrupt-record error, the cut inside the transcript, and the places the limit is passed on: `CompactHistory`, `automaticCompactionOptions`, manual compaction, `boundRunner`, `compactionFor` and the loader) were each caught by a failing test, not a build error.
- **Open.**
  - A corrupt backup keeps failing every compaction of a session with `append_limit` above 0 until it is repaired or the limit is set to 0; there is no repair or skip option, by decision (fail closed).
  - No test runs the real `jad` binary against a provider; the app tests use the HTTP service with a fake provider.
  - Sub-agents keep no backup, so the limit does nothing for them (see above); adding a child backup was not asked for.
  - One very long line is read into memory whole. The backup scan (`scanBackupTurns`) reads each line with `bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\n')`, which has no line-size cap, and the unterminated last line of the backup is also held while it waits to be joined to the transcript's first line. So the memory is bounded in the number of turns (the ring of at most 1000 offsets) but not in the size of a single record: a backup or transcript with one huge line (or no newline at all) needs memory for that line, and `json.Valid` checks it whole. This is the same as the existing transcript and backup readers, which also read whole lines; no cap was added because none was specified. Closing it would need a maximum record size (a setting with a default) and a decision on what happens to a longer line (fail closed like a corrupt record, most likely); with `append_limit` 0 nothing is read, so the limit does not apply there.
  - The audit files named above still describe `min_turns`.
  - Unrelated and deferred by the user: OAuth providers and the legacy adapter.

## Standalone `anthropic-adapter` command removed (T-014) (Go, 2026-11-12)

- **Decision.** `cmd/anthropic-adapter` (the TCP listener that served `POST /v1/responses` on top of the Anthropic Messages API) is deleted, with its tests. A model with `"api": "anthropic_messages"` already runs the same `internal/anthropicadapter` handler in process (`app.providerTranslator`, `sessionfs` model validation); that path is unchanged.
- **Breaking change.** A model file whose `base_url` points at a running standalone adapter (for example `http://127.0.0.1:8788/v1` with the default `responses` api) no longer has anything to talk to. Change it to `"api": "anthropic_messages"`, with `base_url` the Anthropic API root or left out. A standalone config file becomes the model file's `anthropic` object without `listen`, `caller_token_env` and `upstream.base_url`. No user data was touched: a built binary or a config file on disk is left alone.
- **No other caller found.** `git grep` over scripts, frontend, CI and sample files found no use of the command or of port 8788 outside the command, its README and the adapter schema; `go.mod` loses nothing, since the command imported only the standard library and the package.
- **Listener-only code removed.** `Config.Listen`, `Config.CallerTokenEnv`, the caller-token hash and its check (`resolveCallerToken`, `HasCallerToken`, `callerAllowed`), `DefaultListen`, `DefaultCallerTokenEnv`, `MinCallerTokenLength`, the `listen must be non-empty` check, the production `LoadConfig`, and the command's fail-closed non-loopback guard, exposure warning and upstream-URL redaction for its startup log. The caller-token tests went with them. The `Origin` refusal while a `credential_file` is set stays: it is in `Handler.ServeHTTP`, shared, and now has its own test without a caller token (`TestBrowserOriginIsRefusedWhenTheAdapterHoldsACredential`) plus the case without a credential file.
- **Kept on purpose.** `ParseEmbeddedConfig` still refuses `listen` and `caller_token_env` by name (`embeddedRefusedKeys`, "is not used: jad runs the adapter in process, with no listener") and `upstream.base_url`; a test now pins the message. In `model.schema.json` the `anthropic` object keeps its explicit `not required listen / caller_token_env / upstream.base_url` rule. `sample/schemes/anthropic-adapter.schema.json` no longer lists `listen` and `caller_token_env`, so they are also unknown keys there; the schema still validates the `anthropic` object, and its wording no longer names the command.
- **Fixtures.** `sample/anthropic-adapter.json` and `sample/anthropic-adapter-api.json` are used by package tests only, so they moved to `internal/anthropicadapter/testdata/adapter.json` and `adapter-api.json`, minus their `listen` line. `LoadConfig` is now a test helper in `config_test.go` (read file, decode, `finish`), so the roughly 40 tests that load a fixture config are unchanged. The fixtures keep `upstream.base_url`, which a model file refuses; they are fixtures of the translation rules, not valid model-file objects.
- **Docs.** The command README moved to `internal/anthropicadapter/README.md` with its translation, limits, configuration, caching and credential/billing findings (the 2026-10-08 probes); only the run instructions, the `listen` and `caller_token_env` rows and the `--config` text were removed, and a removal note with migration was added. `backend-go/README.md`, `cmd/claude-auth/README.md` and the schema text point to the package. Historical audit documents (`audit_findings/`, `audit_plan.md`) still name `cmd/anthropic-adapter`; they are records and were not edited.
- **Open.**
  - The untracked, git-ignored `sample/anthropic-adapter-oauth.json` on a developer machine was validated by the old `sample/anthropic-adapter*.json` glob; the glob now covers `testdata/adapter*.json` only, so that local file is no longer checked, and it still carries a `listen` key. It was not deleted or edited.
  - `LoadConfig` exists only in tests, and fixtures are not embedded-valid; moving them into model-file shape (and testing them through `ParseEmbeddedConfig`) would remove that split, at the cost of rewriting the fixture-based tests.
  - A user who ran the command shared between machines has no replacement in this repository; the only route is the in-process adapter.
  - OAuth providers (`claude-auth`, `openai-auth`, `credential_file`) are untouched here; their removal is a separate task. *Done by T-015 (below).*

## OpenAI and Claude subscription sign-in removed (T-015) (Go, 2026-11-12)

- **Decision.** The two unsupported subscription providers are removed: ChatGPT (`auth_mode: "openai_oauth"`) and Claude (`anthropic.upstream.credential_file`). API-key OpenAI and Anthropic models, the in-process Anthropic and Chat Completions translators, MCP server OAuth (`jad mcp login`, `internal/tools/mcp/oauth.go`, tokens under `<state>/.mcp-oauth`), the sandbox hide of `{home}/.jad/auth` and every credential file on disk are unchanged.
- **Deleted code.** `cmd/openai-auth`, `cmd/claude-auth`, `internal/openaiauth`, `internal/claudeauth`, `internal/openaioauth` (the credential reader and request transport), `internal/browser` (its only importers were the two commands; checked with an import search), `app/oauth_client.go` (OAuth source, pre-run credential check, OAuth transport, the cross-origin redirect refusal installed only for OAuth), the `openai_oauth` setting (`sessionfs/openai_oauth_settings.go`, `SessionConfig.OpenAIOAuth`), `Model.AuthMode` and `Model.OAuthAuthFile`, `defaultOAuthAuthFile`/`oauthAuthFilePath`, the Codex endpoint default, the `AuthMode`, `OAuthAuthFile` and `OpenAIOAuth` fields of the runner identity, `anthropicHoldsCredential` and the credential-file placeholder key (an Anthropic model always needs its `api_key_env` value now), `anthropicadapter/credential.go` (credential-file reader, `ExpandCredentialPath`), `Config.HoldsCredential`, `UpstreamConfig.CredentialFile`/`ExpiryMarginMS`, `DefaultCredentialFile`/`DefaultExpiryMarginMS`, `claude-auth.schema.json`, `openai-auth.schema.json`, `sample/openai-auth.json`, `sample/claude-auth.json`, and the tests of all of these. `go.mod` loses nothing.
- **No silent fallback: removed keys are refused by name.** Each message says the key is no longer supported and to use an API key:
  - `model.json` `oauth_auth_file` (any value, any `auth_mode`): `oauth_auth_file was removed: signing in with a ChatGPT subscription is no longer supported; use an OpenAI API key ...`.
  - `model.json` `auth_mode` other than `api_key` (including `openai_oauth`, a non-string, any other word): `auth_mode must be api_key (openai_oauth was removed): ...`. **Choice:** `auth_mode: "api_key"` (and null, as for every field) stays accepted as a no-op and the schema keeps a one-value enum, because it was the documented default that existing model files may spell out and it selects exactly what every model now does; refusing it would break working files for no safety gain. If a later task wants the key gone entirely, the change is one condition in `rejectRemovedOAuthFields`.
  - the `openai_oauth` setting, in a session's or profile's `settings` and in the root `defaults`: `settings.openai_oauth was removed: ...` (checked in `checkLayoutSettings` before the unknown-key error, so it is not reported as "may not carry"). The key stays out of `layoutSettingKeys` and of the `setting.schema.json` key list and properties (the existing test keeps the two in step).
  - `anthropic.upstream.credential_file` and `anthropic.upstream.expiry_margin_ms` (inert without it): `upstream.credential_file was removed: signing in with a Claude subscription is no longer supported; use an Anthropic API key ...`, from `ParseEmbeddedConfig`, so it fails at model load, `jad check` and the catalog PUT (422) as well as at run time.
  - **Where the user sees it.** Model load errors reach `jad check`, the catalog model PUT (422 with the message) and the server log. A run that hits one fails with the generic "run failed" line on the SSE stream, as every configuration error does (`clientRunErrorMessage` withholds details); the log has the text. A test pins that the provider receives no request.
- **Kept on purpose.** `upstream.system_prefix` is applied to every request regardless of credentials (`request.go`), so it stays unchanged in behaviour; only the schema, README and test wording that tied it to the subscription token were reworded (the test sentence is now neutral). Its README findings from 2026-10-08 stay as the reason it is discouraged. The adapter's `Origin` refusal was conditioned on `HoldsCredential` only, so with no credential held it had no caller and was deleted (the accepted-Origin test stays). `{home}/.jad/auth` stays in the default sandbox `hide_paths` (comment and `docs/isolation-decisions.md` D5 reworded): a leftover credential file must stay unreadable to children.
- **Samples.** `sample/jad/models/openai/gpt-fast.json` and `gpt-deep.json` were the only tracked samples with `openai_oauth`; they are API-key models now (`provider: openai`, `api_key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY`, same request). The layout tests copy them, so they are exercised. The ignored local `sample/anthropic-adapter-oauth.json` was not touched and its `.gitignore` rule stays; the rules for the two command binaries were dropped (neither file exists).
- **Docs.** `backend-go/README.md` loses both sign-in sections and gets a short removal note; `anthropicadapter/README.md` replaces the credential-file section with a removal note, keeps the probe findings and drops the two table rows; the schemas (`model`, `setting`, `anthropic-adapter`) are updated. Older records in this file about the removed paths are marked superseded in place, not deleted; `audit_findings/` and `audit_plan.md` stay historical.
- **No migration, no deletion.** Nothing reads, moves or deletes `~/.jad/auth/*.json`, `claude-oauth.json` or any other credential file. A user keeps them or removes them by hand.
- **Breaking change.** A model file or setting that used any removed key fails to load until the key is deleted and `api_key_env` is set. A subscription-only user has no replacement in this repository.
- **Open.**
  - The jad sandbox default still hides `{home}/.jad/auth`; nothing writes there any more. Dropping the entry would be a separate security decision (a leftover file would become readable).
  - `provider: openai-codex` in an older model file is still just a label and is accepted.
  - The generic run-failure line does not show the removed-key message to an SSE client (see above); changing that would change how every configuration error is reported.
  - `go mod tidy` was not run (it needs the network here); `go.mod` imports were checked by hand and nothing became unused.
  - `audit_findings/*` and the local ignored `sample/anthropic-adapter-oauth.json` still mention `credential_file`/`claude-auth`; left as history.

## Usage totals survive compaction: the usage baseline (T-016, Go, 2026-11-12)

User report: after a manual compaction the usage totals in the frontend sometimes disappear or reset, and again after the next message. The tracer's hypotheses (stale scan checkpoints, a retry that reuses a stale cache, the cache deleted during compaction, a silently skipped cache write) were checked with deterministic tests; the frontend turned out to be a mirror of what the backend sends.
